✅ अल्लाह पर भरोसा और पूर्ण विश्वास (तवक्कुल) विकसित करना।
✅ सब्र और शुक्र की आदत पैदा करना।
✅ ज़िक्र-ए-इलाही को बेहतर बनाना।

title: #muftimenkreminders#AllahsLove Do This One Thing.. And Allah Will Be Pleased With You | Mufti Menk
description:
Are you searching for one powerful action that will bring you closer to Allah and earn His love? Are you tired of feeling distant, unsure if your efforts are even enough? This reminder is exactly what your heart has been waiting for. 🕊️ Mufti Menk shares the one thing that can change everything — your relationship with Allah, your peace of mind, your purpose.

✨ Sometimes we overcomplicate things, thinking we need to be perfect. But Islam is not about perfection — it’s about sincerity. And there is one act that, if done with the right heart, will make Allah pleased with you.

This one thing is simple… but it requires intention.
It’s not about impressing people — it’s about pleasing your Lord.
It’s not about being seen — it’s about being sincere.
And the reward? It’s Jannah.

🌟 This video is your spiritual reset. A chance to stop striving for the approval of the world, and start seeking the pleasure of the One who created it. Because when Allah loves you — nothing else matters.

👇🏽 Here are 🔟 life-changing reminders from this video that will transform your Iman:

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
➊✨ Allah’s Pleasure Is the Greatest Success
Stop chasing validation from people. Start chasing the pleasure of the Most Merciful.
➋✨ Sincerity Beats Perfection
Allah doesn’t expect you to be perfect. He wants you to be real. Be honest in your repentance and effort.

➌✨ Every Small Deed Counts
That quiet prayer. That hidden charity. That private repentance. Allah sees it all.

➍✨ Do One Thing Consistently — And Do It Well
Even if it’s just one sincere act done regularly, it can outweigh mountains of deeds.

➎✨ Seek Allah’s Love Over People’s Likes
Social media can’t reward your efforts. Allah can.

➏✨ You Don’t Need to Do Everything — Just Do Something
Start with one prayer. One habit. One change. Allah loves the effort.

➐✨ Allah Knows Your Struggles
He sees the pain you hide. Keep going — He is watching, and He is proud of your effort.

➑✨ Don’t Underestimate a Single Tear
A single tear shed out of fear or love for Allah can erase a lifetime of sin.

➒✨ Let Your Heart Return to Allah, Even if It’s Broken
Sometimes the most shattered hearts make the most sincere du’a.

➓✨ The Path to Allah Begins with One Step
Take that step today. You don’t need to be ready — just be willing.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💬 “Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves.” — [Qur’an 2:222]
Let this verse remind you that Allah’s love is within reach. Just turn to Him.

✨ Don’t wait to be perfect. Be sincere. Be consistent. And Allah will be pleased with you — in this world and the next. 🕋

🔁 Watch. Reflect. Transform.
This one thing could change your entire akhirah.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

This video is for educational and spiritual reflection purposes. All teachings are rooted in authentic Islamic principles and shared to uplift and inspire viewers on their personal journey toward closeness to Allah. May Allah accept it from us. Ameen.

title: Qarun and the Disease of Constant Comparison
description:
Qarun represents more than wealth. His story also points us toward a mindset obsessed with comparison.

A person affected by this mindset cannot simply appreciate what they have. They constantly need to know: Who is my equal? Who is ahead of me? Who is getting more attention, love or success?

You can even see this in the story of Yusuf (AS), where his brothers became consumed with comparing how much their father loved him versus how much he loved them.

Comparison can quietly turn another person’s blessing into a threat.

Taken from our YouTube video: "Hidden Qualities That Destroy Your Good Deeds | The Story of Qarun"

title: Allah defeated them using their own hearts | Deeper Look: Surah Al-Hashr | Nouman Ali Khan
description:
Ma zanantum an yakhruju wa zannu annahum mani'atuhum husunuhum minallahi fa atahumullahu min haythu lam yahtasibu wa qadhafa fi qulubihimur ru'b; yukhribuna buyutahum bi aydihim wa aydil mu'minin (59:2):
مَا ظَنَنتُمْ أَن يَخْرُجُوا ۖ وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُم مَّانِعَتُهُمْ حُصُونُهُم مِّنَ اللَّهِ فَأَتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا ۖ وَقَذَفَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الرُّعْبَ ۚ يُخْرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُم بِأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَيْدِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ

Banu Nadir, a tribe in Madinah that broke its treaty with the Prophet ﷺ and plotted against his life, believed their fortresses would protect them even from Allah. Ustadh Nouman Ali Khan shows how the ayah puts that protection first, as though something always had to stand between them and Allah: alliances, then status, then stone walls. There are only two realities: in the seen one, every protection eventually falls; in the unseen one, the only protection is Allah. Fir'awn made the same mistake when he dared Musa (AS) to call on Allah. 

Allah came at the tribe from the one place no wall covers, hurling fear into their hearts like an arrow. He asks you to imagine the safest people in the region unable to sleep. From the cricket pitch to the battlefield, winning and losing are decided in the heart first. Fear did what no enemy could: the tribe tore down its own homes with its own hands.

title: Fear Goes Where No Army Can
description:
Allah hurls fear into the hearts of Banu Nadir, a tribe in Madinah that broke its treaty with the Prophet ﷺ and plotted against his life: "wa qadhafa fi qulubihimur ru'b," وَقَذَفَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الرُّعْبَ‎ (59:2). 

Ustadh Nouman Ali Khan pictures it as an arrow that passes every wall and lodges in the heart. The word "ru'b" describes a heart swollen with fear the way an injury swells. He asks you to imagine Banu Nadir behind the safest walls in the region, sleepless.

title: Why We Treat Islam Like Childhood Education
description:
In many Muslim families, Islamic learning is treated like something children do for a few years before *“real education”* begins.

Then exams, careers and academic success take priority, while deeper Islamic learning quietly disappears.

The problem is not education itself. The problem is teaching young Muslims that Islam is something basic they complete early, while everything serious comes later.

That mindset can have long-term consequences.

Taken from our YouTube video: "How Motherhood Brought Her Back to Islam"

title: Our Limits Point Back to Allah
description:
The opening of Surah Al-Hashr declares Allah's perfection (59:1); Ustadh Nouman Ali Khan turns it on a phrase we use all the time: "get closer to Allah." 

You get closer to a city by traveling toward it, which assumes it is far. The Quran says the opposite: "nahnu aqrabu ilayhi min hablil warid," نَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ‎ (50:16), We are nearer to him than his jugular vein. 

Allah is already near, even to people conspiring in secret (58:7). The closeness is always there; remembering Him makes it apparent. 

Watch the full episode on Bayyinah TV: https://byna.tv/392

title: Tawbah: A Gift From Allah | Khutbah by Nouman Ali Khan
description:
Why are human beings on Earth in the first place? Is this world a punishment for the mistake of Adam and Eve? Are we born fundamentally broken, carrying a sin we cannot escape without someone else paying the price for us?

In this khutbah, Ustadh Nouman Ali Khan explores the striking differences between the Biblical and Quranic accounts of the creation of Adam (AS) and humanity’s life on Earth. In Surah Al-Baqarah, before Adam (AS) is even created, Allah announces to the angels:

إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً

“Indeed, I am going to place a khalifah on the Earth.” [2:30]

Humanity was therefore not accidentally exiled to Earth as a consequence of Adam (AS)’s mistake. Earth was part of Allah’s plan from the beginning, and the human being was created with both responsibility and the freedom to choose.

The Quran also presents a radically different picture of human nature. Allah knows our capacity for corruption, but He also knows a goodness and potential within the human being that even the angels did not initially understand. And when Adam (AS) and his wife made their mistake, the answer was not inherited guilt or permanent condemnation. Adam (AS) turned back to Allah, Allah accepted his tawbah, and when humanity was sent to Earth, Allah promised:

فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ

“Whenever guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will have no fear, nor will they grieve.” [2:38]

This world, then, is not a prison created to punish us for someone else’s mistake. Allah describes the Earth as a place prepared for us, with the sky, rain, fruits, mountains, animals, and countless blessings to appreciate. The Akhirah is better and everlasting, but that does not mean this world is inherently evil.

And with that freedom comes responsibility. Allah closes Surah Al-Baqarah by reminding us:

لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا

“Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.” [2:286]

In the context of the surah, this is also about the responsibilities Allah places upon us. We have been given choice, guidance, the ability to repent when we fail, and responsibilities that Allah knows we are capable of carrying.

This khutbah challenges some deeply rooted assumptions about original sin, human nature, repentance, responsibility, and what the Quran actually teaches us about why we are here.

title: Allah Is Already Near You
description:
The opening of Surah Al-Hashr declares Allah's perfection (59:1); Ustadh Nouman Ali Khan turns it on a phrase we use all the time: "get closer to Allah." You get closer to a city by traveling toward it, which assumes it is far. 

The Quran says the opposite: "nahnu aqrabu ilayhi min hablil warid," نَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ‎ (50:16), We are nearer to him than his jugular vein. Allah is already near, even to people conspiring in secret (58:7). The closeness is always there; remembering Him makes it apparent.

Watch the full episode on Bayyinah TV: https://byna.tv/392

title: Your Tasbih Is Connected to the Whole Universe | Deeper Look: Surah Al-Hashr | Nouman Ali Khan
description:
Sabbaha lillahi ma fis samawati wa ma fil ardi wa huwal 'azizul hakim (59:1):
سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
Before a single ruling is given, the opening of Surah Al-Hashr sets the listener's mind. Ustadh Nouman Ali Khan explains how: the heavens are already in perfect submission; the chaos belongs to the earth, yet even that chaos is part of Allah's plan. 

He shows why the word “ma” appears twice in this ayah, why a surah about crisis opens with tasbih and what it means that the universe has been declaring Allah's perfection for billions of years before any of us joined in. 

Then the question every believer faces when life feels disordered: how can Allah's perfect plan include all of this? He answers it through Musa (AS), who asked for Harun (AS) so that together they could declare Allah's perfection.

 He closes with a challenge to the way we speak about getting closer to Allah, who is already near.

title: The Idols We Carry in Our Minds
description:
When Ibrahim (AS) asked his people about their tamathil (statues), he was not only asking about physical statues. He was questioning the representations they had attached meaning to.

A statue may look like stone, but in someone’s mind it represents power, success, safety, or control.

That question is not only for the people of Ibrahim (AS). It is for us too. What representations have we built in our minds? What ideas are we devoted to without even realizing it? 
Taken from our YouTube video: "The Idols of Our Time (Prophet Ibrahim’s Legacy)"

title: A Masjid That Raised Generations | Muslims in the Caribbean | Remarkable Stories | Nouman Ali Khan
description:
In recent years, Ustadh Nouman Ali Khan visited a wonderful Muslim community in the Caribbean - specifically in Trinidad and Tobago.

After interviewing the leadership team and some standout, inspiring members of the community, what stuck with Ustadh Nouman was how the masjid he visited felt more like a village.

A masjid should not be a place children are dragged to. It should become the place they drag their parents to.

At San Fernando Jamia Masjid in Trinidad and Tobago, that idea has been built into the life of the community. Children are given room to feel at home, young people are trusted with responsibility, women are given real space to contribute and families experience the masjid as part of their everyday life rather than somewhere they only visit for salah.

That is what makes a community last.

The children running around today may become the people leading the masjid tomorrow. The sisters helping organize programs may be the reason entire families remain connected. A small Quran circle can turn one person’s learning into something an entire group grows from. Even something as simple as making space for children to play can change whether they associate the masjid with warmth or with being constantly told to sit down and stay quiet.

There is a simple principle underneath all of it: if we do not invest in our youth, someone else will.

A masjid is not only meant to preserve a building. It is meant to raise people who feel responsible for what happens inside it long after the previous generation is gone.

That is how a community becomes an inheritance.

title: How To Make Kids Love The Masjid
description:
A masjid should be a place children want to come to, not a place where they spend every visit being told to sit still and stay quiet.

What if children had a space where they could run around, play tag, set up ping pong tables and enjoy themselves without constantly being reprimanded? The rule is simple: play as much as you want, as long as you do not hurt one another. But when the adhan begins, the atmosphere changes. This is Allah’s house, and it is time to stand for salah.

The real goal is not simply to make a masjid more entertaining. It is to help children develop a sense of ownership. When children understand both their freedom and their responsibility, they begin reminding one another of the boundaries instead of waiting for adults to enforce every rule.

If we want the next generation to care about our masjids, we have to give them a reason to feel that they belong there. The goal is not just to bring children into the masjid today. It is to raise the people who will cherish it, protect it and take responsibility for it tomorrow.

title: The Quran Gives You Something Deeper Than Happiness
description:
When a person has no clear purpose, even a small disappointment can begin to feel overwhelming. Allah created us with guidance, and the Quran gives our lives direction beyond temporary emotions and circumstances.

The Quran does not teach us to spend our lives chasing happiness. It gives us purpose. And when we live with that purpose, joy becomes a result rather than the goal itself.

Allah knows our emotions, weaknesses and strengths because He created us. The One who understands us completely is also the One who gave us the Quran.

Taken from our series: "Surah Ar-Rahman: A Deeper Look"

title: The Answer She Didn’t Expect
description:
During therapy after giving birth, she was asked to imagine that money, family expectations and circumstances were no longer obstacles.

Then came a simple question: where do you want to be spiritually?

Her answer surprised even her.

“I want to wear hijab.”

It was not something she had planned to say. It was not the answer she expected from herself. But sometimes, when all the noise is stripped away, something deeper finally comes to the surface.

 Taken from our YouTube video: "How Motherhood Brought Her Back to Islam"

title: Kali Mirch Aur Machis Ki Dibbi Ka Powerful Amal | Nazar Utarne Ka Tariqa
description:

Aksar log mehsoos karte hain ke sab kuch theek chal raha hota hai lekin achanak business ruk jata hai، ghar mein larai jhagra shuru ho jata hai، aur paisa aate aate ruk jata hai۔ Yeh video un tamam logon ke liye hai jo is halat se guzar rahe hain.

Is amal ki bunyaad Hadith-e-Nabawi ﷺ par hai jahan Umm-ul-Momineen Hazrat Ayesha RaziAllahu Anha bayan karti hain ke Nabi Kareem ﷺ ne farmaya: “Al-ainu haq” — yani nazar-e-bad haq hai. Amal se pehle wuzu karna, pak jagah par baithna aur tawajjo ke sath Allah ka zikr karna is amal ka aham hissa hai.

Is amal mein Darood Ibrahim, Surah Falaq, Surah Naas aur Ya Razzaq ka wazifa shamil hai. Khas taur par 100 martaba Ya Razzaq parhne ka zikr hai jismein banda Allah ke la-mehdood khazanay ka tasawwur karta hai. Yeh tasawwur aur yaqeen hi is amal ki asal quwwat hai.

Video mein yeh bhi bataya gaya hai ke amal ke dauran jemaai, aansu ya jism par bojh mehsoos hona aam baat hai jo is baat ki nishani hoti hai ke roohani asar kaam kar raha hai. Amal ke baad dibbi ko ghar ki kisi mehfooz aur unchi jagah par rakhne ka mashwara diya gaya hai jahan aam nazar na pade.

Yeh video sirf amal nahi sikhata balkay Allah se ta’alluq, yaqeen aur tawakkul ka dars bhi deta hai. Saath hi yeh naseehat bhi ki gayi hai ke jab Allah fazl farmaye to us ka shukar ada kiya jaye aur Allah ki raah mein sadqa zaroor diya jaye.

Agar aap nazar-e-bad ka ilaj, rizq mein barkat, aur ghar ki be-sukooni ka Qurani hal dhoond rahe hain, to yeh video aap ke liye bohat mufeed hai.

Teesri do rakat is niyyat se parhi jati hain ke banda Allah ke siwa kisi ka mohtaaj na ho aur ghurbat se mehfooz rahe. Har do rakat ke baad Surah Yaseen ya 21 martaba Surah Ikhlas parhne ka amal bataya gaya hai.

Shab-e-Barat un chand raaton mein se hai jin mein dua radd nahi hoti. Is liye is raat ko sone ke bajaye jaagna chahiye, Quran parhna chahiye, Allah ka zikr karna chahiye aur dil se maghfirat ki dua mangni chahiye.

title: Qaum-e-Aad Par Allah Ka Sakht Azaab | The Screaming Wind Punishment
description:
Is video mein aap Qaum-e-Aad par aane wale us khaufnaak azaab ka zikr sunenge jo Qurani tareekh ka aik bohat hi dehla dene wala waqia hai. Yeh kahani sirf ek qissa nahi, balkay takabbur, ghamand aur Allah ke Rasool ko jhutlane ka anjaam hai. Jab Qaum-e-Aad ne apne Nabi Hazrat Hood Alaihissalam ko khula challenge diya aur kaha ke agar aap sachay hain to hum par azaab le aaiye, to phir Allah ka qehar un par toot para.

Sab se pehle Allah ne un par rehmat ke darwazay band kar diye. Aasman se barish ruk gayi, zameen sukhi ho gayi aur woh pani ki aik aik boond ko tarasne lage. Phir jab unhon ne apni wadiyon ki taraf aik bada sa badal aata dekha to samjhe ke yeh rehmat ka paighaam hai. Lekin Hazrat Hood Alaihissalam ne wazeh farma diya ke yeh rehmat nahi balkay woh azaab hai jis ki tum jaldi macha rahe thay.

Phir jo manzar qaim hua, woh soch ko bhi hila deta hai. Allah ne un par intehai thandi, cheekhne wali aur haddiyon ko jamane wali hawa bhej di. Yeh koi aam toofan nahi tha. Yeh hawa un ko zameen se is tarah ukhaad kar phenk deti thi jaise darakht jarr samet nikal diya jaye. Un ke sar jism se juda ho gaye, aur un ki laashen zameen par is tarah padi thin jaise khajoor ke sookhay, khokhlay tanay.

Yeh azaab saat raatain aur aath din lagataar jari raha. Woh hawa unhein un ke mehalon, pahari qilon aur shehar-e-Iram ke andar tak dhoond dhoond kar maar rahi thi. Jin logon ko apni taqat, jism aur imaraton par naaz tha, woh aik pal mein mitti ka hissa ban gaye.

Aakhir mein jab azaab thama to Allah ne farmaaya: “Kya tum in mein se kisi ko baqi dekhte ho?” Na un ka ghamand bacha, na un ka shehar, aur na un ke buland sutoon. Sirf khamosh, ujray huay ghar aur ibret ka nishan reh gaya.

Yeh video humein yeh sabak deta hai ke jab insaan apni taqat par itraata hai aur Allah ke paighaam ko jhutla deta hai, to phir us ka anjaam sirf tabahi hota hai. Yeh kahani aaj ke daur ke liye bhi ek wazeh warning hai.

description:
ঘরের উন্নতির জন্য সূরা বাকারা প্রতিদিন শুনুন I Surah Al Baqarah Full Quran Recitation | Alaa Aqel


#সূরাবাকারা #surahbaqarah 


Surah Al-Baqarah سورة البقرة

সূরা বাকারা, কুরআনের সবচেয়ে দীর্ঘতম সূরা, আয়াত সংখ্যা ২৮৬, মাসহাফে এটি সূরা ফাতিহার পর দ্বিতীয় ক্রমে এর অবস্থান। রেওয়ায়েত রয়েছে যে ইহা মদিনায় নাযিল হওয়া সর্বপ্রথম সূরা, তবে এই আয়াতটি ছাড়া وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى اللهِ ثُمَّ تُوفَّى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ কেননা, এটি আসমান থেকে নাযিলকৃত শেষ আয়াত যা বিদায় হজ্জের সময় মিনায় কোরবানীর দিন নাযিল হয়েছে। সুদ সংক্রান্ত আয়াতও কুরআনের প্রথম দিকে নাযিল হয়। খালিদ বিন মা'দান বলেন, এ সূরার মর্যাদা, মহিমা, হুকুম-আহকাম ও উপদেশের আধিক্য ইত্যাদি কারণে একে ফুসতাতুল কুরআন (কুরআনের বসতি) বলা হয়। উমর ইবনুল খাত্তাব এ সূরাটির আইনশাস্ত্র এবং এতে যা আছে তা শিখতে বারো বছর সময় নেন, যেখানে তাঁর পুত্র আবদুল্লাহ ইবনে উমর আট বছরেই শিখে ফেলেছিলেন। কারণ এ সূরাটি একেবারে নাযিল না হয়ে ধাপে ধাপে নাযিল হয়।

আবু মাসউদ আল-আনসারী (রাঃ) থেকে বর্ণিত, তিনি বলেন, নবী করীম সাল্লাল্লাহু আলাইহি বলেছেনঃ "সূরা বাকারার শেষের দুটি আয়াত, যে ব্যক্তি রাতে পাঠ করবে, তা তার জন্য যথেষ্ট।" [১২]

আবু হুরায়রা (রাঃ) থেকে বর্ণিত যে, সাল্লাল্লাহু আলাইহি ওয়াসাল্লাম বলেছেনঃ "তোমরা তোমাদের ঘরকে কবর বানাবে না, আর যে ঘরে সূরা বাকারা পাঠ করা হয় সে ঘরে শয়তান প্রবেশ করবে না।" [১৩] [১৪][১৫]

সাহল বিন সাদ (রাঃ) থেকে বর্ণিত, রাসূলুল্লাহ () বলেছেনঃ "প্রত্যেক জিনিসেরই একটি কুঁজ থাকে, এবং কুরআনের কুঁজ হল বাকারা সুরা, আর যে ব্যক্তি এক রাতে নিজের ঘরে এটি পাঠ করবে, শয়তান তার তিন রাত পর্যন্ত প্রবেশ করবে না।" [১৬]

আবু (রা) থেকে বর্ণিত, তিনি বলেন, আমি রাসূলুল্লাহ (সাল্লাল্লাহু 'আলাইহি ওয়া সাল্লাম)-কে বলতে শুনেছি: "তোমরা কোরআন পড়, কেননা কেয়ামতের দিন এটি তার লোকদের জন্য সুপারিশ করবে। তোমরা জাহরাউইন (আল-বাকারা এবং আল-ইমরান) পাঠ কর, কারণ তারা কিয়ামতের দিন আসবে যেন তারা মেঘ বা দুটি মেঘ। অথবা যেন কিয়ামতের দিন তারা দুই দল পাখী তাদের পরিবারের পক্ষে তর্ক করছে। তারপর তিনি বললেন: সুরা বাকারা পড়, কেননা এটা আকড়ে ধরা আশীর্বাদ, আর ছেড়ে দেয়াটা আফসোস। এবং কোনো বাতলাহ ধরতে পারবে না।" [১৭]

জাহরাউইন অর্থ: দুটি আলোক, আল-গিয়াবাহ অর্থ: যা উপর থেকে ছায়া দেয়, আল-ফারাক: কোন কিছুর টুকরো, বাতালাহ অর্থ: যাদুকররা।

ঘটনাটি সূরা আল-বাকারার ৬৭-৭৩ নং আয়াতে উল্লেখ করা হয়েছেঃ

"স্মরণ কর, যখন মূসা (আ.) স্বীয় সম্প্রদায়কে বলেছিল, 'আল্লাহ তোমাদেরকে একটি গরু যবহ করার আদেশ দিচ্ছেন'; তারা বলেছিল, 'তুমি কি আমাদের সঙ্গে ঠাট্টা করছো? মূসা বলল, আল্লাহর আশ্রয় নিচ্ছি, যাতে আমি অজ্ঞদের অন্তর্ভুক্ত না হই।"
তারা বলল, 'আমাদের জন্য তোমার প্রতিপালককে স্পষ্টভাবে জানিয়ে দিতে বল তা কীরূপ? মূসা বলল, 'আল্লাহ বলছেন, তা এমন এক গরু যা বৃদ্ধও নয় এবং অল্প বয়স্কও নয়- মধ্য বয়সী। সুতরাং যা (করতে) আদিষ্ট হয়েছ, তা পালন কর'।"

"তারা বলল, 'তুমি আমাদের জন্য তোমার রবের নিকট দো'আ কর, তিনি যেন আমাদের জন্য স্পষ্ট করে দেন, কেমন তার রঙ'? সে বলল, 'নিশ্চয় তিনি বলছেন, নিশ্চয় তা হবে হলুদ রঙের গাভী, তার রঙ উজ্জ্বল, দর্শকদেরকে যা আনন্দ দেবে'।"

"তারা বলল, 'তুমি আমাদের জন্য তোমার রবের নিকট দো'আ কর, তিনি যেন আমাদের জন্য স্পষ্ট করে দেন, তা কেমন? নিশ্চয় গরুটি আমাদের জন্য সন্দেহপূর্ণ হয়ে গিয়েছে। আর নিশ্চয় আমরা আল্লাহ চাহে তো পথপ্রাপ্ত হব'।"

"সে বলল, 'নিশ্চয় তিনি বলছেন, 'নিশ্চয় তা এমন গাভী, যা ব্যবহৃত হয়নি জমি চাষ করায় আর না ক্ষেতে পানি দেয়ায়। সুস্থ যাতে কোন খুঁত নেই'। তারা বলল, 'এখন তুমি সত্য নিয়ে এসেছ'। অতঃপর তারা তা যবেহ করল অথচ তারা তা করার ছিল না।"

"আর স্মরণ কর, যখন তোমরা একজনকে হত্যা করলে অতঃপর সে ব্যাপারে একে অপরকে দোষারোপ করলে। আর আল্লাহ প্রকাশ করে দিলেন তোমরা যা গোপন করছিলে।"

"অতঃপর আমি বললাম, 'তোমরা তাকে আঘাত কর গাভীটির (গোশতের) কিছু অংশ দিয়ে। এভাবে আল্লাহ জীবিত করেন মৃতদেরকে। আর তিনি তোমাদেরকে তাঁর নিদর্শনসমূহ দেখান,যাতে তোমরা বুঝ।"

সূরা আল-বাকারার এই নামে নামকরণ করা হয়েছে কারণ এতে বনী ইসরাঈলের গাভীর কাহিনী রয়েছে এবং এটি ইহুদীদের কাছ থেকে যেমন ঘটেছিল আল্লাহর আইন বাস্তবায়নের জন্য তাড়াহুড়ো করার প্রয়োজনীয়তা নির্দেশ করে। সূরা আল-বাকারার অন্যতম উদ্দেশ্য হল উম্মতকে পৃথিবী গড়ার জন্য প্রস্তুত করা, আল্লাহর ধর্ম প্রতিষ্ঠা করা এবং মানুষের প্রকৃতি স্পষ্ট করে দেওয়া এবং এতে রয়েছে ইমানের ভিত্তি এবং শরীয়তের সম্পূর্ণতা। [১৮]

সূরা আল-বাকারার সবচেয়ে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ বৈশিষ্ট্যগুলির মধ্যে রয়েছে:

এটি কোরানের দীর্ঘতম সূরা। [১৯]

এতে পবিত্র কোরআনের শেষ আয়াত রয়েছে।

এটি কোরানের দীর্ঘতম আয়াত (ঋণের দায়েনা আয়াত) ধারণ করে।

এতে রয়েছে কোরআনের সর্বশ্রেষ্ঠ আয়াত (আয়াতুল কুরসি)।

নবীর জীবনীতে উল্লেখ করা হয়েছে, এ সূরা কিয়ামতের দিন তার পাঠকের পক্ষে লড়বে, এ সূরাতে রয়েছে ইসমে আজম, তাকে এটি দ্বারা ডাকা হলে তিনি উত্তর দেন এবং এটি আকড়ে ধরা আশীর্বাদ এবং এটি ছেড়ে যাওয়া অনুশোচনা, এবং যাদুকরেরা এটি বহন করতে পারে না।

title: Book Release: The Uncrucified Christ | Dr. Ali Ataie
description:
The wait is over! Dr. Ali Ataie's highly anticipated book, The Uncrucified Christ, is officially here!

Was Jesus of Nazareth (ʿĪsā عليه السلام) actually crucified? Is the crucifixion an established historical fact, or is there room for a serious scholarly reassessment of one of the most widely accepted claims in Christian history?

In his groundbreaking new book, The Uncrucified Christ, Dr. Ali Ataie challenges conventional historical assumptions surrounding the crucifixion of Jesus and presents a scholarly defense of the historical plausibility of the Qur'anic account.

Drawing upon biblical scholarship, historical criticism, early Christian history, textual analysis, and Islamic theology, Dr. Ataie engages one of the most consequential questions in the history of Christian-Muslim dialogue: What really happened to Jesus of Nazareth?

The Qur'an declares:

"And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them." (Qur'an 4:157)

For centuries, the Qur'anic denial of Jesus' crucifixion has stood in sharp contrast to the traditional Christian narrative and the prevailing consensus among historians. But how conclusive is the historical evidence? What assumptions underlie the scholarly consensus, and can an alternative reconstruction of the events surrounding Jesus' final days be historically defensible?

In this special book release video, we celebrate the publication of Dr. Ataie's long-awaited work and introduce readers to an important contribution to contemporary Islamic scholarship, historical Jesus studies, and Christian-Muslim theological engagement.

Whether you are Muslim, Christian, a student of biblical studies, or simply interested in the historical Jesus, *The Uncrucified Christ* invites you to revisit one of history's most significant religious questions through a fresh and thought-provoking scholarly perspective.

EMAIL RECEIVED – WHAT DOES IT MEAN?
If you received an email about the CM Punjab E-Bike Scheme 2026, it does not automatically mean that you have been selected. The email may be an application acknowledgement, verification update, request for information or another processing notification. Read the complete message and compare it with the status in your official account.

BALLOTING AND SELECTION LIST
The Punjab government has said that 100,000 students will be selected through balloting. The announced distribution start date is 5 November 2026, but this does not mean every applicant will receive a bike on the same day. Check the official portal for your own result and further instructions. Do not trust unofficial lists or screenshots shared on WhatsApp and Facebook.

WHERE TO CHECK YOUR SELECTION / APPLICATION STATUS?
Official portal: https://bikes.punjab.gov.pk/
Log in with the same CNIC and account details used during registration. Check your dashboard for the latest status and instructions. If a selection list is published, verify it through an official Punjab Government announcement or portal link. Avoid unknown websites asking for your CNIC, password or personal details.

BANK OF PUNJAB STATUS / VERIFICATION
A bank-related status may concern document checking, guarantor information, eligibility or financing. Its exact meaning depends on the status shown in your account and the official message you receive. If more documents are required, follow the instructions provided by the scheme. Never share your OTP, password or banking credentials with anyone.

WHEN WILL THE BIKE BE DELIVERED?
The distribution phase has been announced to start from 5 November 2026. Individual handover dates, locations and next steps may differ. Wait for official selection and delivery instructions before visiting a dealer or office. Do not pay an agent who promises guaranteed selection or early delivery.

• Phase 2 aims to provide 100,000 electric bikes to students.
• The government has stated that selection will be through balloting.
• Distribution is announced to begin on 5 November 2026.
• Reported monthly instalments are around Rs. 3,000; confirm the final amount in your own financing documents.
• The Punjab government has said it will bear the interest cost.

Always verify final terms and your personal status through official sources.

Q: Does receiving an email mean I am selected?

Want Allah's Blessings in Your Life? Never Miss These 6 Habits | Samih Jad Speakes
description:
Do you want more blessings, peace, and happiness in your life? Do you wish to strengthen your connection with Allah and make Him a part of every moment of your day? The key to a blessed life is not only making dua when you need something, but also remembering Allah consistently throughout your daily routine. In this powerful Islamic reminder, Samih Jad shares six important habits that can help you increase your Dhikr, strengthen your Iman, and develop a deeper relationship with Allah.

The first habit is to take advantage of the blessed times for remembering Allah, especially in the morning after Fajr and in the evening before sunset. These precious moments are excellent opportunities to recite the morning and evening Adhkar taught by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The second habit is to increase your remembrance of Allah through meaningful words of Dhikr, such as SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, and Allahu Akbar. Remembering Allah with sincere hearts and understanding the meaning of these beautiful words can bring countless spiritual benefits into your life.

The third habit is to make the recitation of the Holy Quran a part of your daily routine. Even if you begin with a few verses every day, consistency is what matters. Every letter of the Quran carries a reward, and regular recitation helps keep your heart connected to the words of Allah. The fourth habit is to use your free and wasted moments wisely. Whether you are travelling, waiting in a queue, cooking, walking, or completing everyday tasks, you can use these moments to remember Allah instead of allowing your time to pass without benefit.

The fifth habit is to improve your Salah and make it a true opportunity to remember Allah. Prayer should not become a routine performed without concentration or understanding. Instead, give your Salah the attention it deserves, reflect on what you recite, and make sincere Dua to Allah. The sixth and most important habit is to connect Dhikr with every situation in your life, following the beautiful example of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. From waking up and leaving your home to eating, drinking, travelling, experiencing difficulties, and receiving blessings, remember Allah in every situation. You can also speak to Allah in your own language and ask Him for your needs through sincere Dua.

This powerful reminder by Samih Jad teaches us that remembering Allah is not limited to a specific time, place, or form of worship. It is a way of life that keeps our hearts alive and strengthens our connection with our Creator. Start applying these six habits from today, even if you begin with small steps. Make Dhikr a regular part of your daily routine, remain consistent in your worship, and encourage your family and friends to remember Allah as well. May Allah fill our lives with His blessings, grant peace to our hearts, increase our Iman, and make us among those who remember Him abundantly. Ameen.

title: Why are "Muslim" Countries Banning The Hijab?
description:
How does a country that is 96% Muslim turn little girls away from school for wearing the hijab? In this episode of Muslim Atlas, we look at Azerbaijan’s school ban and a wider pattern across Central Asia, where Muslim majority governments in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan have moved against the hijab, the niqab, beards and religious education.

To understand why, we go back over a thousand years. From Prince Vladimir’s famous rejection of Islam, to Ivan the Terrible’s conquest of the Muslim khanates, to Catherine II’s invention of a state controlled muftiate, we trace how the Russian Empire built a system to contain and control its Muslim subjects.

Then came the Soviet Union. Mosques were closed in their thousands, scholars were shot or sent to the Gulag, waqf lands were seized, scripts were changed twice in a single generation, and the Hujum campaign tore the veil from women at public rallies. The Kazakh famine alone killed around a quarter of the population.

When the USSR collapsed in 1991, the same Communist Party men took power in the newly independent states, and they kept the same tools: official state Islam, the language of “extremism”, the demonisation of the veil, national identity placed above faith, and a surveillance state to enforce it all. This is the story of how colonised nations came to mimic their colonisers, and why the hijab ban is a symptom of something much older.

title: Raised by iPad or Raised by Taqwa? 6 Rules of Islamic Parenting | Part 1 | Sh. Mirza Yawar Baig
description:
"Allah gave the child to you. You give the child to the iPhone, then the iPhone will get the sadaqah of this child, not you."

You will not be asked whether your child became a doctor or an engineer. You will be asked about one thing: their tarbiyah. In Part 1 of this parenting workshop in Kuwait, Sh. Mirza Yawar Baig shows why the screen is lethal for children, what to do tonight, and the six rules of Islamic parenting that raise a child on taqwa.

About Momin Saeed

Momin Saeed is the Head of Abrahamic Finance, an Islamic finance advisory organization serving clients throughout Canada and internationally. He is an experienced Islamic finance professional, real estate investor, entrepreneur, and advocate for ethical financial practices.

He also serves as the Canadian Country Correspondent for Islamic Finance News, providing international readers with reporting and analysis on developments within Canada's growing Islamic finance industry.

Momin holds the Certified Shariah Advisor and Auditor (CSAA) designation from the Accounting and Auditing Organization for Islamic Financial Institutions (AAOIFI) in Bahrain and the Chartered Islamic Finance Professional (CIFP) designation from INCEIF University in Malaysia.

He is also a member of the Chartered Institute of Islamic Finance Professionals (CIIF) and has participated in international conferences, professional presentations, and published work related to Islamic financial development.

Alongside his Islamic finance advisory activities, Momin brings nearly two decades of experience in Canadian commercial real estate as an investor and developer.

As Founder and President of NŪR Real Estate Group in Alberta, Canada, he is developing innovative investment partnerships designed to provide Shariah-compliant ownership opportunities in commercial real estate, including multifamily, industrial, and self-storage properties.

His work emphasizes genuine risk-sharing, equity-based investment structures, and alternatives to conventional interest-bearing financing.

Through Abrahamic Finance, Momin also advises emerging technology companies and entrepreneurial ventures, helping organizations develop business models and financial strategies consistent with ethical and Islamic financial principles.

He holds an MBA from the Smith School of Business at Queen's University and a Bachelor of Commerce in Accounting from the University of Alberta.

Earlier in his career, he served as the first Executive Director of the Alberta Muslim Public Affairs Council, an organization subsequently incorporated into the National Council of Canadian Muslims.

Combining financial expertise, entrepreneurship, and community leadership, Momin continues to advance Islamic finance, responsible investment, and sustainable economic opportunities throughout North America.

“Business Ethics Across Religions & the Implications for Modern Finance”

The North American Conference on Islamic Finance brings together scholars, researchers, financial professionals, entrepreneurs, and industry leaders to explore the intersection of ethical principles, religious values, sustainability, and contemporary financial practices.

title: How to Control Anger and Protect Yourself from Shaytan
description:
When Someone Hurts You, How Should You Respond? | Controlling Anger in Islam

When someone insults us, hurts us or treats us unfairly, our natural reaction may be to retaliate. But the Quran teaches us something far more powerful: to respond to evil with what is best.

Allah says in Surat Fussilat (41:34):

“Good and evil are not equal. Repel evil with what is best, and the one between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he were a close friend.”

In this tafsir of Surat Fussilat (Ayahs 34–36), Shaykh Haytham Tamim explains how we can overcome anger, respond to provocation with patience and kindness, and protect ourselves from the whispers of Shaytan.

00:00 How should we respond when someone hurts us?
00:54 How the Prophet ﷺ responded to insults and provocation
02:26 Why controlling anger takes practice
03:24 Think before you react
04:45 The story of the Jewish rabbi who tested the Prophet ﷺ
06:32 How enemies can become close friends
07:47 Kindness is a sign of strength, not weakness
09:09 Why patience is essential
12:10 How Shaytan exploits our weaknesses
13:12 Shaytan's whispers – a spiritual cyberattack
15:42 How to seek refuge in Allah effectively
17:36 Why remembering Allah protects us from Shaytan
18:37 Training ourselves through salah and dhikr

Saying A‘udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim (I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan) should not be an empty phrase. It is a sincere appeal to Allah for protection, made with conviction and awareness.

True strength is not having the power to retaliate. It is having the self-control to choose a better response.

Part of Utrujj's Activate Your Imaan tafsir series with Shaykh Haytham Tamim.

title: Gaza, the ʿUlamā, and the Failure of the Muslim Political Class | Hashiya by Yaqeen
description:
Is the crisis facing Muslims today a failure of knowledge or a failure of will? 

Editor-in-Chief Dr. Ovamir Anjum sits down with Hashiya authors Dr. Farah El-Sharif and Dr. Ebrahim Moosa to take up that question through their respective essays "Islam After Gaza: Rebirth After Tribulation" and "Inhabiting the Threshold: The Madrasa Between Inheritance and Interrogation."

They agree on the diagnosis: failed political leadership, the state capture of religious scholarship, and the hollowness of the "rules-based order." They part ways on the cure. Should scholars act now, with courage and moral clarity, or invest first in the deep formation needed to act wisely? Along the way they ask what's missing from madrasa education, and whether modern Islam has lost the Prophet ﷺ.

description:
مراجعة الوحدة الثانية برمجة تانية بكالوريا 2027 | الأمن السيبراني وحل امتحان | مستر أحمد حامد

🔐 في مراجعة الوحدة الثانية برمجة تانية بكالوريا 2027، مستر أحمد حامد مجمعلك شرح الوحدة الثانية «الأمن السيبراني» كاملة، مع مراجعة أهم الأفكار وحل امتحان شامل على الوحدة، عشان تعرف تربط الدروس ببعض وتتعامل مع أسئلة الامتحان بثقة.

هنبدأ مع مستر أحمد حامد بمراجعة أهداف الأمن السيبراني، والفرق بين السرية والسلامة والتوافر، وبعدها هنشرح الدرس الأول «تقنيات التشفير والمصادقة» وهنفهم إزاي بنحمي البيانات أثناء انتقالها عبر الإنترنت.

هنراجع الفرق بين HTTP وHTTPS، ودور بروتوكول TLS، والتشفير المتماثل والتشفير بالمفتاح العام، وكمان الشهادات الرقمية والتوقيع الرقمي والمصادقة الثنائية ومتعددة العوامل.

💻 بعد كده هننتقل للدرس الثاني «تصميم أمان الشبكات»، وهنفهم مع مستر أحمد حامد إزاي المؤسسات بتحمي شبكاتها باستخدام جدار الحماية Firewall، والشبكات الافتراضية الخاصة VPN، والمنطقة المعزولة DMZ، ومفهوم الدفاع في العمق Defense in Depth، والفرق بين الأمان التقليدي ونهج انعدام الثقة Zero Trust.

وفي الدرس الثالث «الاستجابة للحوادث وإدارة المخاطر» هنراجع إزاي نتعامل مع أي حادث أمني، بداية من التحضير والاكتشاف، مرورًا بالاحتواء وإزالة التهديد والاستعادة، وصولًا للدروس المستفادة، مع فهم طريقة تقييم المخاطر وتحديد الأولويات.

✅ وفي الجزء الأخير من المحاضرة هنحل مع مستر أحمد حامد امتحان شامل على الوحدة الثانية، فيه أسئلة اختيار من متعدد وصح وغلط وأسئلة مقالية بتربط بين أفكار الدروس الثلاثة.

الفكرة مش إنك تحفظ الإجابة، لكن إنك تفهم السؤال وتعرف توصل للحل حتى لو جالك بصياغة مختلفة في الامتحان.

لو بتدور على مراجعة الوحدة الثانية برمجة تانية بكالوريا 2027، أو مراجعة الأمن السيبراني تانية بكالوريا، أو حل امتحان الوحدة الثانية برمجة 2027، فالمحاضرة دي هتساعدك تلم الوحدة وتراجع عليها بشكل منظم.

title: Zombie Outbreak Survival: The One Mistake That Gets You Killed
description:
Your neighbor is in the middle of the street, chewing on something that used to be the mailman. Your phone is at two percent, and what you do in the next ten seconds could decide whether you see Tuesday. Most people freeze. This video asks what happens if you don’t.

This is a day-by-day walkthrough of a zombie outbreak, from the first hour to day thirty. Zombies are fiction, but the survival habits are real, and they’d help in plenty of real emergencies. We cover why running for the highway may be the deadliest choice you can make, how normalcy bias makes people hesitate when they should act, and what it takes to secure water, shelter, and supplies. We also look at how survival groups form and fall apart, and why the middle of the month is one of the most dangerous stretches. Then comes the one mistake that gets people killed again and again in zombie stories, and it isn’t the bite.

If you’re curious how people endure disasters, history has plenty of examples to learn from.

Subscribe for more dark stories about survival and the end of the world, and tell us in the comments the first thing you’d grab on day one.

title: Why Allah Allows Divorce & How He Enriches You | Shaykh Mikaeel
description:
Shaykh Mikaeel on why staying in a broken marriage out of fear of being broke or alone completely misses who Allah is.

Have you ever stayed in a painful situation just because you were terrified of what happens to your security once you leave? You convince yourself that your spouse is the source of your sustenance and love. But Allah reminds you that people are merely channels, not the ultimate source. When you cling out of terror, you forget His name Al-Mughni, The Enricher.

Look at the story of Barira and Mughith in Medina, where the Prophet ﷺ respected her choice to walk away, or how Allah enriched the Prophet ﷺ through Khadija without making her irreplaceable. When a separation happens, the Quran promises that Allah will enrich both people from His boundless abundance. What you need comes directly from Him, never just the human channel.

If you've been terrified to walk away from a toxic marriage because you fear ending up broke or alone, this will reframe your tawakkul.
If you've been struggling to stay patient and avoid haram while waiting for the means to get married, take heart in Allah's timing.
If you've ever felt completely empty while chasing superficial wealth or social media validation, this reminder shows where true richness lives.

If this lecture helped you, share it with someone who needs to hear that Allah is Al-Mughni and can enrich them even through divorce or delayed marriage. May Allah reward you.

title: Fiqh Lecture: Issues Concerning Disliked Acts During Prayer | October 30th, 2026
description:
This lecture, delivered by Sheikh Ammar Yasir at Masjid Omar, focuses on the fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) regarding actions that are considered disliked (makruh) during prayer (salah).

Key topics covered include:

Distractions and fidgeting: The speaker explains the importance of maintaining focus and humility (khushu) in prayer, advising against unnecessary movements or playing with clothing, hair, or surroundings.
Postural discipline: Discussion on maintaining proper composure and avoiding haste, which can detract from the reverence of the act of worship.
Disliked bodily actions: Guidance on specific physical habits or expressions that should be avoided to preserve the sanctity and correctness of the prayer.
The purpose of prayer: A recurring theme is that the prayer is a direct conversation with the Creator, and therefore, one should strive to perform it with the utmost care, stillness, and concentration.

title: Psychology of the Haram Police
Allah Is Making You an Offer You Cannot Afford to Refuse
description:
What if helping others is actually the greatest thing you can do for yourself?

In this powerful reminder, Yasmin Mogahed explains a profound Islamic principle: the way we treat Allah's creation is connected to how we receive His mercy.

When you help someone in need, show mercy to others, forgive those who hurt you, or give something for the sake of Allah, you are not truly losing anything.

You are investing in your Hereafter.

Through powerful reminders from the Quran and Sunnah, Yasmin Mogahed explores:

- Why helping others is ultimately helping yourself
- How Allah promises mercy to those who show mercy
- Why charity is never truly lost
- The reality of what we take with us into the grave
- The power of Sadaqah Jariyah
- How forgiving others can become a means of receiving Allah's forgiveness
- Why everything we give for the sake of Allah remains with us
- The importance of standing against injustice and helping the vulnerable

One of the most powerful lessons in this talk is that what we hold onto in this life will eventually pass away. But what we give for the sake of Allah is never truly lost.

May Allah make us among those who show mercy, forgive others, help those in need, and seek His forgiveness.

Watch until the end and reflect on this question:

**What are you holding onto that Allah is asking you to give?**

Subscribe for more Islamic reminders, Quran reflections, and powerful talks from Yasmin Mogahed.

title: Is Homeschooling for Everyone? | Mariyam & Rustam of Crink
description:
Can a child really learn well without going to school every day? In this episode of Uppu Podcast, we sit down with Mariyam and Rustam, founders of Crink, an AI-native online counselling platform, who have homeschooled their four children.

We begin with a bigger question: in the age of AI, what is school for, and what can’t a machine replace? From there we talk about how they started with a one-year trial, why they say homeschooling is not for everyone, the “bad company” worry, free play, boredom, and what a day at home looks like. We also cover the practical side: syllabus, NIOS and exams, life after 12th, and what homeschoolers can miss. Along the way: dyslexia, reading in English and Malayalam, higher-order thinking, and how they approach the Seerah with their children.

title: UNDERSTANDING YOUR MARITAL NERVOUS SYSTEM: Why Couples Fight and How to Build a Peaceful Marriage
description:
Theme: Neuroscience, Emotional Intelligence, Marriage Counselling and Islamic Spirituality

Why do couples who genuinely love each other repeatedly hurt one another? Why do small disagreements become major arguments? Why does one spouse pursue conversation while the other withdraws? And how can couples break destructive patterns and build a marriage characterised by emotional safety, mutual understanding and sakīnah?

In this insightful lecture, Ustaz Dr. Abdulfattah Adeyemi explores the fascinating intersection of neuroscience, psychology, marriage counselling and Islamic spirituality to help us understand what happens inside us—and between us—when relationships become emotionally challenging.

Our nervous systems influence how we respond to criticism, interpret silence, experience emotional triggers, and manage conflict. When we understand these responses, we can begin moving from automatic reactions towards deliberate, compassionate and responsible behaviour.

Drawing on practical relationship principles and the guidance of the Qur'an and Sunnah, this lecture offers a deeper understanding of what it takes to build a healthier, more peaceful and spiritually fulfilling marriage.

THIS LECTURE IS FOR:

Married couples seeking to improve communication and emotional intimacy.

Singles preparing for marriage and wanting to understand relationship dynamics.

Muslim couples interested in integrating Islamic values with practical relationship skills.

Parents, family counsellors, marriage educators and relationship coaches.

Anyone interested in emotional intelligence, human behaviour and personal development.

THE CENTRAL MESSAGE: 

You may not control every emotion that arises within you, but you can learn to respond more wisely. A healthier marriage is not necessarily one without disagreements; it is one in which both partners learn to address difficulties with greater understanding, responsibility, respect and mercy.

Watch, reflect, share with someone who may benefit, and begin practising the lessons in your own relationships.

title: 7 Lessons Every Genocide Teaches Us | Suleiman Hani
description:
Genocide doesn't begin with violence alone. It begins with words, dehumanization, propaganda, and the silence of those who witness injustice.

What lessons should we learn from the atrocities of the past and present, and how should those lessons change the way we live?

In this Jumuah khutbah, Shaykh Suleiman Hani explores 7 lessons from genocide and ethnic cleansing, drawing from the Qur'an, the story of the People of the Ditch (Ashab al-Ukhdud), Prophet Musa (AS) and Pharaoh, and examples of oppression throughout history and our world today.

From Palestine and Sudan to Bosnia and the Rohingya, this khutbah examines the patterns of injustice, the responsibilities of witnesses, and the certainty of Allah's justice.

The seven lessons explore:
1. How dehumanization and propaganda pave the way for violence.
2. Why remaining a passive spectator is not always neutral.
3. Why institutions of power cannot be our only source of hope.
4. How oppressors justify their actions and see themselves as righteous.
5. Why no injustice escapes Allah's knowledge or accountability.
6. The importance of breaking cycles of abuse and oppression.
7. Why faith, certainty, and trust in Allah endure beyond oppression.

These lessons aren't limited to global conflicts. They also challenge us to examine how we treat our families, neighbors, colleagues, and communities.

What role do we play when injustice takes place, and what will we leave behind for the next generation?

Watch the full khutbah and share this reminder.

title: Are Muslims Allowed to Vote in America? | Islam & Civic Responsibility
description:
Are Muslims allowed to vote in America? What does Islam teach about civic participation, justice, and responsibility toward the society in which we live?

In this thought-provoking episode of the SB Life Institute Podcast, host Safraz Bacchus explores an important question facing Muslim communities in the United States: Should Muslims actively participate in the democratic process, and what role does faith play in making that decision?

Drawing on his experiences within the American Muslim community, Safraz discusses the challenges of belonging, anti-Muslim prejudice, political participation, and the importance of recognizing that Muslims are an integral part of the society they call home.

The conversation begins with his experience attending the Muslim Day Parade in New York, where a post promoting unity and togetherness attracted hateful and anti-Muslim comments. He reflects on the importance of responding to prejudice while standing confidently for dignity, belonging, and shared humanity.

### WHAT THIS EPISODE EXPLORES

• Muslims and Voting in America:  Why civic participation matters and how Muslims can exercise their democratic rights.

• Faith and Civic Responsibility:  How Islamic teachings encourage responsibility toward God, family, neighbours, and the wider community.

• The Quran and Justice:  A reflection on Quran 4:135 and the responsibility to stand firmly for justice, even when it is difficult.

• Belonging and Muslim Identity:  Why Muslim Americans should not see themselves as second-class citizens or feel disconnected from their society.

• Choosing Ethical Leadership:  Why integrity, accountability, compassion, and service should matter when evaluating public leadership.

• Empowering the Next Generation: Why young people need education, critical thinking, and opportunities to participate in shaping their communities.

• Unity Over Division:  Why communities benefit from leaders who bring people together rather than divide them based on religion, race, ethnicity, or nationality.

Safraz also discusses the importance of supporting those who work toward justice and the common good, drawing upon the Quranic teaching to cooperate in righteousness and goodness.

This is not about promoting a political party or telling people which candidate to support. It is about understanding civic responsibility, making informed choices, and recognizing the power individuals have to contribute to their communities.

Your voice matters. Your participation matters. And your responsibility toward society does not end at the doors of your home or place of worship.

title: The Interview with H ❌ Dilly Hussain
description:
The Interview with H ❌ Dilly Hussain

Some people find their voice to be heard. Others find their voice because remaining silent is no longer an option. 🎙️

The one with Dilly Hussain (S3•E12)

What does it take to stand by your convictions when the world challenges everything you believe in?

And what happens when the very voice that gives you purpose also comes with a price?

In this upcoming episode of The Interview with H, I sit down with Dilly Hussain, co-founder of 5Pillars, editor at 1Nation Media and host of Blood Brothers, for a deeply personal conversation about faith, identity, courage, justice, sacrifice and the responsibility of having a voice.

Known for his outspoken views, challenging conversations and willingness to confront difficult issues, Dilly has become a recognisable voice in Muslim media.

But beyond the headlines, the debates and the public persona…

Who is the man behind the microphone?

We explore the experiences that shaped him.

The convictions that drive him.

The challenges of speaking out when silence might be easier.

The sacrifices that come with standing for what you believe in.

The emotional weight of witnessing injustice.

And the personal battles that the world never gets to see.

What shapes a man who refuses to remain silent?

Where does conviction end and responsibility begin?

How do you fight for justice without losing yourself in the process?

And in a world where everyone has an opinion, how do we distinguish between simply having a voice and using that voice with purpose?

We speak about Muslim identity, the power of media, the struggles facing our Ummah, brotherhood, masculinity and the importance of remaining grounded in faith when the world around us feels increasingly divided.

Because perhaps courage isn’t always about speaking louder.

Perhaps it’s about standing firm when standing alone would be easier.

Perhaps strength isn’t measured by how fiercely we defend our beliefs, but by how willing we are to question ourselves, remain humble and grow.

And perhaps the greatest test of conviction isn’t what we are prepared to say in front of the world…

But who we remain when the cameras are switched off, the applause fades and we are left alone with our conscience and Allah.

A conversation that goes beyond journalism, activism and public opinion.

A conversation about the experiences that shape us, the principles that guide us and the legacy we hope to leave behind.

Because behind every strong voice is a human story.

And sometimes, understanding that story changes the way we hear the voice.

🎙️ Coming soon on The Interview with H

title: This Is How You Make a Strong and Sincere Tawbah | 6 important Steps | Ustadh Abu Bakr Zoud
description:
Topic: This Is How You Make a Strong and Sincere Tawbah | 6 important Steps .
 Ustadh Abu Bakr Zoud 
Do you want to make a strong and sincere Tawbah (repentance) to Allah? ❤️

In this powerful Islamic reminder, discover the 6 essential steps to making a strong Tawbah to Allah (Subhanahu wa Ta'ala) and returning to Him with a sincere heart.

Here are the six important conditions of sincere repentance:

1. Tawbah for the sake of Allah: Turn back to Allah sincerely.
2. Fear, hope, and love: Repent out of fear of Allah, hope in His forgiveness, and love for Him.
3.Repent at the right time: Make Tawbah before the signs of the end of life arrive.
4.Regret your sins: Feel genuine remorse for what you have done.
5.Give up the sin: Stop committing the sin and turn back to Allah.6.
6. Make a firm commitment: Make a sincere intention in your heart never to return to that sin.
Remember, never lose hope in Allah's mercy. No matter how many mistakes you have made, turn back to Allah and seek His forgiveness.

May Allah grant us all sincere Tawbah and forgive our sins. Ameen. 🤲

In this episode:
• The difference between journaling and muḥāsaba
• How reflection can turn into repetitive overthinking
• Why specific actions reveal more than harsh labels about ourselves
• How to recognise progress we may overlook
• A five-minute evening practice
• The question behind our actions: towards whom was my heart turned?

🌙 TRY TONIGHT’S PRACTICE

After your last prayer, write three honest lines:

1. What I owed today and did.
2. What I owed today and skipped.
3. One thing I did that I shouldn’t have.

Be specific about your actions. Turn to Allah with what you have written, then choose one thing to do differently tomorrow.

And ask yourself:
“Towards whom was my heart when I did it?”

💬 What is one small change you would like to make tomorrow? Share only what you feel comfortable sharing.

title: Finding Humans in the Machine Age
description:
Since the industrial revolutions of the late nineteenth century, our civilization has increasingly modeled itself after the factory and the processor. We have constructed a world obsessed with raw efficiency, instrumentation, speed, and continuous measurement. In this system, those who learn to think, work, and act like machines are rewarded with status and wealth.



 



Meanwhile, those who long for a more soulful, unhurried existence, seeking to live as integrated human beings connected to the earth, the cosmos, and their Creator, are often sidelined and told to adapt or be left behind. In today’s episode we explore how to reclaim our humanity from the gears of this mechanical age.



 



 



Book recommendations:



 



The Burnout Society by Byung-Chul Han



Fahrenheit 451 by Ray Bradbury



 



About the hosts:



Walead Mosaad is an internationally recognized scholar in Islamic studies and human development. His academic and traditional training has accorded him the opportunity to work with communities worldwide as a teacher and project driver. He has completed degrees from Rutgers University and Fath Islamic Seminary in Damascus. He received his PhD from the University of Exeter in Arab and Islamic Studies, and was also classically trained at the Al-Azhar University.



He is currently the Chair and Scholar-in-Residence of Sabeel Community. He has traveled extensively throughout the Muslim world, as well as Europe and the Far East, delivering lectures on various topics, including spirituality, ethics and intercultural peace building.



https://www.sabeelcommunity.org/walead-mohammed-mosaad  



 



 



Rehan Khan is a professor of leadership and novelist. He is an advocate for virtue-based storytelling as well as leading with a moral lens. Over 30 years Rehan has advised several global and regional brands. As an adjunct professor he teaches post-graduate courses in AI and the Future of Work, as well as Leadership: A Moral Perspective, and Personal Influence at one of the world’s leading international business schools.



He is a keen observer of history and techno-science. Rehan is the author of a Tomb of Empires (2024) a historical fiction set in 90BC in the Middle East, the Carnegie nominated A Tudor Turk trilogy (2019-2022) set in the Ottoman Empire and Tudor England, and the fantasy sci-fi series, Tales of Khayaal (2025) set on the Earth like planet of Ikleel. These gripping stories also ask readers to consider the role of virtue within the human story.

title: The Last Umayyad Caliph | IHP 11-3
description:
The rise and reign of Marwan II (Marwan ibn Muhammad) marked the desperate final stand of the Umayyad Caliphate as internal fractures tore the empire apart from within. Emerging from years of rugged campaigning in the Caucasus, Marwan brought a hardened, regimental military doctrine to an empire paralyzed by systemic crisis and exhausted frontiers.   

The rapid collapse of central authority created an unprecedented power vacuum in the imperial core. Following the assassination of Walid II, the short caliphates of Yazid III and Ibrahim shattered dynasty legitimacy, sparking immediate challenges across Syria, Palestine, and Iraq. As royal contenders traded assassinations and purges, the volatile Qays-Yaman rivalry exploded into open civil war, disintegrating the traditional Syrian military dominance that had upheld the dynasty for nearly a century.   

Across the provinces, regional defiance accelerated the dynastic decline. The far western Maghreb splintered with the emergence of the heretical Bargawata Confederation, while the frontiers of Khorasan devolved into factional infighting between Nasr ibn Sayyar and Juday al-Kirmani. In Iraq, a sweeping Kharijite resurgence led by al-Dahhak overwhelmed major garrison towns, drawing defectors from every quarter.   

Marwan’s southern march from Haran culminated in the bloody Battle of Ain al-Jar, driving Ibrahim from power and placing Marwan on the throne of a fragmented realm. Yet even as he brutally besieged Homs and quelled Syrian uprisings, the gathering Abbasid storm in the east was quietly preparing to sweep away the entire Umayyad order under Ibrahim the Imam and Abu Muslim. This breakdown explores the military maneuvers, palace coups, and deep-seated tribal fractures that defined the climax of the Third Fitna.

title: Would Anyone Miss Muslims If They Disappeared? | Dr. Shadee ElMasry
description:
Are Muslims sometimes making it harder for people to embrace Islam, practice their faith, or find a place within the Muslim community?

In **Season 7, Episode 6 of *Talking With Teachers***, Dr. Abdullah bin Hamid Ali welcomes **Dr. Shadee ElMasry**, founder of Safina Society, for a wide-ranging and thought-provoking conversation about Muslim identity, religious commitment, community leadership, and the importance of prophetic character.

Drawing on his upbringing in America, his experiences studying Islam in Morocco, and his years of teaching and community work, Dr. Shadee reflects on the challenges facing Muslims today—and what it means to build strong, principled, and compassionate Muslim communities.

**Among the questions explored:**

- Are Muslims sometimes too judgmental toward one another?
- How can we maintain Islamic principles without alienating people who are struggling?
- What responsibilities do American Muslims have toward their neighbors and wider society?
- Why is compassion essential to effective da'wah?
- What role do traditional scholarship, good character, and spiritual companionship play in preserving Islam for future generations?

The conversation also explores Muslim political engagement, the influence of converts on American Islam, the importance of community service, and the need to build lasting connections with Allah, His Messenger ﷺ, and the Muslim community.

**One particularly challenging question emerges:** If Muslims disappeared from their communities tomorrow, would their neighbors notice their absence? Would they miss the contributions Muslims make to society?

This episode challenges us to consider not only how faithfully we practice Islam, but also how effectively we embody its teachings in our relationships with others.

**Watch the full conversation and share your thoughts:** How can Muslims uphold their religious principles while making their communities more welcoming, compassionate, and beneficial to society?

title: How Trauma Is Destroying Your Relationships
description:
Speak 1-1 with Ustadh Abdel Rahman Mussa about your trauma at https://www.endmytrauma.com/deen

How much of who you are today is being shaped by a past you thought you'd left behind?

Childhood trauma, emotional and sexual abuse, toxic relationships, broken marriages, self-sabotage, and the hidden psychological battles we fight within ourselves. Could there be more to these struggles than we realise?

In this powerful and thought-provoking episode of the Deenspiration Podcast, I'm joined by Abdel Rahman Mussa, who has spent over two decades working with survivors of childhood trauma and abuse.

Together, we explore some deeply uncomfortable questions, challenge popular narratives surrounding mental health, and examine how our past experiences can influence the way we think, love, trust, and navigate relationships.

Why do some people struggle to move on, even years after being hurt? Can healing sometimes feel like letting an abuser win? Have we become too attached to the identity of being a victim? Is modern therapy addressing the root causes of trauma, or simply helping people cope? And how does Islam fit into all of this?

We also discuss real-life cases of abuse, the dangers of religious and emotional manipulation, generational trauma, and why telling someone to "just make dua" isn't always the answer.

This isn't your typical mental health conversation. Some perspectives may challenge what you believe, others may resonate deeply with your own experiences. The goal isn't necessarily to agree on everything, but to encourage deeper understanding, meaningful discussion, and greater compassion for those silently struggling.

⚠️ **CONTENT WARNING & DISCLAIMER**

This episode contains discussions of sexual abuse, childhood trauma, emotional abuse, and other sensitive experiences that some viewers may find distressing. Viewer discretion is advised.

The views and opinions expressed by our guest are his own and do not necessarily represent those of Deenspiration. This conversation is intended for educational discussion and should not be considered medical or psychological advice, diagnosis, or treatment. If you are experiencing trauma or mental health difficulties, please seek support from an appropriately qualified professional.

title: Moments with The Messenger | Episode 4: Beloved: The Women Who Raised the Prophet ﷺ
description:
Beloved: The Women Who Raised the Prophet ﷺ

Seerah and Sisterhood: Love, Leadership, and Grief

In this gathering, we explore the women who nurtured the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the lasting place they held in his heart. Their stories invite us to reflect on caregiving, belonging, leadership, and loss—and to deepen our love for the Messenger ﷺ by getting to know him.

Our purpose is both Seerah and sisterhood: learning his story, applying its lessons, and building a community where women know and support one another.

In This Session

The women who nurtured him
We meet his mother, Aminah bint Wahb; his early wet nurse, Thuwaybah; his devoted caregiver, Barakah, known as Umm Ayman; and his wet nurse, Halimah al-Saʿdiyyah. Their care reminds us that the women who raise, nourish, and protect children have a lasting place in our collective story.

Milk kinship and the meaning of family
The discussion introduces milk kinship in Islam and the significance of bonds formed through nursing. These relationships carry enduring family connections and marriage restrictions, giving nursing a meaning far beyond a temporary arrangement of care.

Umm Ayman: a lifetime of love and service
Umm Ayman cared for the Prophet ﷺ from childhood, accompanied him through the loss of his mother, and remained beloved to him throughout his life. Her migration, service, and grief at the ending of revelation reveal a woman of profound faith whose story deserves to be remembered.

Zayd and Usamah: belonging, dignity, and leadership
The stories of Zayd ibn Harithah and his son, Usamah ibn Zayd, show how the Prophet ﷺ put human dignity into practice. His appointment of the young Usamah to lead an expedition challenged assumptions about age, ancestry, and social status.

Accountability with a path forward
Usamah’s story also brings together two powerful moments: the Prophet’s ﷺ strong correction of a grave mistake in battle and his later decision to entrust him with leadership. The lesson for parents, teachers, and community leaders is clear: hold young people accountable while allowing them to learn, grow, and earn trust.

Halimah and unexpected barakah
The session recounts the Seerah narrative of Halimah welcoming an orphan whom others had passed over, and the blessings her household experienced through his presence. Her story invites us to reconsider where we expect goodness to come from—and whom we might overlook.

Aminah’s love and the pain of letting go
Aminah’s decision to send her infant into another woman’s care opens a reflection on the difficult choices mothers make for their children’s well-being. The discussion follows his early childhood, the account of the opening of his chest, and his return to his mother.

A mother’s death and grief across a lifetime
The gathering closes with Aminah’s death when the Prophet ﷺ was six and his later tears at her grave. His enduring love reminds us that spiritual strength does not erase sorrow.

Lessons to Carry With Us

* Knowing the Prophet ﷺ deepens our love for him. Seerah invites us to internalize his example and bring it into our daily lives.
* Caregiving deserves recognition. The women who nurtured him remain part of the story we tell and honor.
* Equality becomes meaningful through decisions. Who we trust, appoint, and welcome reveals the values we live by.
* A serious mistake need not define a whole life. Correction and opportunities for growth belong together.
* Grief has no fixed timeline. Tears can coexist with patience, faith, and trust in Allah.
* Sisterhood requires mutual care. We become a community when we begin helping one another.

Reflect With a Sister

1. Who has nurtured you beyond your immediate family? How might you honor her?
2. Where might assumptions about age, race, or social standing shape whom you trust or recognize?
3. How can you hold someone accountable while leaving room for growth?
4. What does the Prophet’s ﷺ expression of grief give you permission to feel?
5. What is one step you can take this month to help turn this gathering into a community?

“Grief has no timeline. Grief is not negated by piety or sabr or tawakkul. Tears are rahma, and we follow a man who cried.”

title: IPCI : Jesus in the Tanakh, IS THE CHRISTIAN CHRIST FOUND IN THE OLD TESTAMENT?
description:
Maulana Ismail Moosa (South Africa) faces Australian Reverend Samuel Green for the second time to unpack this fundamental question. IS THE CHRISTIAN CHRIST FOUND IN THE OLD TESTAMENT?

Christian View of Jesus in the Tanakh

Messianic Prophecies: Christians read the Tanakh as pointing forward to Jesus of Nazareth as the promised Messiah and Son of God. 
Passages like Isaiah 7:14 (the virgin birth), 
Isaiah 53 (the suffering servant), and 
Psalm 22 (details of the crucifixion) 
are interpreted as explicit previews of Jesus's life, death, and resurrection. The New Testament builds directly upon the Tanakh, viewing Jesus as the final and supreme word of God who fulfills the Law (Torah) and the Prophets (Nevi'im).

Islamic View of Jesus in the Tanakh

Islam views Jesus (Isa) as a Prophet, Messenger, and the Messiah (al-Masih) sent to the Children of Israel, rather than as God incarnate or the Son of God. Muslims respect the original revelations given to Moses (Taurat) and David (Zabur), which they believe originally pointed to pure Monotheism.
Islamic tradition holds that while the core message of past scriptures was divine, subsequent human interpretations or textual transmissions led Jews and Christians to misunderstand certain prophecies. Explore specific verses (such as Isaiah 7 or Psalm 110) to see how Christian and Islamic commentators interpret them differently?

Reverend Samuel Green—a Chemical Engineer and theologian—is no newcomer to interfaith dialogue. Having served as a campus evangelist and Islamic Engagement Director since 1999, as well as founding author of the Answering Islam website, he has debated almost every mainstream Muslim apologist over the last 15 years.

description:
An Israeli company tried to buy his AI startup. He refused. Now, he's taking on ChatGPT, OpenAI, Claude, and Big Tech.

At just 24 years old, Hani Chihabi and his brother built Thaura AI, an alternative to ChatGPT and other major artificial intelligence platforms. Within just two weeks of launching, they reached 100,000 users without spending a penny on advertising.

But what makes someone walk away from a successful career in tech to challenge some of the world's most powerful AI companies? And can we really trust the systems we're increasingly sharing our thoughts, questions, and personal information with?

Born in Syria and raised in Germany, Hani found himself working in the technology industry while watching the destruction unfolding in Palestine. Uncomfortable with the companies and systems he was helping support, he decided to leave his job and build something different.

In this episode of The Thinking Youth, Hani reveals how an Israeli company approached them about acquiring Thaura AI, why they refused to sell, and what it takes to compete against the biggest names in artificial intelligence.

The conversation comes at a particularly important moment for the future of AI.

In an October 19, 2026 interview, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke about the need for greater use of artificial intelligence to counter online narratives and campaigns he accused of influencing young Americans and Europeans against Israel. His remarks highlight a growing debate over the use of AI, bots, and digital platforms to influence public opinion.

As governments and technology giants increasingly recognize AI as a tool of political and economic power, who gets to decide what information we see, what AI systems are allowed to say, and how our conversations and personal data are handled?

With OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini, and Meta AI becoming increasingly influential, questions surrounding AI censorship, political bias, privacy, surveillance, and the ethics of artificial intelligence are more relevant than ever.

We discuss the darker side of ChatGPT and Big Tech, the politics of artificial intelligence, the risks of centralized AI infrastructure, and why Muslims need to move beyond simply using technology to building their own alternatives.

Hani also shares his remarkable personal journey: teaching himself to code in just seven months, building a company with his brother, reaching 100,000 users, and navigating the personal sacrifices that come with entrepreneurship.

Can we trust ChatGPT with the way we think? Who controls the AI systems shaping our understanding of the world? Can independent AI startups challenge Big Tech? And what would it take to build a genuinely ethical alternative?

title: The Screen and the Soul: Breaking Screen Addiction| Dr Francesca Bocca Aldaqre
description:
Is your screen helping you rest—or helping you escape?

In Lecture 4, **The Screen and the Soul**, we explore screen addiction through the Islamic understanding of the nafs (self), qalb (heart), rūḥ (soul), and the work of tazkiyah: purification and spiritual growth.

From endless scrolling to the phone we reach for without thinking, this lecture examines how digital habits shape our attention, relationships, parenting, and connection with Allah. It asks us to look beneath the habit: what discomfort are we trying to avoid, and what would actually nourish us?

The central teaching is practical: removing a habit needs to be accompanied by cultivating something better. Reclaiming our attention begins with meaningful alternatives—Qur’an, dhikr, du‘ā, family connection, time outdoors, service, and purposeful activity.

IN THIS LECTURE:
• Dopamine, anticipation, and the pull of unpredictable rewards  
• Four patterns of screen dependence across different stages of life  
• Ghaflah (heedlessness), lahw (distraction), and hawā (unchecked desire)  
• The difference between numbing ourselves and finding restorative rest  
• Why app limits and willpower can leave underlying needs unresolved  
• Practical replacements for scrolling in the morning, during the commute, while waiting, and before sleep  
• How our digital habits shape the example we set for our children  
• Rebuilding our capacity to contribute to family and community  

CHAPTERS  
00:00 — Opening: The screen, the soul, and the possibility of change  
10:15 — Why screens? Why now?  
22:15 — Four faces of screen addiction, one underlying pattern  
35:35 — Training the nafs and cultivating better habits  
48:20 — Two practical assignments and closing du‘ā  

THIS WEEK’S PRACTICE  
Choose one daily moment when you automatically reach for your phone. Replace it with one specific practice for seven days: a page of Qur’an, a few minutes of dhikr, a du‘ā, or meaningful connection with someone you love.

You can also plan a day from Fajr to Maghrib with your phone put away. Decide beforehand what will fill that time: a walk, a family meal, a visit, reading, or an act of service.

REFLECTION  
What is one phone habit you want to change—and what will you put in its place? Share your intention in the comments.

ABOUT THE SERIES  
This is the fourth lecture in a five-part series exploring the inner life through an Islamic framework.

Next lecture: **The Entitled Child and the Exhausted Parent**

Subscribe for the next lecture, and share this reminder with someone who wants to reclaim their attention and strengthen their connection with Allah.

May Allah awaken our hearts, guide our habits, and make us people of remembrance, presence, and beneficial action. Āmīn.
