title: The Great Hafiz of Hadith Sayyiduna Jabir ibn Abdillah Part 2 - Shaykh Riyadh ul Haq
description:
The Great Ḥāfiẓ of Ḥadīth Sayyidunā Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh Part 2 of 2
Delivered by Shaykh Riyadh ul Haq on Friday 17th May 2024 at Al Kawthar Academy, Leicester

FREE audio download: https://soundcloud.com/shaykhriyadhulhaq/great-hafiz-hadith-jabiribnabdillah-part2/

Part 1: https://youtu.be/pwL_9hm9uBQ

This second part deepens the portrayal of Sayyidunā Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh (ra) by focusing on his life of service, simplicity, and deep attachment to the Prophet ﷺ. Through numerous incidents - such as the fulfilment of the Prophet’s promise by Abū Bakr (ra), the Prophet’s personal care during illness, and the well-known miracle of feeding hundreds from a small meal - the talk shows how Jābir’s (ra) life was filled with barakah due to sincerity and devotion. His complete adherence to the Sunnah in even small matters, like eating simple food or walking in battles, reflects a life shaped entirely by imitation of the Prophet ﷺ. His participation in campaigns after Uhud and his eagerness to serve, despite hardship, further highlight his commitment and sincerity.

The talk then shifts into a powerful reflection on the nature of knowledge in Islam. It argues that true ʿilm is not mere information or speech, but a spiritual light embodied through humility, service, and character. Using examples from Jābir’s (ra) life and later scholars, the talk explains how knowledge is transmitted through companionship, respect for teachers, and personal transformation, forming a continuous chain back to the Prophet ﷺ.

The session concludes by warning against modern misunderstandings of knowledge as superficial learning, stressing instead that true scholarship requires immersion in a tradition of sincerity, discipline, and ethical refinement - qualities exemplified by Jābir (ra) and the early generations.

title: Habits That Drain Your Mental & Emotional Energy | Dr. Marwa Assar
description:
Habits That Drain Your Mental & Emotional Energy | Dr. Marwa Assar
Are you feeling mentally exhausted, emotionally drained, or overwhelmed by everyday life? Sometimes, the habits we repeat every day slowly take away our peace, confidence, and happiness without us even realizing it.

In this powerful motivational talk, Dr. Marwa Assar explores the habits that can drain your mental and emotional energy and shares important lessons about self-awareness, emotional strength, personal growth, and protecting your inner peace.

✨ IN THIS VIDEO, YOU WILL DISCOVER:

Habits that may leave you feeling mentally and emotionally exhausted

How overthinking can affect your peace of mind

Why constantly seeking approval can drain your confidence

The importance of setting healthy personal boundaries

How negative thinking can influence your daily life

Why comparing yourself to others can steal your happiness

How to stop giving unnecessary attention to negativity

Ways to protect your energy and develop a healthier mindset

How to prioritize yourself and focus on personal growth

🧠 PROTECT YOUR MENTAL AND EMOTIONAL ENERGY

You cannot control every situation or every person's behavior, but you can become more mindful of your habits, reactions, and choices. Learn to recognize what drains you, make room for what strengthens you, and focus on building a calmer, more balanced life.

Remember: protecting your peace is not selfish. It is an important part of living with self-respect, emotional awareness, and purpose.

If you enjoy motivational speeches, self-improvement, emotional intelligence, mental strength, and Islamic motivation, this video is for you.

title: Struggling to Concentrate in Salah? Try These Powerful Solutions | Ustadh Hisham Abu Yusuf #salah
description:
Do you stand for Salah, only to find your mind wandering somewhere else? Do you struggle to concentrate, remember what you are reciting, or feel that your heart is not fully present before Allah?

You are not alone in this struggle. Many Muslims experience distractions during Salah, but there are practical steps we can take to improve our focus and strengthen our connection with Allah.

In this reminder, we explore how to overcome distractions during Salah, develop greater khushu (humility and attentiveness), prepare our hearts before prayer, and learn to return our attention to Allah whenever our minds wander.

🌿 In this reminder, you will learn:

- Why distractions happen during Salah.
- Practical ways to improve concentration in prayer.
- How understanding what you recite can help your focus.
- How to prepare your heart before standing for Salah.
- Islamic guidance on fighting distractions and developing khushu.

Remember, do not let your struggle with concentration make you abandon the effort to improve. Keep turning to Allah, seek His help, and strive to make every Salah better than the last.

May Allah grant us khushu in our prayers and make Salah a source of peace, comfort, and closeness to Him. Ameen.

🤍 Subscribe to Jannah Seeds for more Islamic reminders, beneficial knowledge, and spiritual encouragement.

Share this reminder with someone who may benefit from it.

#Salah #Khushu #IslamicReminder #JannahSeeds #PrayerInIslam

title: The Story Of Imam Ibn Furak | Ustadh Yusuf Ash Shaybani
The Last Day You Will Ever See Me Like This. 1 Day Before Spinal Reconstruction Surgery.
description:
I wanted to write something thoughtful here, but my arms, hands, and fingers hurt too much.

Tomorrow morning, I’m having spinal reconstruction surgery. I filmed this on my way to my pre-surgery appointment.

I wish I had told you sooner how much pain I’ve been in. I wish I had let you in on this journey.

I’m letting you in now. I won’t be filming every moment, but I’ll speak to you when I can and share what I can through surgery and recovery.

Alhamdulillah for it all. May Allah accept my pain as a means of cleansing me of my sins in this life and preparing me for Jannah.

Please keep me in your duas.

The HSM TribeCast | Season 2, Episode 6

Society loves the comfort of a single label. We are often told to pick a lane, master a single craft, and remain predictable. But for the multi-hyphenate woman, this can feel less like mastery and more like a cage. 

In this episode, multimedia artist Haneefah Adam takes us into the psychology of the divergent mind. From her famous "Hijarbie" creation to food art and everything in between,, Haneefah shares how she seamlessly transitions between her massive talents while remaining deeply anchored in her faith.

इस वीडियो में हम जानेंगे हज़रत आदम अलैहिस्सलाम और हज़रत हव्वा अलैहस्सलाम के निकाह से जुड़ा वाक़िया, जन्नत में उनकी ज़िंदगी, शैतान के वसवसे और उस दरख़्त का क़िस्सा, जिसके फल से अल्लाह तआला ने उन्हें मना फ़रमाया था।

इस वाक़िये में हमें शैतान की चालों, अल्लाह तआला के हुक्म की अहमियत, तौबा और उसकी रहमत से जुड़ी कई अहम बातें सीखने को मिलती हैं। हज़रत आदम अलैहिस्सलाम की तौबा का ज़िक्र हमें यह भी याद दिलाता है कि इंसान को अपनी ख़ता पर नदामत के साथ अल्लाह तआला की तरफ़ रुजू करना चाहिए और उसकी रहमत से कभी मायूस नहीं होना चाहिए।

title: What Allah Withholds May Be His Mercy | The Names of Allah Class 25: Al-Mani | Shaykh Mikaeel Smith
description:
What if the things we fear most are actually the very things Allah is using to protect us and help us grow?

In this powerful reminder on the name of Allah, **Al-Mani’** — The Protector and Preventer — we reflect on fear, anxiety, confidence, addictions, unanswered duas, and the doors Allah sometimes keeps closed for our own good.

This talk explores what it truly means to trust Allah when life does not go the way we planned. From the story of Yusuf (AS) to our own struggles with fear, failure, and self-doubt, we are reminded that Allah’s wisdom can be present even in what we do not receive.

Class 25 of this series is a reminder that Allah’s protection is not always found in what He gives us. Sometimes, His greatest protection is in what He withholds.

Before there were castles, there were walls made from earth and wood.

Thousands of years before medieval knights defended massive stone castles, early communities were already developing ways to protect their homes and people. Earthworks, defensive ditches, wooden palisades, and naturally defensible hills became some of humanity’s earliest forms of fortification.

But how did these simple defenses eventually evolve into massive stone castles and powerful gunpowder fortresses?

This is Part 1 in the history of fortifications.

What should we cover next—the first ancient fortresses, Roman forts, or the rise of medieval castles?

title: How to Cope With the Loss of a Spouse
description:
How do you recover after losing a spouse while raising children on your own?

In this episode of "Ask Me Anything", I respond to a sister who asked for advice on navigating the loss of her husband and the challenges of single parenting.

Losing a spouse changes your life in ways that take time to process. There is no single way to grieve, and there is no fixed timeline for healing.

In this video, I share some of what helped me and some practical thoughts on moving through grief while continuing to show up for your children.

→ Giving yourself permission to grieve in your own way
→ Finding your own “grieving language”
→ Choosing gratitude for what you had rather than focusing only on what was lost
→ Understanding that grief can soften and change over time
→ Looking after your physical and spiritual wellbeing
→ Maintaining some routine and stability for your children
→ Leaning on family, friends and your community instead of trying to do everything alone
→ Making space for your own needs so you can continue to show up for your children

If you’re going through a loss, I hope this conversation reminds you that you don't have to have everything figured out right away. Healing takes time, and everybody’s journey looks different.

If you have experience of grief or single parenting, share the advice you wish someone had given you in the comments. Your words may help someone else in the community.

If you have a question you'd like me to answer in a future "Ask Me Anything" episode, you can submit it anonymously here:

Can Shaytan Use Your Good Deeds Against You? | Quranic Psychology | Dr Mohammad Akram Nadwi
description:
What if Shaytan’s greatest trick is not always to make you sin—but sometimes to encourage you to do good?

In this powerful extract from the Who Am I? – Diploma in Qur’anic Psychology (Tazkiyah al-Nafs), Shaykh Dr Mohammad Akram Nadwi explores a subtle danger in the spiritual life: even prayer, fasting, teaching, charity and other acts of worship can become corrupted when the heart develops the wrong intention.

Drawing on the classical Islamic tradition, he explains three ways an apparently good deed can be corrupted:

1. Wrong intention — seeking admiration, status or superiority rather than Allah.
2. Wrong method — performing an act in a way that departs from the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ.
3. Wrong goal — using an act of worship primarily to obtain a worldly outcome for which it was not prescribed.

A person may outwardly be doing something virtuous while pride, self-admiration, showing off or the desire for worldly recognition quietly enters the heart.

The lesson is profound: tazkiyah is not simply about avoiding sins. It is about continually examining the heart—even while doing good.

From the Who Am I? – Diploma in Qur’anic Psychology with Shaykh Dr Mohammad Akram Nadwi at Cambridge Islamic College.

title: Young Muslims, Bright Futures by Br Zakaria Ahmed
What Makes a Muslim Community Strong?
description:
What makes a Muslim community strong?

After spending the summer in Toronto and having the opportunity to speak to different Muslim communities, I found myself returning again and again to the same subject: love.

A community is only as strong as the individuals who make it up. And our real strength lies in each of us having his own personal, meaningful and loving relationship with Allah — a relationship that does not depend upon parents, teachers, organisations or anyone else.

This is especially important when raising our children. We don't merely want them to obey Allah because their parents are watching, or even simply out of fear or the desire for reward. We want them to worship Allah because they love Him.

And sometimes we discover the depth of that relationship in unexpected ways — even through hardship. If a tribulation strikes and the first thought that comes to your heart is, “Is Allah displeased with me?”, then notice something beautiful: the first One your heart turned to was Allah.

As I mention in the video:

“Is there a greater fear than losing the love of the one you love?”

Ultimately, strong families, strong communities and a strong Ummah begin in the same place:

Your own relationship with Allah.

It starts with you.

title: Surah al kahaf #friday motivation #quran #allah  #friday
description:
​Surah Al-Kahf: The Stories of the 4 Trials (Lessons & Spiritual Shield) 🛡️✨

​Why are we commanded to recite Surah Al-Kahf every Friday? Far from just a collection of ancient historical events, this extraordinary surah serves as our weekly shield, map, and spiritual compass. In this deep dive, we explore the four legendary trials of humanity described in Surah Al-Kahf—Faith, Wealth, Knowledge, and Power—and uncover the timeless wisdom we need to survive the greatest tests of this worldly life (and the tribulations of the end of times).

​In this video, we break down each story and the essential cures Allah gives us:

​🕒 Timestamps:

0:00 - Introduction: The Secrets of Surah Al-Kahf

1:15 - Trial 1: Faith — The People of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf)

Witness the inspiring story of the young believers who chose isolation over disobedience. Driven out of their homes by a tyrant king for refusing to worship idols, they took refuge in a massive cave. Allah put them to sleep for over 300 years, protecting their faith from a world that mocked everything they stood for. The Cure: Seek righteous companionship and place absolute trust in Allah.

​4:45 - Trial 2: Wealth — The Two Gardens

The cautionary tale of a man blessed with two sprawling, lush, and abundantly fruitful gardens. But as his pride grew, gratitude left his heart. He boasted of his superiority, looked down on others, and forgot the One who gave him everything—until he woke up to find his paradise turned to ashes. The Cure: Stay humble, recognize the true Giver, and practice gratitude.

​8:30 - Trial 3: Knowledge — Musa (AS) & Al-Khidr

Journey alongside Prophet Musa (AS) on his quest to learn from the wise servant Al-Khidr. Guided through seemingly inexplicable and tragic events—a damaged boat, a heartbreaking loss, and an unpaid repair—Musa learns that human understanding is strictly limited, and that Allah's divine wisdom operates far beyond our immediate perception. The Cure: Humility, patience, and trusting the unseen plan of Allah.

​12:15 - Trial 4: Power — Dhul-Qarnayn

Uncover the saga of the righteous, just, and unstoppable ruler Dhul-Qarnayn, who traveled to the ends of the earth. When a desperate people begged for protection from Gog and Magog (Yajuj and Majuj), he refused payment, gathered their labor, and erected an epic barrier of iron and copper. Instead of taking the credit, he proclaimed, "This is a mercy from my Lord." The Cure: Sincerity and using your influence, strength, and resources to serve others.

​✨ The Ultimate Shield: The Prophet ﷺ warned us that whoever memorizes the first ten verses of Surah Al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal (Anti-Christ). This is because the Dajjal will test humanity with these exact four trials.

​Watch, reflect, and share this reminder to bring the light of Surah Al-Kahf into your week!

​🔔 Don't forget to LIKE, SHARE, and SUBSCRIBE for more Islamic wisdom and reminders!

True happiness in the Qur'an and Islamic tradition is tied directly to knowing and purifying the soul (nafs), echoing the famous spiritual axiom often translated as, "He who knows himself knows his Lord". 

The Qur'anic Foundation of Success and Self-Purification
- The Path of Success: The Qur'an explicitly links ultimate well-being and prosperity to self-purification. As stated in Surah Ash-Shams, “Successful indeed is the one who purifies himself.” 
- The Inner State (Sa'adah): In the Qur'an, permanent felicity or happiness (sa'adah) is contrasted with wretchedness on the Day of Judgment, and it belongs to those who find eternal peace in Paradise through God's grace (Qur'an 11:108). 
- The Greatest Bliss: Material accumulations do not define true joy; rather, the ultimate fulfillment is attaining the divine pleasure of Allah. 

Self-Knowledge and Knowing the Creator
- The Axiom: The phrase "He who knows himself is truly happy" was famously highlighted by classical scholars like Imam al-Ghazali in The Alchemy of Happiness, building on the tradition "Man 'arafa nafsahu faqad 'arafa Rabbahu" (He who knows himself knows his Lord). 
- Recognizing Limitations: Scholars explain that acknowledging one's own created weakness, ignorance, and utter dependence leads a person to truly comprehend Allah's infinite strength, knowledge, and absolute glory. 
- Polishing the Heart: Self-knowledge requires stripping away the rust of ego, selfish desires, and earthly illusions so that the inner spiritual heart can reflect divine guidance.

This was a special gathering for the final recitation and completion of this great masterpiece of Imam Malik ibn Anas, followed by the granting of Ijazah with connected chains of transmission under the guidance of His Eminence, Shaykh Muhammad Al-Yaqoubi 

Studying the six major hadith collections with precision, paying attention to the exact wording, the names of the narrators, and the authenticity of the texts, is one of the most essential foundations for students of sacred knowledge. This is the very path that Shaykh al-Yaqoubi continues to uphold, following the way of the great hadith masters and pious scholars of the past.

BIOGRAPHY 

Shaykh Muhammad al-Yaqoubi, a descendent Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is a world-renowned Syrian scholar of Islamic jurisprudence, hadith, and theology. He is widely recognised as one of the most influential Muslim leaders in the world; with his speeches, classes, and books having impacted thousands of lives for the better.

A prolific writer and poet, his most recent books - ‘Shama’il of al-Habib al-Mustafa’ and ‘Introduction to Sahih al-Bukhari’ - are indispensable for Muslim learners. He has penned 60 poems, of over 5000 lines, in praise of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ - including the doubling (tashtir) of the famous Burdah and Hamziyya poems - which earned him the title of ‘the Busiri of this time’. 

In recognition of his work for building peace and harmony, and better understanding between all religious groups, Shaykh al-Yaqoubi received the International Award of Ambassador of Liberty and Peace in 2016.

For several years running, the Royal Aal al-Bayt has included him as one of the 500 most influential Muslims in the world, with the 2026 edition placing him 33rd.

His bestselling book, ‘Refuting ISIS’, has been published in 10 languages, including Arabic and English, and is widely heralded by critics. The book has played a significant role in the defeat of the ideology of Daesh and has been accredited with saving the lives of many youths, whilst helping people worldwide understand Islam’s position on this topical issue.

The Shaykh speaks 5 languages and has lectured in 35 countries.

title: Islamic Therapy, Trauma & Healing the Muslim Soul | Ayishah on The Mindful Muslim Podcast
description:
Can Islamic therapy help you truly heal?

In this episode of The Mindful Muslim Podcast, Sivan Kader is joined by Ayishah Swiecinska, Islamic psychologist, therapist and author of Islamically Inspired Self-Development, to explore the connection between mental health, spirituality and the Muslim healing journey.

Together, they discuss Islamic therapy, trauma, anxiety, OCD, spiritual bypassing, religious guilt, the importance of sincere nasiha, and why many Muslims feel misunderstood in mainstream therapeutic spaces. Ayishah also shares powerful case studies from her work, including stories of reverts, clients navigating abuse, perfectionism, spiritual confusion and the search for deeper healing through Qur’an, Sunnah and Islamic psychology.

Whether you are struggling with your own personal growth, supporting someone through their healing journey, or curious about faith-based therapy, this episode offers a heartfelt and thought-provoking look at what it means to heal the mind, heart and soul.

title: 3 Men Were Given Blessings. Only 1 Passed.
description:
In this video, Sheikh Muiz Bukhary journeys through this powerful authentic narration from Al-Bukhārī and Muslim and uncovers a dimension of the story that is frighteningly relevant to our lives today. 

Three men. Three extraordinary transformations. But only one of them understood what was really happening.

The Prophet ﷺ told us the remarkable story of three men from Banī Isrāʾīl: a man afflicted with a severe skin condition, a bald man, and a blind man.

Allah healed them.

Allah gave them wealth.

Allah multiplied what they had until each possessed an entire valley of livestock.

It sounds like the test was over.

But it had only just begun.

Because sometimes the greatest test is not what happens when Allah takes something away from you.

It is what happens to your heart after Allah gives you everything you once desperately wanted.

What happens when yesterday's miracle becomes today's normal?

What happens when the blessing you once begged Allah for becomes something you barely notice?

And if your past walked up to you today, would you even recognize it?

Perhaps the question is not simply whether Allah has blessed you.

The question is:

What have His blessings done to your heart?

وَمَا بِكُم مِّن نِّعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ

“Whatever blessing you have is from Allah.”
(Qur'an 16:53)


If this reminder benefits you, share it with someone who may need to hear it.

title: Bilkul
The Afterlife Manual — The 133-Page Book That Will Change How You See The World
description:
This time on The Ordinary Muslim I'm looking at The Afterlife Manual by Ousama Alshurafa. It's 133 pages.. You could literallyread it in a day or two. And it's built around a single argument that runs like a golden thread from the first page to the last.

I'm three quarters of the way through and I couldn't wait to talk about it — so this is a short summary rather than a full review. The deep dive is coming.

In this episode:
— Why I'm covering this book before finishing it
— Who Ousama Alshurafa is
— Life as a sorting system
— The eight obstacles, and why five are your family
— Why you're not seeing the world as it really is
 — Space, time, and the two things your mind does
— Nothing stands on its own two feet except Allah
— You are not your thoughts
— There has only ever been now
— Al-Asr: the oath sworn by the squeeze
— Uploads and downloads

About the author
Palestinian, from Gaza. Grew up in California, based in Toronto. An engineer by training with a Master's from Harvard, over twenty-five years in da'wah, and an ijaza in the Qur'an. He's clear that he doesn't consider himself a scholar — he describes himself as passing on what he was taught.

Where to get the book
The Afterlife Manual: Every Muslim's Guide to Happily Ever Hereafter is available on Amazon in paperback and Kindle. The author also makes a free PDF available on his website for anyone who genuinely can't afford a copy — no one should miss out on it over money.

He also runs a multi-part live series on his own YouTube channel where he reads the book chapter by chapter and answers questions as he goes. Well worth your time, and a lot of what's in this video came from watching it.

Previously on the channel
Episode 1 — Bidayat al-Hidayah by Imam al-Ghazali. Worth watching first if you haven't: Ghazali walks you to the edge of this life and stops. This book starts on the other side of that line.

If this was useful, subscribe — new episode every Friday, one classical or contemporary Islamic book at a time.

Wallahu a'lam.

title: Emergency Appeal: Help Women & Children - Reopen Shelter
description:
GIVE NOW https://gofund.me/d949a7721
Years ago, Khadijah Dawah & Community Services opened its doors through the mercy of Allah and the generosity of a widow who turned her late husband’s empty home into a refuge for women and children in need. It became a place of safety, warmth, and sisterhood — a home for those with nowhere else to go. A little over a year ago, tragedy struck when a fire forced everyone out. Alhamdulillah, with community support, the house was repaired and reopened. But just as the families began to settle back in, another disaster hit: the pipes burst, flooding the crawlspace and neighboring homes. The city had no choice but to shut off the water and close the shelter until repairs could be completed.We found a contractor ready to begin the work. Permits were pulled, and a $3,000 deposit was paid from what little funds remained. Families were moved again — some sleeping in cars, others crowded into a small apartment, and a few staying in a storeroom behind a storefront. So far, $1,500 has been raised, but $12,000 is urgently needed to finish the plumbing and reopen the shelter. Every dollar helps bring women and children back to safety.Every donation helps restore a home built on compassion and faith.

title: Ep 142 - Is Your Halal Meat Really Halal? | The UK’s First Halal & Tayib Farm
description:
What does halal truly require from us? Is it only about how an animal is slaughtered, or should it also include how that animal lived?

In this episode, Nadeem sits down with Khalil from Willowbrook Farm, the UK’s first Halal and Tayib farm, for a powerful conversation about food, farming, animal welfare, sustainability and our responsibility as Muslims toward the earth.

Khalil shares the remarkable Willowbrook story, beginning in 2002 when his parents left their careers, sold their home and committed themselves fully to building an ethical farm from empty land. The family faced years of opposition and planning difficulties, living in camouflaged caravans on their own land while raising thousands of chickens and working toward permission to build a permanent home.

The conversation explores why a halal stamp may tell us very little about the life an animal experienced. Khalil explains the difference between traditional chickens raised slowly over 12 weeks and commercial chickens produced in as little as four weeks, as well as the uncomfortable realities behind intensive, “free-range” and organic farming.

They also discuss:

• The difference between halal and Halal and Tayib
• Why cheap meat always carries a hidden cost
• Animal welfare before the moment of slaughter
• The problems with intensive and industrial farming
• Whether ethical farming can remain financially sustainable
• Foraging, mushrooms and reconnecting with nature
• Eating seasonally and using the whole animal
• Self-sufficiency and the limits of modern sustainable living
• Needs, wants and escaping consumer culture
• Repairing, reusing and delaying unnecessary purchases
• Islamic stewardship and our duty as caretakers of the earth
• Eco-camping, farm visits and activities at Willowbrook Farm

This is not simply a conversation about farming. It is an honest examination of the way we eat, consume and live, and whether our everyday choices reflect the values we claim to hold.

The goal is not perfection overnight. It is to become more conscious, eat less but eat better, ask where our food comes from and begin making small, meaningful changes.

Visit Willowbrook Farm:
https://willowbrookfarm.co.uk/

#Halal #EthicalFarming #SustainableLiving

description:
The Heart or the Brain? Where Does Consciousness Really Reside?

🎥 Presented in 4K with crystal-clear audio
👤 Delivered by Shaykh Zakareeya Baksh

Where does consciousness actually reside? Most people instinctively point to the brain—but is that the only possibility?

For centuries, Muslim scholars have discussed the relationship between the heart, the brain, and the human soul. Today, modern neuroscience and philosophy continue to wrestle with the very same mystery, known as the "hard problem of consciousness."

In this episode of Islam Explained, Shaykh Zakareeya Baksh explores what the Qur'an, Sunnah, and classical Islamic scholarship teach about consciousness. Discover the three major scholarly perspectives on the role of the heart and the brain, why the Qur'an repeatedly describes the heart as a place of understanding, and how these discussions intersect with modern scientific observations.

Rather than reducing the issue to a simple answer, this episode examines the evidence through the lens of revelation and the Islamic scholarly tradition, while engaging with one of the most profound questions in neuroscience and philosophy today.

title: How Should We Understand the Signs of Qiyamah? | Shaykh Akram Nadwi
description:
How should Muslims understand the signs of Qiyamah? Is it correct to interpret current events as fulfilments of end-time prophecies?

In this insightful talk, Shaykh Akram Nadwi explains why the Prophet ﷺ informed us about the signs of the Day of Judgement, and why we should avoid speculating about their fulfilment. Using examples from the Qur'an and Sunnah, he discusses the meaning of ta'wil, the wisdom behind the signs of the Hour, and why only Allah knows when the Hour will come.

Rather than encouraging predictions, these signs are meant to strengthen our faith, inspire us to prepare for the Hereafter, and give believers hope in Allah's promise.

Topics covered:
• Why the Prophet ﷺ spoke about the signs of Qiyamah
• Should we link current events to end-time prophecies?
• The meaning of ta'wil
• The wisdom behind the signs of the Day of Judgement
• Why only Allah knows when the Hour will come

Want to learn more?

Study this topic in depth with Shaykh Akram Nadwi's comprehensive two-day on-demand course, The Day of Judgement: Major & Minor Signs, available on Al-Salam Institute On-Demand:

title: A Believer's State Changes 40 Times in a Day - Shaykh Hamza Yusuf - Malayalam
You Were Taught The Qur’an Wrong
description:
Most Muslims were taught how to read the Qur’an.

Very few were taught how to understand it.

Think about it. Many Muslims spend years in madrasa learning the Arabic alphabet, tajwīd, and recitation. Some even memorise the entire Qur’an. Yet after all those years, many still struggle to explain the meaning of the verses they recite every day.

How did that happen?

In this video, I explore one of the biggest problems facing Muslims today: our relationship with the Qur’an. Have we reduced the Book of Allah to mere recitation while neglecting its meanings, lessons, commands, and guidance?

The Qur’an was not revealed simply to be recited beautifully. It was revealed to be understood, reflected upon, and acted upon.

title: Artistic Director of San Francisco Ballet Tamara Rojo on choreography, directing, and research
description:
What is it really like to leave a 27-year legacy in London to steer one of America’s most historic ballet companies? Three years after her bittersweet departure from the UK, the legendary Tamara Rojo sits down with acclaimed writer and critic Graham Watts for a captivating, wide-ranging conversation. Now fully settled as the Artistic Director of the San Francisco Ballet, Tamara opens up about the relentless pace of her tenure, the staggering structural differences between British and American arts funding, and how she managed to lead the company to a record-breaking $12 million Nutcracker box office. From her refreshing philosophy on respecting historical legacy (rather than letting ego rewrite it) to her pioneering efforts to bring thousands of young, diverse faces into the opera house, Tamara shines as a dynamic, deeply conviction-led force in the global dance community. She also shares fascinating insights into her 6-year PhD research on the psychology of elite dancers, her own celebrated choreography (Raymonda and Cinderella), and what it takes to leave an audience irrevocably changed.

Listen to discover:

Life in California: Tamara reflects on her first three years in San Francisco and what she misses most about the British sense of humour. [03:26]

US vs. UK Arts Funding: The massive shift from relying on a public funding safety net to navigating a system built entirely on box office and multi-generational donors. How a massive, record-breaking anonymous bequest gave her the creative freedom to bridge the old way of running the company with the new. [07:43]

Respecting Legacy Over Ego: Tamara explains her "evolutionary, not revolutionary" approach to leadership and her constructive relationship with predecessor Helgi Tomasson. [13:48]

Diversifying the Audience: Breaking down the perception barriers of ballet and activating the opera house with Mariachi bands, Flamenco, and local community art. [23:15] 

The Psychology of an Elite Dancer: Tamara reveals what she learned from her 6-year "rabbit hole" of PhD research on why some incredibly talented dancers thrive in the studio but struggle on stage. [35:43]

Directing Her Own Choreography: Re-editing Raymonda for American audiences and why her Cinderella has become a staple Christmas tradition in Sweden. [40:20] 

Reflecting on her ENB Legacy: Tamara looks back at her proudest moments at the English National Ballet, from championing female choreographers to securing their state-of-the-art new building. [45:19] 

Interview from the LBC In Conversation series. Recorded on 3rd December 2025.


The London Ballet Circle is a charity that offers informal talks with luminaries from the world of dance. We also organize visits to rehearsals and a range of other ballet-related activities. The money raised helps to support student dancers, ballet schools and companies across the UK.

Membership is open to all dance fans world-wide. Join the LBC to get free zoom links to our upcoming online talks.

description:
This lecture (Jumuah Bayan) was delivered in a Madina Masjid in Oxford UK on the Friday 30th of May 2026 by Shaikh Riyad Nadwi.

Please find below details of the supplication mentioned in the lecture:
حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مَعْمَرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ، حَدَّثَنَا الْحُسَيْنُ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ بُرَيْدَةَ، عَنْ بُشَيْرِ بْنِ كَعْبٍ الْعَدَوِيِّ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي شَدَّادُ بْنُ أَوْسٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ سَيِّدُ الاِسْتِغْفَارِ أَنْ تَقُولَ 

اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي، لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَىَّ وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لاَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ ‏"‏‏.‏ 

قَالَ ‏"‏ وَمَنْ قَالَهَا مِنَ النَّهَارِ مُوقِنًا بِهَا، فَمَاتَ مِنْ يَوْمِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُمْسِيَ، فَهُوَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ، وَمَنْ قَالَهَا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ وَهْوَ مُوقِنٌ بِهَا، فَمَاتَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصْبِحَ، فَهْوَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ ‏"‏‏.‏
Shaddad bin Aus r.a. narrated: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said "The most superior way of asking for forgiveness from Allah is: O Allah, You are my Lord, there is none worthy of worship except You. You have created me, and I am Your servant, and I am faithful to Your covenant and promise as much as I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your blessings upon me, and I admit my sins. So forgive me, for none forgives sins except You. The Prophet (ﷺ) added. "If somebody recites it during the day with firm faith in it, and dies on the same day before the evening, he will be from the people of Paradise; and if somebody recites it at night with firm faith in it, and dies before the morning, he will be from the people of Paradise." (Reported by Bukhari)

title: 03. Walking Purposefully Between Safa and Marwa: The Hidden Wisdom of Sa‘i
description:
Sa‘i between Ṣafā and Marwah is one of the most powerful journeys within Hajj — a journey that takes only minutes with our feet, but can transform a lifetime within our hearts.

In this video, Dr Shaykh Omer El‑Hamdoon explores the profound spiritual lessons hidden in the footsteps of Hājar (AS), whose courage, trust, and perseverance became immortalised in the rites of Hajj.

Sa‘i is not simply walking or running between two hills. It is a living reminder of a mother’s unwavering faith in Allah at a moment of complete vulnerability. When Hājar ran between Ṣafā and Marwah searching for water for her infant son Ismā‘īl, she embodied the essence of *tawakkul* — taking action with full trust in Allah’s mercy. Her story teaches us that even when we feel alone, unseen, or overwhelmed, Allah is closer than we imagine, preparing relief from places we could never expect.

What does Sa‘i teach us?
It teaches us that effort is not optional. That hope must be active. That trust in Allah is not passive waiting, but striving with the heart and limbs. Sa‘i reminds us that Allah sees every step, every tear, every moment of struggle — and that no sincere effort is ever wasted. The spring of Zamzam did not appear until Hājar had exhausted every possible means. Her perseverance became a symbol for all believers: *Do your part, and Allah will open doors you never knew existed.

In this reflection, Dr Shaykh Omer El‑Hamdoon unpacks the deeper meanings of Sa‘i, showing how this ritual mirrors the emotional and spiritual journeys we all face. Whether you are dealing with hardship, uncertainty, or a test that feels beyond your strength, Sa‘i teaches you how to walk through it with dignity, patience, and trust.

In this video, you will discover: 
• The story of Hājar and the divine wisdom behind her struggle  
• How Sa‘i represents the balance between effort and reliance on Allah  
• Why movement, even when tired, is a form of worship  
• How Sa‘i teaches resilience, hope, and emotional strength  
• The connection between Sa‘i and the believer’s daily challenges  
• Practical ways to apply the lessons of Sa‘i in your personal life  

Sa‘i also teaches us about perspective. From Ṣafā, the path looks long. From Marwah, the return feels tiring. Yet the believer keeps moving — not because the path is easy, but because Allah commanded it. Life mirrors this rhythm: moments of clarity followed by moments of confusion, moments of strength followed by moments of weakness. Sa‘i reminds us that faith is not about never feeling tired — it is about continuing the journey with sincerity.

Why this message matters today: 
In a world filled with anxiety, uncertainty, and constant pressure, the story of Hājar offers a timeless blueprint for spiritual resilience. Her Sa‘i was not just a physical act; it was a declaration of trust in Allah’s plan. Every believer today walks their own Sa‘i — between fear and hope, between difficulty and relief, between effort and surrender. Understanding this ritual can reshape how we face our own struggles.

*About the speaker:*
Dr Shaykh Omer El‑Hamdoon brings together classical Islamic teachings, spiritual reflection, and practical wisdom to help Muslims reconnect with the deeper meanings of worship. His calm, thoughtful style makes complex concepts accessible and spiritually uplifting.

If this video inspires you, please like, share, and subscribe for more reflections, reminders, and spiritually enriching content. May Allah accept the Sa‘i of every pilgrim, ease the struggles of every believer, and fill our hearts with the trust and perseverance of Hājar.  
**Ameen.**

title: 07 The Wajibat of Hajj Explained (Part 2) — Essential Fiqh Every Pilgrim Must Know
description:
Understanding the **Wājibāt of Hajj** is essential for every pilgrim who wants their Hajj to be valid, complete, and pleasing to Allah. While many Muslims know the basic rituals of Hajj, fewer understand the difference between the *arkān* (pillars) and the *wājibāt* (obligatory acts), and what happens if one of these obligations is missed. In this detailed and accessible lesson, **Dr Shaykh Omer El‑Hamdoon** explains the Wājibāt of Hajj in a clear, structured, and practical way, helping pilgrims prepare with confidence and clarity.

The Wājibāt are the actions that must be performed during Hajj, and although missing one does not invalidate the entire pilgrimage, it does require a compensatory sacrifice (*dam*). Knowing these rulings before travelling is not simply a matter of technical fiqh — it is part of fulfilling the trust of worship with excellence (*iḥsān*). When a pilgrim understands what Allah has obligated, they walk through the sacred journey with purpose, awareness, and tranquillity.

In this video, **Dr Shaykh Omer El‑Hamdoon** breaks down each Wājib in a way that is easy to follow, supported by evidence from the Sunnah and the understanding of the scholars. Whether you are a first‑time pilgrim or someone revising your knowledge, this lesson will give you the grounding you need to perform Hajj correctly and confidently.

**What you will learn in this video:**  
• The definition of Wājib in the context of Hajj  
• How Wājibāt differ from Arkān and Sunnah acts  
• The list of Wājibāt that every pilgrim must perform  
• The wisdom behind these obligations  
• What to do if a Wājib is missed  
• The rulings related to *dam* (compensatory sacrifice)  
• Practical tips to avoid common mistakes during Hajj  

This lesson is not only for those travelling this year. It is for anyone who wants to deepen their understanding of Islamic jurisprudence, appreciate the structure of Hajj, and recognise how every act — even the technical ones — carries spiritual meaning. The Wājibāt teach discipline, order, humility, and obedience. They remind us that worship is not only about emotion and inspiration, but also about following the guidance of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ with precision and devotion.

**Why this topic matters:**  
Many pilgrims enter Hajj with enthusiasm but without sufficient knowledge. This can lead to confusion, mistakes, or unnecessary hardship. By learning the Wājibāt, a pilgrim protects their worship, avoids doubt, and performs Hajj with a heart that is both sincere and informed. Knowledge brings peace, and clarity brings confidence.

**About the speaker:**  
Dr Shaykh Omer El‑Hamdoon is known for his balanced, clear, and practical approach to Islamic teaching. His ability to combine fiqh, spirituality, and real‑world application makes his lessons accessible to all levels of learners. In this series on the jurisprudence of Hajj, he guides viewers through the essential rulings with precision and warmth.

If this video benefits you, please like, share, and subscribe for more fiqh lessons, spiritual reflections, and educational content. May Allah accept the Hajj of every pilgrim, grant clarity to those preparing, and reward all who seek knowledge for His sake.  
**Ameen.**

title: New York City: Is NYC the Safest City for Muslims?
description:
Is New York City a safe haven or a unique challenge for Muslims in 2026? 🗽✨
From the ubiquitous "Halal Food" carts glowing on Times Square to the historic minarets of the Islamic Cultural Center of New York, Islam is visibly woven into the fabric of the world’s most iconic metropolis. With hundreds of thousands of Muslims calling the five boroughs home, NYC appears, on paper, as one of the most welcoming cities globally.

But is visibility synonymous with safety?

In this episode of The Global Muslim Experience, we look beyond the landmarks to explore the reality of life in Gotham. We navigate the bustling streets of Manhattan and the vibrant neighborhoods of the outer boroughs to answer a fundamental question: Is NYC the Safest City for Muslims?

We dive deep into:

The overwhelming accessibility of Halal dining and prayer spaces.

The resilience and strength of diverse communities across Queens and Brooklyn.

The raw reality of navigating the subway and streets as a visible religious minority.

Authentic, personal narratives from professionals, students, and families.

We compile the raw data and the real human stories to understand the dual existence of feeling completely at home while facing systemic challenges. Join us as we explore the definitive Global Muslim Experience in New York City.

description:

title: Piety Is Not Punishment | O You Who Believe Ep. 25 | Mustafa Briggs | Ramadan 2026
description:
"O you who believe, do not make unlawful the good things which Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress." (5:87)

Islam is not a religion of extremes.

Allah made beautiful things lawful for you.
Good food. Marriage. Rest. Enjoyment. Comfort.

And then He told you not to forbid them upon yourself.

Because there is a type of person who thinks the closer you get to Allah, the more you must suffer.
Who believes that denying yourself everything is the path to piety.

But that is not what Allah asked.

He asked for balance.
Enjoy what is good. Avoid what is harmful. Do not cross the limits.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) corrected the companions who wanted to pray all night, fast every day, and never marry. He told them that was not his way.

Piety is not punishment.
Worship is not deprivation.
And gratitude for what Allah made lawful is itself an act of faith.

Ramadan teaches us discipline, not denial.
We fast to appreciate, not to suffer.

Quranic Dua's for Forgiveness, Safety, Acceptance & Righteous Children | Part 1
description:
The Qur’an does not only guide us in belief — it teaches us how to speak to Allah.

In these powerful Qur’anic duʿas, we learn how the Prophets and the righteous asked Allah for forgiveness, safety, acceptance, and righteous generations.

These are not ordinary prayers.
They are words Allah Himself placed in the Qur’an so that we can call upon Him with them.

The first duʿa is the repentance of Adam عليه السلام:

رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَا أَنفُسَنَا وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْخَاسِرِينَ

“Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers.” (Qur’an 7:23)

This duʿa teaches us the essence of true repentance — no excuses, no blame, just honesty before Allah.

The second duʿa is the prayer of Ibrahim عليه السلام for safety and provision:

رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْ هَٰذَا بَلَدًا ءَامِنًا وَٱرْزُقْ أَهْلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ

“My Lord, make this a secure land and provide its people with fruits.” (Qur’an 2:126)

It reminds us to ask Allah not only for rizq, but also for security, peace, and stability in our homes and communities.

Then comes the beautiful duʿa of Ibrahim and Ismaʿil عليهما السلام while building the Kaʿbah:

رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّآ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

“Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.” (Qur’an 2:127)

Even while doing one of the greatest acts of worship in history, they still feared their deeds might not be accepted.

Finally, they made this powerful duʿa for their children and future generations:

رَبَّنَا وَٱجْعَلْنَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ لَكَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَآ أُمَّةً مُّسْلِمَةً لَّكَ

“Our Lord, make us submit to You and from our descendants a nation that will submit to You.” (Qur’an 2:128)

Through these duʿas we learn to ask Allah for:

• sincere repentance
• safety and barakah in our lives
• acceptance of our deeds
• righteous children and generations

May Allah make these duʿas alive in our hearts, accept our repentance, bless our homes, and raise from our families people who truly submit to Him.

Āmīn.

title: How to manage your emotions
description:
Are you feeling overwhelmed by anger, frustration, or sadness in your relationships or the world today? In this powerful talk, sister Haleh Banani explains how to transform destructive emotions into constructive actions using Islamic principles.
Drawing on 30 years of faith-based counseling, sister Haleh reminds us that emotions are not our enemies; they are vital pieces of information meant to guide us.
However, when we fail to regulate our emotions and simply react, we risk destroying our relationships and committing actions we may regret for decades.
By looking at the ultimate role model, Prophet Muhammad (2), we learn how to remain dignified, poised, and God-conscious even in the face of immense injustice, humiliation, and grief
sde, you will learn

 "Name it to Tame it": A psychological technique to move emotions out of the reactive amygdala and into the logical prefrontal cortex, instantly calming your nervous system.

The 3 Steps to Emotional Intelligence:
Moraqaba (Mindfulness/Self-awareness): Understanding your triggers, healing childhood wounds, and deactivating the things that make you react.

Mujahada (Internal Struggle): The daily striving to lower your gaze, control your tongue, and fight your ego (nafs) rather than succumbing to desires.

Muhasabah (Daily Self-Evaluation): Holding yourself accountable at the end of each day and following up any bad deeds (like snapping at your children) with good deeds.

The Heaviest Deed on the Scale: Why your character-especially how you treat your spouse, children, and parents behind closed doors-will weigh heavier than extra prayers or fasting on the Day of Judgment.

Avoiding the "Sewage Water": Why you should never lower your standards to match the negative energy of disrespectful or difficult people.

Taming the Nafs: How to take the "remote control" away from Shaytan and train your ego to become a partner that pushes you toward good deeds and Jannah.

Wisdom is a gift from Allah that does not automatically come with age, education, or even Islamic knowledge. Watch this video to learn how to actively seek that wisdom, break generational patterns of dysfunction, and build a peaceful home.

title: Deep Tadabbur on the Story of Um Musa (AS)
description:
What can the story of Umm Musa (the mother of Prophet Musa AS) teach us about tawakkul, worry, and trusting Allah’s plan?

In this Qur’an reflection lecture, we explore one of the most powerful moments in the Qur’an: when Allah inspired a mother with an impossible command...to place her baby in a river and trust in His promise.

Through deep tadabbur of selected verses in Surat Al-Qasas and Surat Taha, this lecture disects the verses, and uncovers timeless lessons on faith, fear, patience, and divine wisdom. Why did Allah test Umm Musa in this way? How evident was His mercy? How does Allah strengthen the human heart during uncertainty? And what does this story teach us about surrendering control while living in a world full of worry?

This session combines tafsir, spiritual reflection, and practical lessons to help us understand how the Qur’an speaks directly to our emotional and spiritual struggles today.

Topics covered:
 • The story of Um Musa in the Quran
 • Tawakkul (trust in Allah) explained through Qur’anic stories
 • Tadabbur: how to reflect deeply on the Qur’an
 • Allah’s promise and divine timing
 • Strengthening the heart through the Qur’an
 • Faith during hardship and uncertainty

title: 4 ноября 2026 г.
When Your Heart Feels Far From Allah, Listen to This
description:
Your mistakes do not mean you should give up on returning to Allah.

This Islamic reminder speaks to anyone carrying guilt, struggling with prayer, facing hardship, or feeling distant from their faith. Through sincere repentance, consistent worship, and better treatment of others, we can begin taking practical steps back towards Allah.

You do not have to wait until your life is perfect to begin. Protect your next prayer. Ask for forgiveness. Put right what you can. Start today.

This reminder covers:
• Returning to Allah after repeated mistakes
• Repentance and restoring other people’s rights
• Holding on to prayer during hardship
• Trusting Allah while taking practical action
• Overcoming comparison and practising gratitude
• Building consistent good deeds
• Bringing kindness into your family life

References:
Qur’an — Surah Az-Zumar, 39:53
Qur’an — Surah Ar-Ra’d, 13:28
Sahih al-Bukhari — 6464

This is an original, independently written Islamic reminder. It is not a recording or transcript of Mufti Menk or another scholar.

Share this reminder with someone who needs encouragement to return to Allah.

title: Witr, Explained Step by Step | The Prayer He Never Missed
description:
He never missed it. Not at home. Not on a journey. Not even on the back of his mount.

This is Witr, the prayer the Prophet Muhammad Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam ended every night with, explained step by step: what it is, when it is prayed, how many rak'ahs, exactly how to pray it, the Dua-e-Qunut, and what to say when it ends.

WITR IN SHORT
Time: after Isha, until Fajr. If you fear you will not wake at night, pray it before you sleep. If you rise in the last third of the night, make it your last prayer.
Rak'ahs: 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9. Begin with 1 if you are starting; 3 is his most common practice.
Three rak'ahs, two patterns: (1) pray 2, give salam, then pray 1 on its own; (2) pray 3 together with one sitting at the end.
Recitation: first rak'ah Surah Al-A'la, second Surah Al-Kafirun, third Surah Al-Ikhlas (after Al-Fatihah).
Dua-e-Qunut begins: "Allahummah-dini fi man hadayt..." (O Allah, guide me among those You have guided). The full dua is taught in the video. Its position differs by school: before the bowing (Hanafi, all year), or after rising from the bowing (Shafi'i, emphasised in the second half of Ramadan).
After the salam, three times: Subhanal-Malikil-Quddus (Glory be to the King, the Most Holy), raising the voice on the third.
Missed it? Pray it when you wake and when you remember.

REFERENCES
Three advices of Abu Hurairah (RA): Sahih al-Bukhari 1178, Sahih Muslim 721
Witr on the mount while travelling: Sahih al-Bukhari 1000, Sahih Muslim 700
"Allah is Witr and loves the Witr": Sahih Muslim 2677
Status of Witr (Ali RA): Sunan al-Tirmidhi 453. Note on grading: al-Tirmidhi graded this narration hasan; al-Hakim and al-Albani graded it sahih; Darussalam grading lists it as da'if. The two scholarly positions on Witr (strongly confirmed Sunnah / wajib) are presented in the video with their sources.
"Make Witr the last of your prayers at night": Sahih al-Bukhari 998, Sahih Muslim 751
Pray Witr early if you fear not waking: Sahih Muslim 755
Night prayer two by two, then one rak'ah: Sahih al-Bukhari 990, Sahih Muslim 749
Five, seven and nine rak'ahs (Aisha RA): Sahih Muslim 746
Surahs recited in Witr: Sunan Abi Dawud 1423
Qunut dua taught to Al-Hasan (RA): Sunan Abi Dawud 1425, Sunan al-Tirmidhi 464
Subhanal-Malikil-Quddus after Witr: Sunan Abi Dawud 1430, Sunan an-Nasa'i 1699
Dua after Witr: Sunan Abi Dawud 1427
Missed Witr prayed when remembered: Sunan Abi Dawud 1431

Surah Al-Waqiah is the 56th chapter of the Holy Quran and contains profound reminders about the Day of Judgment, the rewards awaiting the righteous, and Allah's limitless power. It encourages believers to strengthen their faith, remain grateful, and trust in Allah's provision.

Many people choose to recite Surah Al-Waqiah regularly as part of their personal worship and remembrance of Allah. title: Surah Al-Anfal | Quran in English — Chapter 8: The Spoils of War
description:
After the battle came another test: how would the believers handle victory?

Surah Al-Anfal — The Spoils of War — addresses the believing community in connection with the Battle of Badr. It turns attention from the spoils themselves to faith, obedience, reconciliation, and reliance upon Allah.

The chapter recalls fear, prayer, and divine help. It warns against disputes that weaken a community and against pride in moments of strength. It also addresses trusts, treaties, preparation for conflict, and responding to an inclination toward peace.

Listen to Surah Al-Anfal in English through the Saheeh International translation. This is Chapter 8 of our Quran in English series — one surah per video, in Qur’anic order.

🎧 LISTEN. UNDERSTAND. MEMORIZE.
Explore the whole Qur’an in the Joyful Muslims app — iPhone and Android:
👉 https://joyfulmuslims.com/yt
Qur’an listening has no cap.

IN THIS SURAH
• The spoils of war and reconciliation among believers
• The qualities of sincere faith
• The Battle of Badr and reliance upon Allah
• Steadfastness, obedience, and avoiding destructive disputes
• Honouring trusts and recognising the tests of wealth and family
• Treaties, conflict, and the possibility of peace
• The bonds between those who migrated and those who sheltered them

Listen with the setting of Badr in mind. Reflect on the responsibilities that come with both vulnerability and strength, and explore the chapter’s historical context through tafsir.

GO DEEPER IN THE APP
• Tafsir Ibn Kathir, verse by verse — explore the meaning and context of what you hear
• Memorization tools to help you learn and review at your own pace
• The whole Qur’an, with no listening cap
• Original Arabic beside the translation, line for line
• The classical audiobook library in clear English — a new book every Friday
• Five languages
• Offline listening, Apple Watch, Lock Screen

Free to start. Explore the audiobook library with 5 free hours every month. No card required.

👉 https://joyfulmuslims.com/yt

———
SURAH & TRANSLATION
Surah Al-Anfal (الأنفال) — The Spoils of War.
Chapter 8 of the Qur’an · 75 verses.

English translation: Saheeh International, published by Noor International.
Translation text sourced from QuranEnc.com:
https://quranenc.com/en

Captions retain the translation’s wording, including bracketed explanatory words. Footnote reference numbers and footnotes are omitted.

English narration uses Riko, a synthetic voice. Bracketed words are spoken without announcing the brackets, and Arabic names are pronounced in Arabic.

This video presents an English translation of the meanings of Surah Al-Anfal. The original Qur’anic text is Arabic. Verse-by-verse Tafsir Ibn Kathir is available separately in the app.

title: The 4 Women Who Rank Highest in Jannah — And Who Is First?
description:
Rasulullah صلى الله عليه وسلم once drew four lines on the ground and asked his Companions what they were. Then he named the four best women of the people of Paradise: خديجة بنت خويلد رضي الله عنها, فاطمة بنت محمد رضي الله عنها, مريم بنت عمران عليها السلام, and آسية بنت مزاحم رضي الله عنها, the wife of Pharaoh.

One lived in the house of Pharaoh. One was raised in the care of a prophet. One was his own wife. And one was his own daughter. But another authentic narration sets one of these four apart from the rest, so who is first?

In this video we follow their stories in the order they lived, using only the Qur'an, authentic hadith and the explanations of Sunni scholars. Anything that comes from later tafsir reports is clearly labelled in the narration.

If this video benefited you, subscribe to Iman Aldeen TV and tell us in the comments which of these four women stayed with you the most.

──────────────
REFERENCES

QUR'AN
• Surah Al-Qasas 28:7–9 (the infant Musa عليه السلام and the wife of Pharaoh)
• Surah At-Tahrim 66:11 (the prayer of the wife of Pharaoh)
• Surah Al Imran 3:35–38 (the vow of the wife of Imran and the provision in the sanctuary)
• Surah Al Imran 3:42 and 3:45 (the angels address مريم عليها السلام)

HADITH
• The four lines: Musnad Ahmad 2663, graded sahih by al-Albani (Sahih al-Jami' 1135); al-Mustadrak al-Hakim 3882, graded sahih al-isnad by al-Hakim
• "Sufficient for you among the women of the world...": Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3878, graded sahih by at-Tirmidhi
• "The best of her women was Maryam... the best of her women was Khadijah": Sahih al-Bukhari 3432
• "Many men reached perfection...": Sahih al-Bukhari 3769; Sahih Muslim 2431
• The first revelation and the words of Khadijah: Sahih al-Bukhari 3 and 4953
• Salam from her Lord and the house of qasab: Sahih al-Bukhari 3820
• The testimony of Aishah about Khadijah: Sahih al-Bukhari 6004; Sahih Muslim 2435–2436
• The secret told to Fatimah: Sahih al-Bukhari 3623–3624 and 6285–6286; Sahih Muslim 2450
• "...the leader of the women of Paradise, except Maryam bint Imran": Sahih Ibn Hibban 6952
• "Fatimah is the leader of the women of Paradise, except Maryam bint Imran": Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3768; Musnad Ahmad 11636, graded sahih by al-Albani (Sahih al-Jami' 3181)

TAFSIR AND SCHOLARS
• Tafsir Ibn Kathir on Al-Qasas 28:9
• Tafsir al-Baghawi on At-Tahrim 66:11 (reports of the pegs, the sun and the angels' shade, attributed to the mufassirun and to Salman al-Farisi; these are not established at the level of sahih hadith)
• Ibn Hajar, Fath al-Bari 6/448, on the virtues of Asiyah
• Ibn al-Qayyim, Bada'i al-Fawa'id 3/161, on comparing the virtue of these women
• IslamQA answers 23466 and 264320

And Allah سبحانه وتعالى knows best.

The Arbitration between Ali and Muawiya following the Battle of Siffin turned a near-victory for the Caliph into a catastrophic political disaster that permanently shattered his authority. Held at Dumat al-Jandal, the negotiations were designed to resolve the civil war through Quranic principles. Instead, they devolved into a trap of brilliant political manipulation. Ali’s representative, the pious but politically naïve Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, agreed to a proposal to depose both Ali and Muawiya to let the Muslim community choose a new leader. However, Muawiya’s shrewd negotiator, Amr ibn al-Aas, betrayed the pact. After Abu Musa publicly stepped Ali down, Amr stepped forward, refused to depose Muawiya, and instead declared him the rightful ruler. This deceptive manoeuvre completely delegitimised Ali's caliphate in the eyes of many, while instantly elevating Muawiya from a rebellious governor to a legitimate contender for the empire. Ultimately, this failed arbitration solved nothing. It triggered a violent mutiny among Ali's own fanatical soldiers—who formed the extremist Kharijite sect—and directly paved the way for the rise of the Umayyad Dynasty.

description:
Dajjal is called the greatest trial this world will ever face — but the Prophet Muhammad Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam did not leave us helpless before him. This video gives you the protection FIRST: four clear steps you can start tonight. Only then do we turn to the evidence — who Dajjal is, the man who already met him face to face, and how the greatest trial in history comes to an end.

How to protect yourself from Dajjal — the four steps:

Surah Al-Kahf — memorize the first ten verses
The dua after tashahhud — in every prayer
Know his description — before you ever see him
Hold fast — to the truth you already know

THE DUA (pray it after tashahhud, in every prayer)

Arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ، وَمِنْ عَذَابِ النَّارِ، وَمِنْ فِتْنَةِ الْمَحْيَا وَالْمَمَاتِ، وَمِنْ فِتْنَةِ الْمَسِيحِ الدَّجَّالِ

Transliteration: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min 'adhabil-qabr, wa min 'adhabin-nar, wa min fitnatil-mahya wal-mamat, wa min fitnatil-Masihid-Dajjal.
Translation: O Allah, I seek refuge with You from the punishment of the grave, and from the punishment of the Fire, and from the trials of life and death, and from the trial of the False Messiah, Dajjal.

REFERENCES (verify everything yourself)

Sahih Muslim 809 — the first ten verses of Surah Al-Kahf protect from Dajjal (Abu Darda, Radiyallahu Anhu)

Sahih al-Bukhari 1377 — the refuge dua after the final tashahhud (Abu Hurayrah, Radiyallahu Anhu)

Sahih Muslim 2937 — Nawwas ibn Sam'an (Radiyallahu Anhu): the description, the forty days, the young man, the descent of Isa (Alayhis Salam) at the white minaret of Damascus, the end at the gate of Ludd
Sahih Muslim 2942 — Tamim al-Dari (Radiyallahu Anhu), narrated by Fatimah bint Qays (Radiyallahu Anha): Al-Jassasah, the chained man, Baysan, Tabariyyah, Zughar, and the two cities he can never enter

title: माशाल्लाह जमीयत के प्रोग्राममें शामिल हुए हरियाणा मेवात new# viral # short video #
The Mysterious Death of Maryam (AS) — What Islam Really Says
description:
How did Maryam (مريم عليها السلام), the mother of Prophet Isa (عيسى عليه السلام), die? And what did the Angel of Death say to her? Millions have heard a moving story about her final moments. But where does it actually come from?

In this video we go through her life as the Qur’an tells it:

her mother’s promise before she was born;
the provision she received in the mihrab;
the angels who told her she was chosen above all the women of the world;
the day beneath the palm tree;
the baby who spoke to defend her.

Then we look at what happened after her son was raised. We cover the later historical reports about her final years, the famous conversation with the Angel of Death, and what the scholars of hadith said about them. Finally, we look at what the authentic Sunnah tells us is said to a believing soul at the moment of death.

Throughout the video, we separate what is established in the Qur’an and authentic Sunnah from later reports, so you know exactly what is confirmed and what is not.

⏱️ Chapters
00:00 Introduction
00:53 A Promise Made Before She Was Born
04:00 Chosen Above All the Women of the World
07:07 The Day She Wished She Had Died
09:44 The Child Who Spoke for His Mother
12:31 A Sign for the Worlds, and Then Silence
15:25 What Later Historians Reported
18:32 The Conversation Millions Have Heard
21:39 “O Good Soul”

📖 References

Qur’an (translations from quran.com):

Aal ‘Imran 3:35–37 (her mother’s vow, her birth, Zakariyya عليه السلام): https://quran.com/3/35
Aal ‘Imran 3:42–44 (chosen above the women of the world): https://quran.com/al-i-imran/42-44
Aal ‘Imran 3:42–52 (the good tidings and the mission of Isa عليه السلام): https://legacy.quran.com/3/42-52
Maryam 19:16–22 (Jibril عليه السلام appears to her): https://quran.com/19:22
Maryam 19:22–28 (the palm tree and the return to her people): https://legacy.quran.com/19/22-28
Maryam 19:29–34 (the child speaks in the cradle): https://legacy.quran.com/19/29-34
Al-Mu’minun 23:50 (a sign, and refuge on high ground): https://quran.com/muminun/50
An-Nisa 4:158 (raised to Allah): https://quran.com/4/158
Al-Ma’idah 5:75 (a woman of truth; they both ate food): https://quran.com/5/75
As-Sajdah 32:11 (the Angel of Death): https://quran.com/32:11

Hadith:

Every child is touched by Shaytan except Maryam and her son (Sahih al-Bukhari 3431 & 4548): https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4548
The hadith of al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib on the death of the believer (Musnad Ahmad, via Mishkat al-Masabih 1630): https://sunnah.com/mishkat:1630
– Graded sahih: https://dorar.net/h/LWGDraqk
The best women of Paradise (graded sahih):
– https://dorar.net/h/g007CnW8
– https://dorar.net/h/QpDH4tUA

On 19:16–23: https://quran.com/19/16/tafsirs

On 5:75: https://quran.com/5/75/tafsirs

Scholarly rulings:

Is the Angel of Death’s name Azrael? (IslamQA): https://islamqa.info/en/answers/40671
No authentic evidence for the name Azrael (Islamweb): https://www.islamweb.net/en/fatwa/312115/

description:
Look at the world around you. What do its signs reveal about the One who created it?

Surah Al-An‘am — The Cattle — calls the listener to reflect on the heavens, the earth, life, and death. It challenges the worship of anything besides Allah and questions the inherited beliefs people follow without knowledge.

Through Abraham’s rejection of false objects of worship and the accounts of earlier messengers, the chapter turns attention toward the Creator. It also confronts invented religious restrictions and sets out commands concerning parents, children, property, honesty, and justice.

Listen to Surah Al-An‘am in English through the Saheeh International translation. This is Chapter 6 of our Quran in English series — one surah per video, in Qur’anic order.

🎧 LISTEN. UNDERSTAND. MEMORIZE.
Explore the whole Qur’an in the Joyful Muslims app — iPhone and Android:
👉 https://joyfulmuslims.com/yt
Qur’an listening has no cap.

IN THIS SURAH
• Allah’s oneness and the signs of His power in creation
• Revelation, resurrection, and accountability
• Abraham’s rejection of false worship
• The messengers and their shared call to guidance
• Invented restrictions concerning food and livestock
• Kindness to parents, protection of life, and care for orphans
• Honest measures, just speech, and following the straight path

Listen in sections. Reflect on the signs described and the beliefs we inherit. Return to the closing commands and consider how they shape everyday conduct.

Surah Al-Waqiah is the 56th chapter of the Holy Quran and contains profound reminders about the Day of Judgment, the rewards awaiting the righteous, and Allah's limitless power. It encourages believers to strengthen their faith, remain grateful, and trust in Allah's provision.

Many people choose to recite Surah Al-Waqiah regularly as part of their personal worship and remembrance of Allah. While there are narrations often mentioned regarding its virtues, Muslims should always rely on authentic Islamic teachings and remember that all blessings, provision, and success come only from Allah سبحانه وتعالى.

The Leper, the Bald & the Blind: The Angel Returned in Disguise — Only One Passed
description:
Three men from the Children of Israel: a leper, a bald man, and a blind man. Allah سبحانه وتعالى sent an angel to each of them, and each was given exactly what he asked for. Years of blessing turned into valleys full of camels, cows, and sheep. Then the angel came back in another form, asking for something very small, and only one of the three gave the answer that pleased Allah سبحانه وتعالى.

This is one of the stories told by the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم himself, preserved in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. In this documentary we follow it word by word, with no invented names, places, or endings, only what the authentic narration tells us.

Subscribe to Iman Aldeen TV and turn on notifications for more stories from the Qur'an and the authentic Sunnah.


⏱ CHAPTERS
00:00 Three Men, One Test
00:42 Three Men the People Turned Away From
02:44 The Question at the Leper's Door
04:42 Hair, Sight, and a Single Sheep
06:45 When the Valleys Filled
08:48 The Traveller Who Asked for One Camel
11:00 The Third Man's Answer
13:03 "Keep Your Wealth"
15:01 The Valley in Every Life

📖 REFERENCES

Hadith

description:
Keep your promises. Stand for justice. Do not let hatred lead you to act unfairly.

Surah Al-Ma’idah — The Table Spread — opens with a command to fulfil obligations. It connects faith with the choices of daily life: what we eat, how we prepare for prayer, how we honour agreements, and how we treat others.

The chapter recounts Moses and his people, the two sons of Adam, and the disciples of Jesus asking for a table spread from heaven. Through these accounts, it calls the listener to reflect on obedience, the gravity of taking a life, gratitude, and accountability before Allah.

Its closing passage turns to Jesus, peace be upon him, and his testimony before Allah — bringing the chapter’s questions of worship, truthfulness, and responsibility into sharp focus.

I Studied 100+ of Pakistan's Most Driven People - 8 Habits They All Share
description:
What makes driven people driven? After sitting down with 100+ of Pakistan's most driven creators, founders and scholars, I noticed the same patterns again and again. Here are the 8 habits they all share.

پاکستان کے 100 سے زیادہ کامیاب لوگوں سے گفتگو کے بعد، وہ 8 عادتیں جو ان سب میں مشترک ہیں۔ کامیابی کا راز: کیا کرنا ہے نہیں، بلکہ کیا نہیں کرنا۔

Much of success isn't in what you have to do. It's in what you must NOT do.

Like Napoleon Hill did for Think and Grow Rich, I started taking notes on what the most driven people around me think and do. The first 4 habits come straight from my podcast guests, on camera and off. The last 4 come from the books, podcasts and conversations that followed.

⏱️ CHAPTERS
0:00 Nobody thinks about you for more than 2 minutes
0:17 What I learned from 100+ driven people
1:30 The Napoleon Hill approach
2:42 The 8-point structure
3:38 #1 Identity: your inner dialogue
5:26 #2 Silent discipline: stop announcing your goals
7:36 #3 Fear is the enemy ("log kya kahenge")
9:33 Seeing opportunity in adversity
10:22 #4 Take things into your own hands: just do it
11:48 The next 4 habits
12:42 #5 Success is in what you DON'T do
14:20 #6 Words are power
16:51 #7 Generosity: give before you ask
18:41 #8 It's all a game of energy
21:05 Final thoughts

📌 THE 8 HABITS OF DRIVEN PEOPLE
1. Identity: how you talk to yourself decides who you become
2. Silent discipline: do the reps when no one is watching
3. Fear is the enemy: rejection is part of the process, not the verdict
4. Take control: the most important word in "just do it" is "just"
5. What NOT to do matters more than what to do
6. Words are power: self-talk inside, communication outside
7. Generosity: give your time, advice and a smile without expecting anything back
8. It's all a game of energy: where your attention goes, your reality follows

💬 This is a work in progress, not a finished article. Do you agree? Disagree? Tell me in the comments. Your comments help me refine these ideas.

title: Zakir Naik Faces a Challenge Over the Divinity of Jesus
description:
Is Jesus God, or is he a messenger of God? 
This is the central question in this intense exchange between Dr. Zakir Naik and a Christian woman who firmly believes that Jesus is God.

Facing the renowned Muslim preacher, she defends her belief with determination. But Dr. Zakir Naik presents a direct challenge: can she identify an unequivocal statement in the Bible where Jesus himself says, “I am God” or “Worship me”?

To support her position, she refers to the famous passage in John 1:1, the expression “the Word of God,” and the extraordinary miracles performed by Jesus. Dr. Zakir Naik examines her arguments and repeatedly brings the discussion back to one central question: **What did Jesus actually say about himself?**

As the debate unfolds, consider a fundamental question: do the miracles of Jesus prove that he is God, or do they demonstrate the power of the One who granted him those miracles?

In Islam, Jesus (Issa, peace be upon him) is the Messiah and a noble prophet and messenger of Allah. Muslims believe in his miraculous birth and the extraordinary signs he performed, while maintaining that these miracles demonstrate God's power rather than make Jesus the Creator.

Watch this debate and examine the arguments surrounding one of the most important theological questions shared by Muslims and Christians.

title: The King Who Heard of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) Centuries Before His Birth
description:
Centuries before Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم was born, a king of Yemen marched his army to Yathrib, then turned away after two rabbis told him a prophet of the final age would one day migrate there. Later accounts say he wrote a letter to that prophet, passed down for generations until it was read to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم himself. But how much of this famous story is actually true?

In this video we follow the journey of تُبَّع, the king of حِمْيَر: the town that fought him by day and fed him by night, the Kaaba he planned to destroy and ended up clothing, the verses he left behind in Yathrib, and the house of أبو أيوب الأنصاري رضي الله عنه where the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم stayed. Most importantly, we look at what the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم himself said about this king in authentic hadith.

Throughout the video, we separate what is established in the Qur’an and authentic Sunnah from what comes from tafsir reports and later retellings, including the famous “thousand years.”

📌 Chapters
00:00 The king, the letter and the question
00:52 A Title Carried by Kings
04:01 Fought by Day, Fed by Night
07:02 The House Built by إبراهيم عليه السلام
10:11 Words Left in Yathrib
13:06 After the King Was Gone
16:14 A City That Was Waiting
19:16 The House of أبو أيوب الأنصاري رضي الله عنه
22:37 His People Were Blamed, He Was Not
📖 References

Qur’an
Surah Qaf 50:14: https://quran.com/50/14
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:89: https://quran.com/2/89
Surah Ad-Dukhan 44:37: https://quran.com/44/37

Hadith
Sunan Abi Dawud 4674 (“I do not know whether Tubba’ was accursed or not”), graded sahih by al-Albani: https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4674
Musnad Ahmad, from سهل بن سعد رضي الله عنه (“Do not curse Tubba’, for he had accepted Islam”), graded sahih by al-Albani in Sahih al-Jami’ 7319: https://dorar.net/h/KATvAq05
Sahih Muslim 2053c, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم staying in the house of أبو أيوب الأنصاري رضي الله عنه: https://sunnah.com/muslim:2053c
The narration “first to clothe the House” (weak, contains al-Waqidi): https://dorar.net/h/Bqo5pCUf

Tafsir and scholarly explanations
Tafsir ابن كثير رحمه الله on Ad-Dukhan 44:37: https://quran.com/ad-dukhan/37/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir
IslamQA 131521, “Who were the people of Tubba’?”: https://islamqa.info/ar/answers/131521
Islamweb Fatwa 59075, “The story of Tubba’ and his people”: https://www.islamweb.net/ar/fatwa/59075/
Tafsir الألوسي رحمه الله on Ad-Dukhan 44:37 (the later report of the letter): https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/index.php?page=bookcontents&ID=4358&flag=1&bk_no=201&surano=44&ayano=37

Accounts of the letter, the house built for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and the “thousand years” come from later reports and are not established in the Qur’an or authentic Sunnah. Allah سبحانه وتعالى knows best.

title: Surah An-Nisa | Quran in English — Chapter 4: The Women
description:
Justice begins with those whose rights are easiest to overlook.

Surah An-Nisa — The Women — opens by reminding humanity of its shared origin. It then turns to the responsibilities that bind people together: caring for orphans, protecting property, honouring marriage, and distributing inheritance.

The chapter calls believers to uphold justice even when it goes against themselves or those closest to them. It addresses family life, the treatment of women, care for neighbours and those in need, and the duty to stand with the oppressed.

Alongside these responsibilities, it examines sincerity and hypocrisy, obedience and accountability, and belief in Allah’s messengers.

Listen to Surah An-Nisa in English through the Saheeh International translation. This is Chapter 4 of our Quran in English series — one surah per video, in Qur’anic order.

🎧 LISTEN. UNDERSTAND. MEMORIZE.
Explore the whole Qur’an in the Joyful Muslims app — iPhone and Android:
👉 https://joyfulmuslims.com/yt
Qur’an listening has no cap.

IN THIS SURAH
• Humanity’s shared origin and the ties of kinship
• Protecting orphans and safeguarding their property
• Marriage, family responsibilities, and inheritance
• Kindness to parents, relatives, neighbours, and those in need
• Honouring trusts and judging fairly
• Standing firmly for justice, even against personal interests
• The oppressed, the responsibilities of believers, and the danger of hypocrisy
• Revelation and belief in Allah’s messengers

Listen in sections and reflect on the responsibilities described. Return to the verses you want to understand more deeply, and explore their context through tafsir.
