title: "Health BENEFITS of Pumpkin: 7 AMAZING Reasons to Eat It"
description:
Try incorporating pumpkin into your diet—it offers numerous benefits, such as:
1. Maintaining skin health and supporting collagen production. Its beta-carotene and vitamin C content promote healthy skin, with vitamin C also being essential for collagen synthesis. 2. Helping to prevent premature aging. The antioxidants in pumpkin help protect cells from damage caused by free radicals (though they are not proven to directly eliminate wrinkles).
3. Supporting eye health. The body converts beta-carotene into vitamin A, which is vital for vision. 4. Boosting the immune system. Vitamins A and C play a key role in maintaining immune function. 5. Aiding digestion. Its fiber content helps promote regular bowel movements, especially when consumed whole or blended without being strained. 6. Supporting heart health. Pumpkin contains potassium, which helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle function. 7. Assisting with weight management. Pumpkin is relatively low in calories and contains water and fiber, which help you feel full.

title: Prophet Muhammad Violated Qur'an during the Hajj
description:
Prophet Muhammad violated the Qura'nic rule of not to have sex with women when in ihram (purity state spent inside a mosque) or when performing Hajj

Q2.197
YUSUFALI: For Hajj are the months well known. If any one undertakes that duty therein, Let there be no obscenity, nor wickedness, nor wrangling in the Hajj. And whatever good ye do, (be sure) Allah knoweth it. And take a provision (With you) for the journey, but the best of provisions is right conduct. So fear Me, o ye that are wise.

Even a hadis in Sunaan Abu Dawud 1837 confirms the stipulation of the Qur'an. https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1837
A pilgrim must not marry and give someone in marriage in the sacred state (while wearing ihram)…

But Prophet Muhammad did not have much regard for the Qur'an or even to his own words when it came to marrying women and having sex with them. So, when he went to Mecca, to perform the Hajj, and a proposal of marriage was offered to him, he quickly accepted the offer and married the woman even though he was in sacred state wearing irham.

Sunaan Abu Dawud: vol.ii, Book 10, Number 1840:
Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Prophet (may peace be upon him) married Maimunah while he was in the sacred state (wearing ihram).

https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4258
Sahih al-Bukhari 4258
Narrated By Ibn Abbas : The Prophet married Maimuna while he was in the state of lhram but he consummated that marriage after finishing that state. 
Maimuna died at Saraf (i.e. a place near Mecca). Ibn ‘Abbas added, The Prophet married Maimuna during the ‘Umrat-al-Qada’ (i.e. the ‘Umra performed in lieu of the ‘Umra which the Prophet could not perform because the pagans, prevented him to perform that ‘Umra).

https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4259
Sahih al-Bukhari 4259

title: The Believer Who Will Walk Out of Madinah to Face Dajjal
description:
On the salt flats just outside Madinah, الدجال will set up camp, unable to enter a city guarded by angels at every pass. On that day one believer will come out to face him. In front of everyone he will be killed and then, as a trial Allah سبحانه وتعالى permits, made to stand again. What he says next, and why الدجال can never touch him a second time, is recorded in both Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.

Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم described this man as the greatest of people in martyrdom in the sight of the Lord of the worlds.

In this video, told only from the Qur’an and authentic Sunnah:

The warning every prophet gave about الدجال
His forty days on earth and the trial of rain, herds and treasures
Why Makkah and Madinah are sealed against him
The believer’s words to الدجال's guards: “There is nothing hidden about our Lord”
What the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم taught us to protect ourselves today
How الدجال's story finally ends at the hands of عيسى عليه السلام

Chapters
00:00 The believer who will face Dajjal
01:10 Among the palm trees
04:05 Forty days
06:55 The city he cannot enter
09:45 The man who comes out
12:50 Stopped before he reached him
15:45 In front of everyone
18:45 More certain than ever
21:40 What he carried with him

References

Qur’an

Surah Ibrahim 14:27 – https://quran.com/ibrahim/27

Hadith

Sahih al-Bukhari 7132: the believer who faces الدجال near Madinah – https://sunnah.com/bukhari:7132
Sahih Muslim 2938a: the same account, with أبو إسحاق's later remark on the man’s identity – https://sunnah.com/muslim:2938a

title: The Last Man Out of the Fire — The Moment Allah swt Laughed
description:
The Last Man Out of the Fire: The Moment Allah سبحانه وتعالى Laughed

When the judgment of all creation is finished, one man will still remain between Paradise and the Fire, with his face toward the Fire. He promises his Lord he will ask for nothing more, and then he asks again, until Allah سبحانه وتعالى laughs.

This is not a legend or a later tale. It is recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, and in this documentary we follow it step by step: the question the companions asked about seeing their Lord, the bridge over Jahannam, the one mark the Fire is forbidden to touch, the man between Paradise and the Fire, the three trees, and the moment THE PROPHET صلى الله عليه وسلم laughed as he told it.

Every scene in this video is taken from authentic hadith. No dialogue, names or details have been added.

What does it mean to live by faith — in worship, in hardship, and in the choices no one else sees?

Surah Al-Baqarah — The Cow — moves from belief in the unseen to the responsibilities of everyday life. Through accounts of Adam, Moses, Abraham, and the Children of Israel, it calls the listener to reflect on guidance, obedience, and the consequences of turning away.

The Qur’an’s longest surah brings together prayer, fasting, charity, pilgrimage, family life, and fairness in financial dealings. It includes Ayat al-Kursi and closes with a prayer for forgiveness, mercy, and help.

title: People think hijab is just a Muslim thing…☝️
description:
Many people associate women's head coverings exclusively with Islam, but did you know that some Christian churches also require women to cover their hair?

During a visit to a church in Georgia, this man discovers a sign instructing women to wear head coverings before entering.

Head coverings have a long history in Christianity, Judaism, and Islam. While the practices and religious teachings differ, modest dress is not unique to Muslims.
Even the Bible discusses women covering their heads during worship in 1 Corinthians 11:5–6.

A reminder that our religious traditions may have more in common than we realize.

title: Why You Can't Stop Thinking About Them | A Letter to the Heart That Won't Let Go
description:
A letter to the heart that won't let go.

You didn't choose this the way people think you did. Nobody sits down one day and decides to hand their whole peace to one human being. It happened slowly — a conversation, a kindness, a moment that stayed longer than it should have.

In this letter: the young man who stood behind closed doors in Egypt and what he did with what he felt (Surah Yusuf), what your heart is actually looking for, and one dua to carry with you — the dua of the love of Allah.

References:
• The Holy Qur'an — Surah Yusuf, 12:23-24 and 12:33
• The Holy Qur'an — Surah Ar-Rum, 30:21
• Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3490 (graded Hasan) — the dua of the love of Allah, narrated from Abu ad-Darda' (RA); the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said it was from the supplication of Dawud (AS)

This video is a reminder, not a fatwa. For personal religious rulings, please consult qualified scholars.

If this letter found you at the right time, pass it to one heart that is still awake tonight.

title: Lorsque le dépôt confié sera trahi, attends-toi à l'arrivée de l'Heure.
description:
Que signifie réellement la trahison du dépôt confié (al-Amânah) ?

Le Prophète ﷺ a dit : « Lorsque le dépôt confié sera négligé, attends-toi à l'arrivée de l'Heure. » On lui demanda : « Comment sera-t-il négligé ? » Il répondit : « Lorsque les responsabilités seront confiées à ceux qui n'en sont pas dignes, attends-toi à l'arrivée de l'Heure. » (Rapporté par Al-Bukhârî).

Dans l'Islam, la notion de dépôt (Amânah) englobe chaque devoir dont nous devons nous acquitter : les responsabilités publiques, mais aussi l'éducation de nos enfants, pour laquelle nous aurons des comptes à rendre devant Allah ﷻ.

title: Angels vs. Shaytans: What Animals Perceive That You Can't
description:
You Will Be amazed Why a Donkey Sees Shaytans and a Rooster Sees Angels

Before Fajr, a rooster crows and a donkey brays — and the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم told us that neither sound is empty. In this video we go through the authentic hadith recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, what these animals see that we cannot, why the rooster is honoured, why the donkey's bray is a warning, what the animals hear coming from the graves, and why every creature waits on Friday morning. Every hadith and verse in this video is taken from the Qur'an and authentic Sunnah.


⏱ CHAPTERS
00:00 Two sounds in the dark
01:09 Every creature has a voice
03:46 Two sounds, two commands
06:04 Seen from where you cannot see
08:26 The rooster that wakes the believers
10:41 When Shaytan runs from the adhan
13:14 A sound from beneath the earth
16:01 Every Friday before sunrise
18:27 Why them, and not us?

📖 QUR'AN
- Surah Al-Isra 17:44 — everything glorifies Allah سبحانه وتعالى
https://quran.com/17/44
- Surah An-Naml 27:18–19 — the ant and Sulayman عليه السلام
https://quran.com/27/18-19
- Surah Al-A'raf 7:27 — Shaytan sees you from where you do not see him
https://quran.com/7/27

📚 HADITH
- The rooster sees an angel, the donkey sees a shaytan — Sahih al-Bukhari 3303
https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3303
- Same hadith — Sahih Muslim 2729
https://sunnah.com/muslim:2729
- Same hadith, with "the accursed" — Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3459 (graded hasan sahih by at-Tirmidhi)
https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3459
- The "at night" wording — al-Adab al-Mufrad 1236 (graded sahih by al-Albani)
https://dorar.net/h/02JaCFTP
- The "at night" wording — Musnad Ahmad 8764 (chain graded sahih by Shu'ayb al-Arna'ut)
https://dorar.net/h/E0B5KZTi
- Dogs and donkeys at night "see what you do not see" — Sunan Abi Dawud 5103 (sahih, al-Albani)
https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5103
- "Do not curse the rooster, for it wakes people for prayer" — Sunan Abi Dawud 5101 (sahih, al-Albani)
https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5101
- Chapter on not reviling the rooster — Riyad as-Salihin 1730
https://sunnah.com/riyadussalihin:1730
- Shaytan flees the adhan — Sahih al-Bukhari 608
https://sunnah.com/bukhari:608
- Everything that hears the adhan will bear witness — Sahih al-Bukhari 3296
https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3296
- The punishment of the grave is heard by the animals — Sahih al-Bukhari 6366
https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6366
- Same account — Sahih Muslim 586a
https://sunnah.com/muslim:586a
- The mule near the graves of Banu al-Najjar — Sahih Muslim 2867
https://sunnah.com/muslim:2867
- Every creature waits on Friday morning in fear of the Hour — Sunan Abi Dawud 1046 (sahih, al-Albani)
https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1046

🔎 SCHOLARLY EXPLANATION
The explanations about the rooster's sense of the night, the angels saying ameen, and animals' perception are from the hadith commentary on Dorar al-Saniyyah:
https://dorar.net/hadith/sharh/10511

And Allah سبحانه وتعالى knows best.

title: Why My Istighfar Doesn't Work | What the Quran Actually Teaches
description:
Why does your istighfar feel empty? You keep saying astaghfirullah, after prayer, at night, and still the same sin, the same heaviness. This video looks at what istighfar actually is, why the way most of us do it leaves it feeling empty, and what the Quran teaches about asking for forgiveness and turning back.

We anchor on Surah Ali Imran, chapter 3, verse 135, and walk through the four movements of the verse: remember, seek forgiveness, know that only Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala forgives, and do not persist. We also cover the four gaps that make istighfar feel empty: the tongue without the heart, the word without the turn, the sin against people, and despair. Then a simple, livable system: Sayyid al-Istighfar line by line, a hundred astaghfirullah spread through the day, the return protocol for repairing what can be repaired, and a rhythm for the week.
This video does not promise wealth, a deadline, or a guaranteed outcome. The Quran gives a direction, not a date.

In this video:
What istighfar really means, and how it differs from tawba (Surah Hud 11:3)
Surah Ali Imran 3:135, the four movements of the verse
What the Quran connects istighfar with: rain, provision, strength, protection, and the hours before dawn
A gentle correction: istighfar is not a transaction
The four gaps: tongue without the heart, word without the turn, sin against people, despair
The Prophet Muhammad Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam, who sought forgiveness a hundred times a day
Abu Bakr Radiyallahu anhu and his dua for forgiveness
How to return quickly after a sin, and why despair is not humility
Sayyid al-Istighfar, the master of all forgiveness prayers, line by line
The return protocol: stop, feel, resolve, repair
A rhythm for the week, and a small piece of the night

References (all sources used in this video):
Quran:
Surah Ali Imran 3:135 (the centerpiece verse, four movements)
Surah Hud 11:3 (ask forgiveness, then turn back in repentance)
Surah Hud 11:52 (strength added to strength)
Surah Nuh 71:10-12 (rain, provision, children, gardens, rivers)
Surah Al-Anfal 8:33 (protection while seeking forgiveness)
Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:18 (the righteous seeking forgiveness before dawn)
Surah Al-Fath 48:2 (the Prophet Muhammad Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam forgiven past and future)
Surah Al-Hijr 15:56 (who despairs of the mercy of his Lord)
Surah An-Nisa 4:110 (whoever seeks forgiveness will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful)

Surah Al-Baqarah 2:222 (Allah loves those who constantly turn back to Him)
Hadith:
Sahih Muslim 2702 (the Prophet Muhammad Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam turns back one hundred times a day)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6307 (he sought forgiveness and repented more than seventy times a day)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4837 (Aisha Radiyallahu anha: "should I not be a thankful servant?")

Sahih al-Bukhari 834 (the dua the Prophet Muhammad Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam taught Abu Bakr Radiyallahu anhu)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6306 (Sayyid al-Istighfar, and its promise for whoever says it morning and evening)

Sunan Abi Dawud 1518 (relief from distress, worry, and unexpected provision). Scholars differ over its chain, and several grade it as weak. The video mentions it with this disclosure and does not build on it.
Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (seeking forgiveness for the believing men and believing women). Some scholars, including Shaykh al-Albani Rahimahullah, grade this hadith hasan. Others consider its chain weaker. The video presents it as a gentle encouragement, not as a foundation.
Other:
Hasan al-Basri Rahimahullah: it is reported that when people came to him with different troubles, his answer kept returning to one word: istighfar. The video presents this as a report, not as a hadith, and does not build on it.

A note on sources: references were checked against the Quran and standard hadith collections. Where scholars differ on a grading, the video says so. If you spot an error, tell us and we will correct it.
This video is a reminder, not a fatwa. For serious matters, especially money or a wrong that touches the law, ask a trusted scholar how to put it right.

Scenes are AI-generated cartoon illustrations of a fictional family. The script is original and human-written.

title: WHEN LIFE TESTS YOU | Futuh al-Ghayb — Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani | Read Aloud
description:
When hardship comes, where does your heart turn? To people, to your own plans, or to Allah? In the opening discourses of Futuh al-Ghayb, Shaykh Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani calls the listener back to obedience, sincerity, and trust — especially when patience is hardest.

🎧 The whole book, and the whole library, in the app — iPhone and Android:
👉 https://joyfulmuslims.com/yt
Free to start. 5 hours of listening every month. No card required.

This is the opening of Futuh al-Ghayb — Revelations of the Unseen — read in English: the Introduction followed by Discourses One through Eleven, in order.

These are direct addresses to the listener: how to meet trials, restrain the demands of the self, and turn toward Allah with a sincere heart. The questions are personal. What are you relying on? What happens to your faith when life does not follow your plans? And can you remain patient while the answer has yet to come?

The reading begins with “In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful” and closes with the reminder: “Only the patient will be paid their reward in full, without reckoning.”

• Obedience and sincerity

• The struggle with the self

title: Was Buddha a Messenger of Allah? What Islam Reveals
description:
What if one of the most influential spiritual figures in human history was originally a messenger sent by God? What if the teachings associated with Buddha today do not fully reflect the message he may have originally received?

For millions of people around the world, Buddha is a symbol of wisdom, spiritual discipline, and compassion. Buddhism has shaped civilizations, influenced cultures, and inspired generations. But a fascinating question arises: Could Buddha have been a prophet of God?

In this thought-provoking discussion, two prominent Muslim speakers, Dr. Zakir Naik and Sheikh Abdurraheem Green, explore this intriguing possibility from an Islamic perspective.

The Quran teaches that God sent messengers to different peoples throughout history, yet not every messenger is mentioned by name. Muslims know the names of some prophets, but many others remain unknown. Could Buddha have been among those messengers whose stories have been lost to history? Is there any basis for considering this possibility, or is it simply speculation?

Dr. Zakir Naik addresses the question directly, examining what Islamic sources do—and do not—tell us about Buddha. He discusses the limits of what can be established from the Quran and Hadith, and considers whether Buddha could have been one of the many messengers sent by God.

Sheikh Abdurraheem Green approaches the subject from another angle. He acknowledges that Buddhism contains teachings about self-discipline, compassion, and good conduct. But recognizing positive moral teachings raises a deeper question: Do good teachings necessarily reveal the true origin of a religion?

These questions lead to a crucial distinction between respecting certain moral teachings and establishing the religious identity of the person who taught them.

00:25 A fascinating question about the history of Buddhism
01:11 Buddha in the Quran?
01:41 How many messengers has God sent?
01:54 Why is Buddhism so fascinating?
03:10 Buddha, a messenger of Allah? Sheikh Green responds
04:30 What Muslims Need to Understand

title: The 4 Attempts to Reach the Prophet's Grave, What Really Happened?
description:
Four times, according to classical historians, people set out to reach the grave of Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم, and four times the plan ended before anyone reached it.

The first came from a ruler in Egypt who wanted the whole world to travel to his city instead of Madinah. Two came from secret tunnels dug beside the mosque. The last was an armed fleet on the Red Sea that came within a single day of Madinah. This documentary follows all four attempts in the order the historians record them. It also shows why the most famous of these stories was first written down almost two hundred years after it is said to have happened, while the least-known one was recorded by a traveller who saw its captives with his own eyes.

At Iman Aldeen TV, we separate what is established in the Qur'an and authentic Sunnah from what comes from later historical reports, and we tell you which is which.

1:21 The House Beside the Mosque

title: Allah Will Remove Shaytan From Your Home | DO This
description:
Many brothers ask me a version of the same question. My home does not feel peaceful anymore. There is a heaviness when I walk through the door. I am not sleeping well. My family argues over small things. Is Shaytan in my home? What do I do?

In this video, I share the answer from the Quran and the Sunnah, in simple words anyone can hold on to. Start with the door. Say Bismillah when you enter. Give salam, even in an empty home. Bring the Quran into your home and recite Surah Al-Baqarah. And keep a short daily dhikr on your tongue.

What this video covers:
The verse that names the enemy: Surah Fatir, chapter 35, verse 6
The hadith about mentioning Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala when entering and eating: Sahih Muslim, number 2018
The hadith about Surah Al-Baqarah in the home: Sahih Muslim, number 780
The example of Umar Radiyallahu anhu: Sahih al-Bukhari, number 3683, and Sahih Muslim, number 2396
The daily dhikr of one hundred times: Sahih al-Bukhari, number 3293, and Sahih Muslim, number 2691
The greeting when entering houses: Surah An-Nur, chapter 24, verse 61

The dhikr in this video:
La ilaha illallah, wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulk wa lahul-hamd, wa huwa ala kulli shay'in qadir.

Meaning: None has the right to be worshipped but Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty, and to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things competent.

A note on the empty-home greeting: giving salam when entering an empty home is encouraged by many scholars, based on Surah An-Nur 24:61. It is presented here as a scholarly encouragement, not as a direct command of a hadith.

Please verify every reference independently. Any mistake in this video is mine. This channel is educational. It does not issue religious rulings. For personal matters, please consult a qualified scholar.

How I research my videos: https://youtu.be/zTYtbFbC780

If this helped you, share it with a brother who feels the same heaviness in his home. And subscribe to Ayah Pulse for more reflections for the modern soul.

title: How the 4 Madhabs Took Over the Muslim World.
description:
Why do most Muslims in Pakistan follow the Hanafi madhab, while Muslims in Morocco follow the Maliki madhab and those in Indonesia mostly follow the Shafi'i madhab?

The answer goes back centuries, to the spread of Islamic scholarship, the journeys of students, the rise of powerful empires, and the trade routes that connected distant parts of the Muslim world.

In this video, we explore the history of the four Sunni madhabs: Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali. We'll look at how the teachings of the four great imams spread across different regions, how rulers and scholars influenced which madhab became dominant, and why the Islamic world gradually developed the religious landscape we see today.

From the Abbasids and Ottomans to Muslim scholars travelling across the Indian Ocean, the story of the four madhabs is about much more than four schools of Islamic jurisprudence. It's a story of knowledge, history, and how generations of Muslims preserved and passed on their understanding of Islam.

And despite their differences in Islamic law, the four madhabs are connected by a shared scholarly tradition, with generations of scholars learning from one another.

So how did four schools of thought that began in the same early Islamic world become so influential across different countries? Let's find out.

title: AI Tried to Find the Wall of Yajuj and Majuj — Its Final Answer Wasn’t What Anyone Expected
description:
The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم once warned that an opening had appeared in the barrier of يأجوج ومأجوج. The Quran describes that barrier of iron and molten copper in remarkable detail, yet no one today can say where it stands.

In this video, we give every clue from the Quran and the authentic Sunnah to artificial intelligence and ask it to find the wall. It builds a search profile from Surah Al-Kahf, examines the famous story of the caliph who sent a man to find the barrier, and tests the Great Wall of China and the Caspian Gates of Derbent. Its final answer changes the question itself.

Every claim in this video was checked against the Quran, authentic hadith and trusted scholarly sources. Later historical reports and disputed narrations are clearly labelled as such.

description:
Fifty archers were told to hold the pass and not to move, whatever happened. When they saw the
Quraysh turning back and the spoils lying open, most of them came down. The horsemen came round
the hill behind them — and the day turned.

🎧 The whole book, and the whole library, in the app — iPhone and Android:
👉 https://joyfulmuslims.com/yt
Free to start. 5 hours of listening every month. No card required.

al-Ashraf, the campaigns of Ghatafan and Bahran, Zayd ibn Haritha and the caravan, then the Battle
of Uhud itself — the martyrdom of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the wounding of the Messenger of
Allah (blessings and peace be upon him), his broken tooth and the rings of his helmet driven in —
and finally the march out to Hamra al-Asad the very next morning, wounded men and all.

title: Why does he always desire you?🤔#muslim #nikah #marriage #islamic #couple
The Miracle of the Man Whom the Earth Refused to Bury
description:
He had read Surah al-Baqarah and Surah Aal ‘Imran, and he used to write for رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم. Then he turned away, and began saying that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم knew nothing except what he himself had written.

When he died, his people buried him. In the morning, the earth had thrown him out. They dug deeper and buried him again, and the earth threw him out again. The third time, they dug as deep as they could, and the earth threw him out a third time.

This story is not a legend. It is recorded in both Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, and one of the Sahaba, أبو طلحة رضي الله عنه, saw it with his own eyes.

In this documentary we tell the story only from the Qur’an and authentic hadith, and we answer the claim he made from the Qur’an itself.

⏱️ CHAPTERS
0:00 – Three Graves, Three Mornings
1:12 – The Men Who Held the Pen
4:31 – The Man Who Read the Two Bright Ones
7:57 – The Claim He Carried Away
10:51 – The First Morning
14:06 – The Accusation
17:10 – As Deep As They Could Dig
20:04 – What أبو طلحة رضي الله عنه Saw
22:53 – What Allah سبحانه وتعالى Preserved

📖 REFERENCES
Every hadith and verse in this video can be checked at the links below.

Hadith

Sahih al-Bukhari 3617 – The man who wrote for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and the earth that threw him out (narrated by أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه): https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3617
Sahih Muslim 2781 – The same story, with “a man among us from بنو النجار”: https://sunnah.com/muslim:2781
Musnad Ahmad – “The earth will not accept him”, and أبو طلحة رضي الله عنه finding him cast out. Ibn Kathir رحمه الله said its chain meets the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim: https://dorar.net/h/Fa3oZynb
Musnad Ahmad – أبو طلحة رضي الل�� عنه: “I saw him lying cast out on top of the earth.” Graded sahih on the condition of Muslim by Shu’ayb al-Arna’ut رحمه الله: https://dorar.net/h/T9aMpO4I
Sahih Muslim 804 – Al-Baqarah and Aal ‘Imran, “the two bright ones”: https://sunnah.com/muslim:804
Sahih al-Bukhari 4990 and 2832 – زيد بن ثابت رضي الله عنه writing the revelation: https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4990 and https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2832
Sahih al-Bukhari 4986 – أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه asks زيد رضي الله عنه to gather the Qur’an: https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4986

Qur’an

Surah An-Nisa 4:95: https://quran.com/4/95
Surah Al-‘Ankabut 29:48: https://quran.com/29/48
Surah An-Najm 53:3–4: https://quran.com/53/3-4
Surah Al-Hijr 15:9: https://quran.com/15/9
Surah Al-A’raf 7:175: https://quran.com/7/175

Note: none of the narrations gives this man’s name, so we do not name him in this video. And Allah سبحانه وتعالى knows best.

title: Why Allah Made Desire the Hardest Test for Men | Control Lust in Islam
description:
Why did Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala create desire so powerful, and how can a Muslim man learn to control it without hating himself?

If you keep returning to the same sin, struggle with lowering your gaze, or feel trapped in a cycle of temptation and shame, this reminder is for you. It explains how to control desire in Islam with responsibility, discipline and hope, not self-hatred.

In this video:
The sin nobody confesses
Principle 1: Desire is natural
Principle 2: Desire is neutral
Principle 3: Desire is needed
How the fall actually happens
Six practical steps
A word for married brothers
What if you fell again?

What you will learn:
- Having a feeling is not the same as acting on it.
- Desire needs responsibility, because your choices decide where it goes.
- Desire has a lawful purpose, through marriage and self-discipline.
- Practical steps: lower the gaze, close the doors that lead to sin, fast when you cannot marry, fill your time with good, and make sincere dua.
- Shame must never stop you from repenting. Keep returning to Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala.

References mentioned:
- Quran 7:19-20, 24:30
- Sunan an-Nasai 3939 (Hasan)
- Sahih Muslim 1006, 2657, 144

In February 1804, the captured American frigate Philadelphia still sat in Tripoli harbor under Yusuf Karamanli’s guns. Lieutenant Stephen Decatur slipped in at night with a small crew, set the ship ablaze, and escaped—denying the Pasha a powerful warship and proving that American sailors could strike inside his own harbor.
Months later, with the naval blockade stalled, former consul William Eaton proposed a different kind of attack. He sailed to Alexandria, found Hamet Karamanli—Yusuf’s exiled older brother—and offered him American support to reclaim the throne. With a handful of Marines under Lieutenant Presley O’Bannon, Greek mercenaries, and hundreds of Arab fighters, Eaton marched nearly 600 miles across the Libyan desert.
On April 27, 1805, the expedition reached Derna. American ships bombarded the harbor battery while O’Bannon’s Marines and Greeks charged the walls. They took the fort, raised the 15-star American flag over foreign soil for the first time, and held the city against Yusuf’s counterattacks. For the first time, the Pasha faced a real threat on land as well as at sea.
The fall of Derna broke the stalemate. On June 10, 1805, Yusuf agreed to a peace treaty. American prisoners were released and tribute payments ended. The line “to the shores of Tripoli” entered the Marines’ Hymn, and the United States had shown it would fight rather than keep paying for safe passage.
This video follows the burning of the Philadelphia, Eaton’s search for Hamet, the desert march, the capture of Derna, and the treaty that followed.

By watching this video, you will gain a deeper understanding of the life and teachings of Prophet Ibrahim, also known as Hazrat Ibrahim or Prophet Abraham in Islam. The story of Ibrahim AS aag ka waqia is a fascinating one, and it serves as a reminder of the power of faith and the importance of standing up for what is right, just like Hazrat Ibrahim did. Our goal is to share Islamic stories in Urdu and Hindi, making them accessible to a wider audience, and to inspire our viewers with the stories of Anbiya ke qissay and Prophet Stories.

Who Will Be the First Person Clothed on the Day of Judgment — and Why
description:
Who Will Be the First Person Clothed on the Day of Judgment — and Why?

On the Day of Resurrection, every person who has ever lived will stand on one plain, barefoot and uncovered, exactly as they were first created. Yet the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم told his companions that one person will be clothed before all of creation, and he named him.

In this video we follow the story from the beginning: the young man who questioned the false idols of his people, the fire that was commanded to be cool and safe, the du'a he made about a Day he had not yet seen, and the authentic sermon in which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم revealed the first garment of the Day of Resurrection. We also look at why scholars think it was given to إبراهيم عليه السلام, whether this places him above the final Messenger صلى الله عليه وسلم, and the meeting between إبراهيم عليه السلام and his father on that Day.

Everything in this video is taken from the Qur'an and authentic hadith. Where a detail comes from a scholarly suggestion or a weak narration, we say so clearly in the narration. And Allah سبحانه وتعالى knows best.

6. He rejoices at your repentance - Sahih al-Bukhari 6309, Sahih Muslim 2747

title: 10 octobre 2026
Why Did This Man Ask Allah to Let Him Farm in Jannah?
description:
What if someone in Jannah, already given everything his soul could desire, asked his Lord for permission to do one ordinary thing from this world: to farm?

This is not a legend or a storyteller's invention. It is an authentic hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, narrated by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). The Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) told it one day while a man from the desert sat among the listeners.

In this video, we go through the hadith step by step: the man's request, the question his Lord asked him, the seed that grew faster than the blink of an eye, the harvest that stood like mountains, the words "Take it, O son of Adam, for nothing satisfies you," and why the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) laughed at what the Bedouin said next.

We also look at why Imam al-Bukhari recorded this hadith twice, once in his Book of Agriculture and once under the chapter "The Speech of the Lord with the People of Jannah," and at what this story means for the seeds we plant in this world.

Everything in this video is taken from the Qur'an, authentic hadith, and recognised Sunni scholarly explanation. The man in Jannah is never named in any authentic source, so we have not given him a name.

If you could ask for one thing from this world in Jannah, what would it be? Tell us in the comments.

CHAPTERS
00:00 Introduction
00:00 The Seed That Never Belonged to the Farmer
00:00 A Gathering, and a Man From the Desert

description:
Did you know Jesus was Middle Eastern and Mary is traditionally depicted wearing a veil?

Many people associate beards and women's head coverings exclusively with Islam, but these traditions have much deeper historical roots.

Jesus (Isa عليه السلام) lived in the Middle East, and Mary (Maryam عليها السلام) is traditionally portrayed with her hair covered, reflecting modest dress practices of the ancient world.

While we don't know exactly what Jesus and Mary looked like, their historical and cultural backgrounds were very different from many modern Western depictions.

In Islam, both Jesus and Mary hold an extraordinary position. Muslims believe Jesus is the Messiah and a mighty messenger of Allah, while Mary is honored as one of the greatest women in history.

Allah says in the Qur'an:
“And when the angels said, ‘O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds.’”
Qur'an 3:42

A reminder that Jesus and Mary are deeply respected in Islam.

title: Mention someone who needs this 😍
The Islamic Hajj Mentioned in the Bible? 🤔
description:
Did you know the Islamic pilgrimage of Hajj has a fascinating linguistic connection to the Bible?
In Exodus 5:1, Moses and Aaron tell Pharaoh to let the Israelites go so they can observe a religious pilgrimage or festival in the wilderness.

But here's where things get interesting.
When examining the original Hebrew on Bible Hub, the word associated with pilgrimage is connected to the Hebrew root ḥāgag. The Brown–Driver–Briggs Hebrew Lexicon even references the Arabic Hajj and pilgrimage to Mecca.

And the connections don't stop there.
In Genesis 16:14, the medieval Jewish commentator Ibn Ezra mentions a well called Zamum. Centuries later, Christian biblical commentator John Gill associated that name with Zamzam, the famous well in Mecca connected to Hajar and Prophet Ismail عليه السلام in Islamic tradition.

These are fascinating linguistic and historical connections between biblical commentary and Islamic tradition, although they do not establish that Exodus describes the Islamic Hajj itself.

Explore the sources and see what you think.

title: The Man Whose Tongue Fell to His Chest — The Warning of Surah Al-A'raf
description:
There is a man in the Qur'an whose name Allah سبحانه وتعالى never revealed, yet Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم was commanded to recite his story. He was given the signs of Allah سبحانه وتعالى, he was known among his people for answered supplication, and still he turned away. In this documentary, we follow what the Qur'an says about him in Surah Al-A'raf (7:175–177), what the early scholars of tafsir said about his identity, and the classical narrations about the day he climbed a mountain to supplicate against Prophet Musa عليه السلام.

We clearly separate what is established in the Qur'an and authentic Sunnah from what comes from later narrations (Isra'iliyyat), and we follow the methodology of Ahlus Sunnah wal Jama'ah throughout.

⏱️ Chapters
00:00 – The man the Qur'an never named
01:00 – Surah Al-A'raf 7:175: given the signs, then he left them
04:19 – Who was he? The answers of the early scholars
06:52 – The scholar whose supplication was answered
10:17 – A people at the edge of the Holy Land
11:40 – The request at his door
16:06 – The road to the mountain
17:52 – On the mountain above the camp
19:53 – The tongue that fell to his chest
21:15 – The example of the dog (7:176–177)
24:55 – Why this story was told
26:01 – A warning for every person of knowledge
27:57 – The supplication of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم

📖 Qur'an

Surah Al-A'raf 7:175 – https://quran.com/7/175
Surah Al-A'raf 7:176 – https://quran.com/7/176
Surah Al-A'raf 7:177 – https://quran.com/7/177
Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:21–26 – https://quran.com/5/21-26

📜 Hadith

The Greatest Name of Allah سبحانه وتعالى, narrated by Buraydah ibn al-Husayb رضي الله عنه. Sunan Abi Dawud 1493, also in Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3475 and Sunan Ibn Majah 3857; graded sahih by al-Albani – https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1493
The first people to be judged on the Day of Judgment, narrated by Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه. Sahih Muslim 1905 – https://sunnah.com/muslim:1905a
Seeking refuge from knowledge that does not benefit, narrated by Zayd ibn Arqam رضي الله عنه. Sahih Muslim 2722 – https://sunnah.com/muslim:2722

📚 Tafsir and classical sources

Tafsir Ibn Kathir رحمه الله on Surah Al-A'raf 7:175–177 (the identity reports, the narration of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and the views on the parable)
Tafsir al-Qurtubi رحمه الله on Surah Al-A'raf 7:175–176
Tafsir al-Tabari رحمه الله on Surah Al-A'raf 7:175
Tafsir texts are available on islamweb.net

⚠️ A note on the narrations
The Qur'an does not name this man. The name Bal'am ibn Ba'ura, the request of his people, the donkey, the mountain, and his tongue falling to his chest come from later narrations recorded by the scholars of tafsir, many of them traced back to the People of the Book. Why Are Jews So Successful? Did God Choose Them Above Others? | Imran Hosein Answers
description:
In this video, Sheikh Imran Hosein addresses a provocative question asked by a participant during one of his conferences: if Jewish people have achieved remarkable success in areas such as finance, media, politics, science, culture, and technology, does this prove that they are a “supreme people” or still uniquely chosen by God?

Sheikh Imran Hosein turns to the Quran, particularly Surah Al-Jumu'ah 62:6, and explains the distinction the Quran makes between the Children of Israel and those who adopted Judaism. He also discusses how the term “Jew” developed historically and challenges the idea that worldly success is evidence of divine superiority.

But what does Islam actually teach about the superiority of one people over another? Sheikh Imran Hosein argues that no nation or ethnic group has an inherent right to superiority and discusses the distinction between European and Oriental Jews in the context of modern political, scientific, and economic influence. In this video, we examine his response and the Quranic perspective presented in the discussion. Do you agree with Sheikh Imran Hosein’s answer? Does worldly success indicate that a people are specially chosen by God, or is true superiority based on something else? Watch the video and share your thoughts in the comments.

Why Makkah Is Protected: From the Elephant to the End of Time
description:
One night, رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم did something in his sleep that those around him had never seen from him before. When they asked him about it, he spoke of an army that would march toward the House of Allah سبحانه وتعالى and be swallowed by the earth on an open plain.

From the army of the elephant to that final army, Makkah has faced threat after threat. In this documentary, we follow them in order and look at what the Qur'an and the authentic Sunnah really say about the sanctuary Allah سبحانه وتعالى made safe.

We begin with the verse in which Allah سبحانه وتعالى reminded قريش that He made Makkah a safe sanctuary while people all around it were snatched away. We follow the army of أبرهة and its elephants, stopped in the valley of Muhassir in the year رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم was born. We hear the narrations of عائشة رضي الله عنها and حفصة رضي الله عنها about the army swallowed at البيداء, and why those who passed the hadith on said, when the army of الحجاج came, "We thought it was them."

We look at the siege of عبد الله بن الزبير رضي الله عنهما, the Qarmatians who carried the Black Stone away for more than twenty years, and the seizure of Al-Masjid Al-Haraam in 1400 AH by men who claimed the Mahdi had come.

Then we turn to the end of time: الدجال, who cannot enter Makkah or Madinah because angels stand guard at their entrances; the Hajj that continues even after يأجوج ومأجوج; and the last man who will ever raise his hand against the Ka'bah, at a time when no one remains on earth who says "Allah, Allah."

No one can name the army mentioned in the hadith, and Allah سبحانه وتعالى knows best.

Write in the comments where you are watching from, and let us make dua together for the people of Makkah and Madinah.

title: The Islamic Empires of China - (Forgotten History)
description:
How did Islam become part of Chinese history?

Islam has been present in China for more than a thousand years, developing through trade, migration, scholarship, political changes, and the rise and fall of different Muslim states and ruling dynasties.

In this video, we explore the Islamic history of China and follow how Muslim communities developed across China, from the early arrival of Islam to the growth of Muslim populations in places like Xinjiang, Gansu, Ningxia, Yunnan, and the northwest.

We’ll look at the different Muslim dynasties and kingdoms that emerged throughout Chinese history, the role of Central Asian and Persian Muslim communities, and how Islam interacted with Chinese culture and politics.

The story also takes us through periods of expansion, conflict, persecution, trade, and cultural exchange. Muslim merchants, soldiers, scholars, and travelers all played a role in shaping the history of Islam in China.

But how did a religion that began thousands of kilometers away become established in one of the world’s oldest civilizations?

And what happened to the Muslim states and communities that developed there?

This is the Islamic History of China — Simplified.

Feel Too Sinful to Return to Allah Listen to This
description:
Do you feel too ashamed of your past to return to Allah? This short Qur’an reflection is a reminder to begin sincere repentance today.

Inspired by Surah Az-Zumar, 39:53–54, this episode reflects on Allah’s call not to despair of His mercy and to turn back to Him. It speaks to the person carrying guilt, repeating a harmful habit, or waiting to feel “good enough” before asking forgiveness.

Returning begins with a choice: leave the wrong, seek forgiveness, sincerely resolve to change, and put right the harm you have caused where possible.

Your step today: identify one thing that keeps pulling you back, and take a practical step to leave it.

Qur’an reference: Surah Az-Zumar 39:53��54
Read the passage: https://quran.com/39/53-54

This is Episode 1 of “Allah’s Message to You | Qur’an Reflections.”
Watch the series through the playlist on this channel.

Subscribe for short Qur’anic reminders you can reflect on and practise. Share this privately with someone who needs encouragement to return.

This video contains an original reflection on the Qur’an, not new revelation or a personal message received from Allah.

May Allah grant us sincere repentance and forgive us. Ameen.

If you feel too sinful to return to Allah, listen to this. You are not beyond His reach, and your journey home can start today.

We often let our past mistakes, broken promises, and secrets convince us that we are unworthy of forgiveness. This weight can make faith feel distant, but despair is not the answer. This Islamic reminder is for anyone struggling with the belief that they have gone too far to return to Allah.

The truth is that sincere repentance is the bridge back to peace. It is not about being perfect before you approach Him; it is about the honesty of your heart when you decide to change. We reflect on why you should never despair of Allah's mercy, regardless of what you have done or how long you have been away. There is always a way to begin setting things right.

Subscribe for honest conversations about faith and spiritual growth, and tell me: what one step can you take today to begin again?

#IslamicReminder #Repentance #AllahsMercy

What Is Sharia Law? Here’s What Many Get Wrong ☝️
description:
What exactly is Sharia, and why is it so often misunderstood?

Sharia is much broader than the punishments or political systems people often associate with the term. For Muslims, it encompasses religious and moral guidance concerning worship, prayer, fasting, charity, family life, personal conduct and many other aspects of everyday life.

Its foundational sources include the Qur’an and the Sunnah of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, while Islamic jurisprudence developed through scholarly interpretation. This is also why there isn't one single universally codified “Sharia law” practiced identically by every Muslim or Muslim-majority country.

Before fearing something, understand what it actually means.

#Islam #Muslim #Sharia #IslamicTeachings #IslamicReminder

title: Islam Warns Against This…☝️
description:
Before judging someone for their past, remember that you may have no idea what has happened between them and Allah.

Someone may have fallen into sin and sincerely repented. What matters is not using another person's mistakes as an opportunity to feel spiritually superior.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is reported to have said:

Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 2505

Your prayers, fasting and charity should bring humility, not arrogance.

Focus on your own relationship with Allah, make excuses for others, and never underestimate the power of sincere tawbah.

title: Why You Keep Missing Tahajjud (And How to Fix It)
description:
Struggling to pray Tahajjud? It is time to look at why you actually want to wake up for this night prayer.

Many people find it difficult to maintain the habit of rising before dawn. You might feel exhausted from your daily responsibilities or simply struggle to find the right motivation. This discussion is for anyone who feels the weight of spiritual struggles when trying to commit to a consistent routine. It is not about forcing yourself awake, but about understanding the sincerity behind your intention.

When you find yourself waking up for Tahajjud, it should come from a place of personal connection rather than obligation. We look at how to balance your work-life demands with the quiet time you crave, helping you approach this act of worship with clarity and peace.

Subscribe for honest conversations about faith and discipline, and tell me: what is the biggest obstacle you face when trying to connect with your night prayer?

You set the alarm. You sincerely want to wake for Tahajjud. Then Fajr arrives, and you wonder why you slept through it again.

This reminder looks beyond the alarm: what fills your heart during the day, how to return after a mistake, why your intention matters, and how to begin with just two rak‘ahs. Missing a night does not mean you should give up. Come back and try again.

title: All He Wanted Was for His Mother to Accept Islam…❤️☝️
description:
All he wanted was for his mother to accept Islam.
For years, he thought, “She’s not Muslim… she’s not Muslim.” 

Then Allah opened a way he never expected.
While discussing what would happen after her death, he explained the simplicity and dignity of an Islamic burial. Her sons could carry her, her daughters could wash her, she would be wrapped in a simple white cloth and laid to rest.

Her response was simple: “That’s what I want.”
Then she gave her Shahada and accepted Islam.
He calls it “the greatest miracle of my life.”
Alhamdulillah, she was eventually laid to rest in a Muslim cemetery.

May Allah have mercy upon her and grant her Jannah.

title: “And whoever relies on Allah, then He is sufficient for him.” ❤️☝️🕋

Allah is not your backup plan.
Sometimes we try everything ourselves first. We make the plan, think through every possibility, and convince ourselves that we have everything under control.

Then, when our plans fall apart, we finally turn to Allah.
But tawakkul means placing our trust in Allah from the beginning, not only turning to Him when we've exhausted every other option.

Make the plan. Take the steps. But put your trust in Allah first. ❤️

description:
What happened to the Ottoman Empire during its final 100 years?

By the 19th century, the Ottoman Empire was facing growing political, military, and economic pressure. European powers were becoming stronger, nationalist movements were spreading across Ottoman territories, and the empire was struggling to hold its vast lands together.

This video covers the last 100 years of the Ottoman Empire, from the 19th-century reforms and the Tanzimat era to the rise of the Young Turks, the Balkan Wars, and the First World War.

We’ll follow the major events that changed the Ottoman Empire during its final century — the loss of territory in Europe, growing nationalism, political reforms, conflicts with European powers, and the devastating consequences of World War I.

The empire entered the 20th century still controlling large parts of the Middle East and surrounding regions. But within just a few decades, its territory was dramatically reduced.

The Ottoman Empire finally ended in 1922, after more than six centuries of existence.

So how did one of history’s longest-lasting empires go from ruling a huge territory across Europe, Asia, and Africa to disappearing completely?

This is the Last 100 Years of the Ottoman Empire — Simplified.


If you're interested in Ottoman history, Islamic history, Muslim history, the Ottoman Empire, the Balkan Wars, World War I, the Young Turks, and the fall of the Ottoman Empire, this video breaks it all down simply.

description:
Why do Muslims say “Alhumdulillah” even when something difficult happens?

At first, she didn’t understand it. Why praise Allah when life becomes painful?

Then she began to understand the deeper meaning: gratitude to Allah isn’t only for the moments when everything goes our way. Even through hardship, a believer can recognize that every experience is part of the journey and continue to place their trust in Allah.

Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said:
“How wonderful is the affair of the believer, for all of his affairs are good.” When something good happens, he is grateful, and when hardship reaches him, he is patient.
Sahih Muslim 2999

title: Why Have Black People Suffered So Much? Were They Cursed by God?
description:
In this video, a member of the audience asks Sheikh Ahmed Deedat a painful question about slavery, discrimination, poverty, and the belief that Black people are inferior. Deedat begins with a story that was used for centuries to defend that belief: the so-called “Curse of Ham.”

He challenges the people who turned a religious interpretation into a justification for oppression. Who decided that an entire people were destined to serve others? And why should anyone accept a claim that gave the powerful an excuse to keep others down?

Deedat then turns to the Qur’an. In Surah Al-Hujurat (49:13), God addresses all humanity. He says that He made us into nations and tribes so that we may know one another. Our differences are not a license to humiliate or dominate. The verse gives a different standard for honor in God’s sight: righteousness.

Deedat’s message also asks us to examine ourselves. The desire to feel superior is not confined to one race or nation. Whenever we judge people by their color, ancestry, wealth, or status, we create the very barriers that this teaching calls us to overcome.

This discussion does not offer a simple explanation for every tragedy in history. It confronts a dangerous answer that has too often been given: Black suffering is not proof of a divine curse, and no race is born inferior.

title: The Fall of Muslim Spain —  History (Simplified)
description:
How did Muslim rule in Spain come to an end?

For centuries, Muslim-ruled territories existed across the Iberian Peninsula. But over time, Muslim Spain began losing territory as Christian kingdoms expanded southward.

This video explains the Fall of Al-Andalus — how Muslim territories gradually became smaller, how the Taifa kingdoms and political divisions affected Muslim Spain, how the Reconquista continued to push south, and how one Muslim state remained in Granada.

By the final centuries of Al-Andalus, Granada was the last major Muslim kingdom in Iberia. In 1492, after the Granada War, the city of Granada surrendered to Ferdinand and Isabella, bringing an end to Muslim political rule in the Iberian Peninsula.

So how did Muslim Spain go from controlling large parts of Iberia to losing its final stronghold?

This is the Fall of Al-Andalus — Simplified.

title: You’ve Been Strong for Too Long
description:
Being the strong one can leave you emotionally exhausted. Everyone knows they can count on you—but who notices when you’re struggling?

Maybe you sit in the car before going inside because you need a few minutes where nobody needs anything. Maybe you stay awake because the night is the only time that feels like yours.

This video is for you.

We explore the weight of always being responsible, how strength can become a role you cannot remove, and what it means to accept support without feeling weak or ungrateful.

0:05   Reconquista and the Origin of Barbary pirate states
1:23   White Slavery
13:02 Tribute and America's First Encounter
22:30 Birth of the U.S. Navy
25:19 The Ultimate Humiliation
30:11 The First Battle (USS Enterprise vs. Tripoli)

For three centuries much of Europe treated the Barbary regencies as a cost of doing business: pay the tribute, swallow the seizures, ransom the captives, and pretend that dignity was optional. That bargain taught the corsair states a simple lesson—infidel ships and crews were revenue. 
The doctrine behind it was not a mystery. Islam licensed the war on those who would not submit, permitted the enslavement of captured unbelievers, and removed the guilt from both by treating them as a duty rather than a crime. 
Jefferson broke the lesson. He refused the extra demand from Tripoli, sent frigates instead of another chest of silver, and let the first American victory at sea announce that the United States would not be farmed. 
Once force answered force, the old racket lost its ease: tribute no longer bought safety, false surrenders no longer bought time, and the habit of treating Christian sailors as livestock became expensive. After that refusal, the Mediterranean did not become gentle overnight—but the assumption that the West would always pay and look away was finished.

I use a combination of primary sources and historical works, including the U.S. Navy's Naval Documents Related to the United States Wars with the Barbary Powers, 1785–1807, Gardner Weld Allen's Our Navy and the Barbary Corsairs, records from the U.S. Naval History and Heritage Command, the U.S. State Department's historical archives, and National Archives materials. I also cross-reference individual events with contemporary correspondence and naval records.

The Battle of Siffin in 657 CE stands as the ultimate, agonizing climax of the First Islamic Civil War, where the political unity of the early Muslim empire was permanently fractured on the banks of the Euphrates River. For days, the grand armies of Caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib and Muawiyah I, the governor of Syria, clashed in a brutal war of attrition that claimed tens of thousands of Muslim lives. Just as Caliph Ali's forces pushed to the brink of a decisive military victory, Muawiyah’s troops executed a brilliant, desperate psychological maneuver: they raised pages of the Quran on the tips of their spears, appealing for divine arbitration instead of further bloodshed. This cunning tactic instantly paralyzed Ali’s ranks, triggering a fierce internal mutiny by soldiers who refused to fight against the holy text. This forced the Caliph into a disastrous political compromise. The resulting, deeply flawed arbitration stripped Ali of his momentum, allowed Muawiyah to solidify his power base, and triggered the violently extremist Kharijite splinter movement. Ultimately, the battlefield deadlock at Siffin cemented the permanent ideological and political schisms that would forever divide the Islamic world into Sunni and Shia paths.

Why Doesn’t the Word “Bible” Appear in the Bible? | Bible vs. Quran, episode 2
description:
In this second episode of our series on the major differences between the Bible and the Quran, we examine one of the Quran’s most striking characteristics: it repeatedly speaks about itself, while the Bible does not present itself in the same way.

The word “Bible” does not appear within the biblical text itself. The Quran, however, repeatedly identifies itself by name and makes direct statements about its origin, purpose, authority, and mission.

It declares:

• “Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Quran…” (Quran 12:2)
• “Surely this Quran guides to what is most upright…” (Quran 17:9)
• “Indeed, it is We Who have revealed the Quran to you…” (Quran 76:23)

But the Quran goes beyond simply naming itself. It openly claims that it could not have been produced by anyone other than God (Quran 10:37). It then invites readers to investigate that claim:

“Do they not then reflect on the Quran? Had it been from anyone other than God, they would certainly have found in it many contradictions.” (Quran 4:82)

This is an extraordinary challenge. Rather than asking people to accept its divine origin without reflection, the Quran invites them to study its message, examine its claims, and search for internal contradictions.

Human authors can make mistakes, overlook details, or contradict themselves. Their books may later require correction or revision. The Quran, however, presents itself as a revelation from God, free from falsehood and internal inconsistency—and places that claim before humanity for examination.

For more than fourteen centuries, believers, scholars, critics, and opponents have closely analyzed the Quran. Its challenge remains open to every generation.

Watch this episode to discover how the Quran defines its own identity and how this differs from the way the Bible presents itself.

title: Bible vs. Quran: Human Authors or the Word of God? | Bible vs. Quran, Episode 1
description:
Although the Bible and the Quran mention many of the same prophets and historical figures, they do not present themselves in the same way. Their differences go beyond individual stories or teachings. They concern some of the most important questions in religion: Who is God? Who is Jesus? What is sin? How can human beings receive salvation? And from whose voice does Scripture claim to speak?

In this five-part series, we will examine five major differences between the Bible and the Quran by looking directly at the texts themselves.

This first episode explores one of the most fundamental differences:

The Bible is a collection of writings composed by different authors, whereas the Quran presents itself as the direct word of God revealed to the Prophet Muhammad.

The Bible is not a single book written by one person at one moment in history. It is a collection of books composed over a long period of time. These writings include historical accounts, biographies, laws, prophecies, poetry, letters, teachings, and testimonies. As readers move through the Bible, they encounter the voices of prophets, kings, historians, disciples, and letter writers.

The number of books also varies among Christian traditions. Protestant Bibles contain 66 books: 39 in the Old Testament and 27 in the New Testament. Catholic and Orthodox Bibles include additional books in the Old Testament.

Furthermore, not every biblical book introduces itself in the same way. Some passages report words presented as coming from God. The Book of Jonah, for example, begins by saying that the word of the Lord came to Jonah and commanded him to go to Nineveh.

The Gospel of Luke opens differently. Luke explains that many people had already written accounts about Jesus. He then says that, after carefully investigating everything from the beginning, he decided to write an orderly account. Luke therefore presents himself as someone who examined earlier reports and collected testimonies before composing his Gospel.

The Quran presents its origin and voice in another way. From beginning to end, it describes itself as a revelation from God conveyed through the Prophet Muhammad. Muhammad is not presented as the author developing his own religious ideas, but as a messenger responsible for communicating what was revealed to him.

This episode therefore does not examine only a difference in literary form. It examines a fundamental difference in how the Bible and the Quran present their origin, voice, structure, and authority.

In the Bible, readers encounter numerous human voices describing events, recording teachings, relating personal experiences, and explaining what they witnessed or understood about God’s actions.

In the Quran, one principal divine voice addresses humanity, recounts events, presents teachings, responds to objections, and gives instructions to the Prophet.

Understanding this distinction is essential for anyone who wants to compare the Bible and the Quran seriously and fairly.

The Battle of Jamal shattered the foundational unity of the early Islamic world in a tragic explosion of violence, marking the devastating onset of the first Muslim civil war (Fitna). On the blood-soaked plains outside Basra in 656 CE, two factions of the Prophet’s closest companions collided in a clash driven by political fracture and hijacked diplomacy. At the absolute center of the carnage stood Aisha bint Abu Bakr, the Prophet's widow, commanding her forces from an armored litter atop a massive camel, which served as both the physical and symbolic rallying point for her army. As the opposing forces of Caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib advanced, the combat concentrated into a brutal, desperate struggle around the beast, with hundreds of warriors falling just to protect or bring down the animal. When the camel was finally hamstrung and collapsed, the battle died with it, leaving thousands of Muslims dead at the hands of their brethren. This catastrophic encounter left an indelible, weeping wound on the Islamic world, fracturing the community along lines that would permanently alter its political, spiritual, and historical landscape.

title: I Survived the Backway—But I Was Still Lost
description:
How do you find your purpose when you feel lost—even after surviving what should have changed everything?

In 2014, I left The Gambia through the Backway. I spent nine days stranded in the Sahara Desert, lived for close to one year in Libya, and crossed the Mediterranean on a wooden boat carrying around 300 people. By the following morning, dozens had died. The Italian Navy rescued us, and I reached Europe alive.

But years later, I discovered something painful: I had survived the journey, yet I was still lost.

This first episode of Operation Ihsan is not only about what I survived. It is about what happened afterward—when procrastination, distraction and a lack of direction began controlling my ordinary days.

If you feel stuck, disconnected from your purpose or far from the person you know you could become, this video will help you begin with what Allah has already placed in front of you: your faith, family, health, work, education and abilities.

THE 7-DAY PURPOSE CHALLENGE

What important responsibility am I avoiding?

Who would benefit if I became more disciplined?

What one promise can I keep for the next seven days?

Choose one small but meaningful action. Keep it for seven days—especially when you do not feel motivated.

Subscribe to Operation Ihsan with Ahmadou Njie for honest videos about faith, discipline and transformation.

CHAPTERS

00:00 What Did You Survive For?
00:38 Why You Still Feel Lost

02:12 What Happened After I Survived
03:22 Survival Is Not Purpose
04:37 How to Begin Finding Purpose

07:14 Your Seven-Day Promise

Visual note: Some journey scenes are cinematic reconstructions based on Ahmadou's account.

0:00  Prophet Muhammad's Kindness (Case 1 - 12)
0:12  Case 3: Prophet Muhammad Stood Up for a Jewish funeral
Sunnah.com/bukhari:1312

3:12    Case 4: Prophet Muhammad Visited a sick Jewish Boy
https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1356

4:36    Case 5: Prophet Muhammad Shortened Prayers because He Heard a Baby Crying
https://sunnah.com/bukhari:707

https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3896
Sahih Bukhari 3896 
Narrated Hisham's father: Khadija died three years before the Prophet departed to Medina. He stayed there for two years or so and then he married 'Aisha when she was a girl of six years of age, and he consumed that marriage when she was nine years old.

Quran Surah At-Talaq (65) verse 4 further treats marriage to pre-pubescent girls as valid.

https://www.altafsir.com/Tafasir.asp?tMadhNo=0&tTafsirNo=74&tSoraNo=65&tAyahNo=4&tDisplay=yes&UserProfile=0&LanguageId=2
The tafsir of Surah At-Talaq 4 clearly explains that if a Muslim divorces his underage wife, or a girl who has not yet started her period, she must wait three months before remarrying. This verse is about marrying and divorcing underage girls.

7:47    Case 6: Prophet Muhammad's Patience with the Bedouin who Pulled His Cloak
https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3149
Compare this with https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4234
In Bukhari 4234, the Prophet’s slave Midʿam took a cloak from the undivided spoils of Khaybar before distribution. When Midʿam was later killed by a stray arrow, people called him a martyr. The Prophet rejected that and said: “No. The cloak he had taken illicitly was burning him as a flame of Fire.” 
Secretly taking from the common spoils (ghulūl) is treated as a serious offense that can nullify the reward of fighting. 
Openly demanding wealth and receiving a gift is a completely different category of action. The two cases are not parallel, so they cannot be used to claim the Prophet rewarded assault while punishing theft in the same way.
If yanking the Prophet’s cloak until it hurt him were meant to be accepted and rewarded as an Islamic ethic, he would have taught it as a standing rule. He never did.

14:01  Case 7: Prophet Muhammad Prayed for the People of Ta'if

15:24  Case 8: Prophet Muhammad Helped with Household Chores
The same household included multiple people he owned outright:
(1) a black slave stationed at his door (Bukhari 7263), 
(2) a black slave named Anjasha who drove his camels (Bukhari 6161), 
(3) a black slave girl who fetched his water (Abu Dawud 332), 
(4) a slave tailor provides him with a gourd dish (Bukhari 5433)
(5) The black slave Mid'am, gifted to Prophet Muhammad as war spoils at Khaybar (Bukhari 6707) 
(6) Prophet Muhammad also personally traded in people (Sahih Muslim 1602).

17:07  Case 9: Prophet Muhammad was Gentle with Children
https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5997
There are additional reports in secondary sources about Prophet Muhammad’s physical affection toward his grandsons Hasan and Husayn that go beyond ordinary kissing of the cheek or forehead.
You can read them for yourself here:
https://sunnah2.com/275 (from al-Nawawi’s Al-Majmu‘)
https://sunnah2.com/2226 (from Ibn ‘Asakir’s Tarikh Dimashq)

18:08  Case 10: The Qur’an Describes His Great Moral Character" (68:4)
Qur’an Surah Al-Qalam (68) verse 4 
"And indeed, you are of great moral character."
But "great moral character" is a claim that has to survive contact with the whole record, not just its best moments — and the same sources that preserve this verse also preserve: 
the execution of hundreds of male prisoners of Banu Qurayza and the (1) enslavement of their women and children (Case 3); 
(2) a conquest amnesty with a kill list attached, including executions at the Kaaba itself for offenses like satire (Case 2); 
(3) a siege of Ta'if with catapults and destroyed orchards, eleven years after praying for that same town's mercy (Case 7); 
(4) marriage to a child, sanctioned by his own precedent and by Qur'anic text (Case 5); 
(5) ownership and trading of human beings, including buying a man outright with two other slaves (Case 8); 
(6) Public promises of spoils to his own fighters, with no record of ever being kept (Case 6); 
(7) and a theology, confirmed in his own words (9:128), that his mercy was for Muslims only — not humanity.

20:50   Case 11: Prophet Muhammad was Gentle and Merciful with Believers
Qur’an Surah At-Taubah (9) verse 128
This verse states plainly what the rest of this document shows through specific cases: Muhammad's mercy is explicitly directed "to the believers", to Muslims only — not to humanity, not universally, but to the Muslim ummah only. 

22:07   Case 12: Prophet Muhammad uses a Superior Method to Repel Evil
Qur’an Surah Fussilat (41) verse 34

The preparation before the Battle of Jamal in 656 CE involved intense mobilization and failed diplomacy. Following Caliph Uthman's murder, Aisha, Talha, and Zubayr raised an army in Mecca and marched to Basra to demand justice. Simultaneously, Caliph Ali advanced from Medina and secured troops from Kufa. When the armies met, Ali initiated peace talks with Talha and Zubayr, nearly reaching a truce. However, overnight saboteurs launched a surprise attack to prevent peace. This sparked panic, causing both sides to believe the other betrayed the treaty, which triggered full-scale war the next morning.

title: Is Donald Trump Dying? Doctors Raise Serious Concerns
description:
In recent weeks, growing speculation about Donald Trump’s health has spread across social media and attracted the attention of doctors, analysts, and commentators. Some have pointed to what they describe as unusual verbal mistakes, apparent confusion, changes in behavior, and physical signs that they believe could indicate a more serious underlying health problem.

Among the examples discussed are several moments in which Trump appeared to confuse names, countries, or political figures. One particular incident drew significant attention after he referred to Iran as the “Islamic Republic of Japan.” While a mistake like this can obviously happen to anyone, some observers have questioned whether repeated incidents of this kind could indicate something more significant.

But the discussion does not stop with Trump’s mental sharpness.

Some medical commentators have also examined his physical appearance and claimed that certain visible symptoms could be associated with serious cardiovascular problems. One doctor has gone even further, publicly suggesting that Trump could be suffering from congestive heart failure and making a much more dramatic prediction about his future.

But how much confidence should we place in these claims?

This video takes a closer look at the arguments being presented by those who believe Donald Trump may be suffering from a serious illness. We examine the incidents that have fueled the speculation, the interpretations offered by medical commentators, and the question of whether observations made from public appearances can really tell us what is happening inside someone's body.

Donald Trump’s actual medical condition cannot be determined simply by watching videos or photographs online. The observations discussed in this video should therefore not be understood as confirmation of any particular diagnosis. They represent claims and interpretations made by individuals based largely on publicly available information.

And this raises an even deeper question: Can anyone truly know when another person is going to die?

From an Islamic perspective, this question has an important answer. Human beings can study diseases, recognize risk factors, analyze symptoms, and estimate probabilities. Doctors can sometimes make remarkably accurate predictions about the progression of an illness. But the exact moment when a person's life will end remains beyond human knowledge.

The Qur'an reminds us that no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die.

This is why Muslims should approach predictions about someone's death with particular caution. A person may appear extremely healthy and die unexpectedly, while another person who is believed to have only a short time remaining may continue living for many years.

title: The Untold Stories of Prophet Muhammad's Kindness (Part 1)
description:
Please support: https://www.patreon.com/NabiAsli
https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/nabiasli1
Prophet Muhammad's Kindness (Part 1) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AmGBuWKZzUk
Prophet Muhammad's Kindness (Part 2) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dvi5QQw3Izk

The stories of Prophet Muhammad's Kindness are rebutted one by one by Nabi Asli. (This video (part 1) rebutted cases 1 and 2. )
1. In Qur’an, Surah Al Anbiya 107, Allah sent Prophet Muhammad as a mercy to humanity. 
He is God’s mercy to the whole worlds!
2. After its conquest, he forgave the people of Mecca. They had persecuted him, exiled him and fought him in wars. Yet, when he conquered Mecca, he did not seek revenge; instead, he declared to them: 'Go, for you are free.'  
The Lesson is Real strength is shown through forgiveness when one has the power to retaliate.
3. Sahih Bukhari reported that Prophet Muhammad stood up for a Jewish funeral. Someone said: “"It is a Jew.”
He replied: "Was he not a human soul?”
This shows that he respected human dignity regardless of faith.
4. He visited a Jewish boy who had once served him and was now ill. This shows compassion and concern across religious boundaries. Who said he hated Jews?
5. According to Sahih Bukhari, the Prophet said that he sometimes intended to make the prayer longer, but when he heard a baby crying, he made it shorter because he knew it would distress the child's mother.
6. He showed patience towards the Bedouin who was harassing him. One of them grabbed his cloak so forcefully that it left a mark on his neck and demanded money. Rather than becoming angry, the Prophet smiled and ordered that the man be given something.
7. He prayed for the people of Ta'if, who had rejected Islam and injured him with stones. Jibril offered him the chance to punish the town. Instead, he prayed that their descendants might come to believe. Isn't this an act of mercy towards the pagans?
8. When asked about Prophet Muhammad’s life at home, Aisha bint Abi Bakr said that he used to serve his family and would leave for prayer when the time came. Can you imagine? A great and noble person like him doing household chores!
9. He was gentle with children. He kissed his grandson. When someone remarked that he had never kissed his own children, the Prophet replied: Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.
10. That’s why Allah said to the Prophet in Surah Al Qalam 4 that: “Indeed, you are of a great moral character.” 
11. He was kind to Muslims. Surah At Tawbah (9), verse 128 says that the Prophet is concerned for the Muslims and is kind and merciful to them.
12. Surah Fussilat (41), verse 34 says that the Prophet repels evil. He does this with a better deed. As a result, his enemy becomes a devoted friend.

The danger of subtle shirk is greater than you imagine.
description:
Subtle Shirk (Ash-Shirk al-Khafi): What It Is and Why It Is So Dangerous ?

Subtle shirk (Ash-Shirk al-Khafi) refers to hidden forms of associating partners with Allah that may not involve openly worshipping idols or other deities, but instead corrupt the sincerity of a person's faith and deeds. It often enters the heart through showing off (riya), seeking praise from people, relying on others as if they independently control one's destiny, or loving, fearing, or hoping in creation in ways that belong only to Allah.

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ warned his companions about this hidden danger, saying that what he feared most for them was the "minor shirk," which he explained as showing off (riya). A person may pray, give charity, or perform other righteous deeds outwardly for Allah, yet secretly desire admiration, status, or recognition from people. Such intentions diminish the sincerity that is essential for worship.

Subtle shirk is especially dangerous because it is difficult to recognize. Unlike obvious shirk, which is visible and easier to avoid, subtle shirk can quietly grow within the heart while a person believes they are acting sincerely. It weakens one's relationship with Allah, deprives deeds of their spiritual reward, and shifts trust and devotion away from the Creator toward the creation.

A believer protects themselves from subtle shirk by constantly renewing their intention (niyyah), remembering that all benefit and harm ultimately come only by Allah's permission, seeking His pleasure above the praise of people, and regularly asking Allah for sincerity. The Prophet ﷺ also taught a supplication: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do unknowingly."

The cure for subtle shirk is sincere faith (ikhlas), humility, self-accountability, and frequent remembrance of Allah. A heart that is devoted solely to Allah finds peace, while a heart attached to the approval of people remains restless. Therefore, every Muslim should regularly examine their intentions and strive to worship Allah alone with complete sincerity.
