title: #vairalvideo #islamicvideo #❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️💚💚💚💚💚🌹🌹🌹🌹🌹🌹🌹
The Most Misunderstood Qur’anic Verse
description:
Many people misunderstand the verse, “Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity” from Qur’an 2:286. It does not promise that life will never feel unbearable—it explains that Allah does not hold you accountable for obligations genuinely beyond your ability.

This Islamic reminder explains how this principle applies during sickness, salah, wudu, tayammum, necessity, sleep, forgetfulness and circumstances outside your control.

The video also explores the true meaning of iman, why “La ilaha illallah” must come sincerely from the heart, and why merely repeating the shahadah without understanding or belief is not enough.

Finally, you will learn why the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ encouraged Muslims to practise consistently without exhausting themselves. Simple and continuous dhikr—remembering Allah while walking, working, sitting or lying down—can become one of the smartest and most sustainable forms of worship.

Topics covered:

* The meaning of Qur’an 2:286
* Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity
* Prayer during sickness and incapacity
* Wudu, tayammum and genuine necessity
* Missing prayer through sleep or forgetfulness
* The true meaning of iman and shahadah
* Sincerity when saying “La ilaha illallah”
* Consistency in worship
* Keeping your tongue moist with dhikr
* Remembering Allah throughout everyday life

May Allah grant us correct understanding, sincere iman and consistency in remembering Him. Ameen.

title: POV : This Happen When You Finally Defeat Your Nafs
description:
What happens when you stop obeying every impulse and begin disciplining your nafs?

This cinematic Islamic POV follows an entire year of inner struggle—from delayed Salah, endless scrolling, anger, temptation, pride, comfort, and procrastination to repentance, self-control, sincerity, and obedience to Allah.

You will experience the first week of resistance, the first month of building discipline, the private victories after three months, the character transformation after six months, the hidden danger of pride after nine months, and the person you become after one full year.

Defeating your nafs does not mean your desires completely disappear. It means those desires stop making your decisions.

This Islamic journey explores how to control your nafs, discipline yourself as a Muslim, resist temptation, strengthen your iman, protect your Salah, reconnect with the Qur’an, practise tazkiyah al-nafs, overcome procrastination, and build a life guided by obedience rather than temporary desires.

description:
What could happen to your heart, faith, discipline, and relationship with Allah after one full year of saying Astaghfirullah 10,000 times every day?

This Islamic POV story follows the spiritual journey from the difficult first day of Istighfar to an entire year of consistently seeking Allah’s forgiveness. At first, the tongue becomes tired, the mind wanders, and completing ten thousand repetitions feels nearly impossible. But slowly, repentance begins softening the heart, strengthening patience, increasing gratitude, and rebuilding trust in Allah.

Throughout the journey, you witness the transformation that sincere Istighfar can create: greater inner peace, stronger salah, renewed hope, increased awareness of blessings, protection from sin, and deeper dependence upon Allah.

Allah tells us through Prophet Nuh عليه السلام:

“Seek forgiveness from your Lord. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving. He will send rain from the sky upon you in abundance, increase you in wealth and children, and provide gardens and rivers for you.”

— Surah Nuh, 71:10–12

This video is a cinematic reflection on the power of sincere repentance and consistent remembrance. It does not claim that a particular number guarantees specific worldly results. True Istighfar requires sincerity, repentance, abandoning sin, and returning the heart to Allah.

May Allah forgive our sins, purify our hearts, place barakah in our lives, and make us among those whose tongues remain moist with His remembrance.

Comment “Astaghfirullah” if you are beginning your own journey of seeking Allah’s forgiveness.

description:
For many people, the theory of evolution and Islam are completely incompatible. Others believe Muslims must either accept or reject evolution in its entirety. But is that really what Islam teaches?

In this video, we explore one of the most debated questions in science and religion: Did humans descend from monkeys? What does Islam really say about the theory of evolution?

We begin by tracing the origins of evolutionary thought, from the ancient Greek philosopher Anaximander to Charles Darwin's groundbreaking theory of natural selection. We then examine how evolution became one of the most influential scientific theories in history.

More importantly, we explore the Islamic perspective through the explanations of renowned Islamic researcher and preacher **Abdur-Raheem Green**. His insights reveal that the Islamic position is far more nuanced than many people assume.

In this video, you'll discover:

• Where the idea of evolution originally came from.
• What Charles Darwin actually proposed.
• Why many Muslim scholars do not completely reject every aspect of evolution.
• Which elements of evolutionary theory are compatible with the Qur'an.
• Why the Qur'an speaks about creation in successive stages.
• The two fundamental points where Islam clearly disagrees with modern evolutionary theory.
• Why the miraculous creation of Prophet Adam (peace be upon him) remains a central belief in Islam.

Whether you're a Muslim seeking a better understanding of your faith, a student interested in science and religion, or simply curious about one of today's most controversial topics, this video offers a clear and balanced explanation grounded in Islamic teachings.

At the beginning, memorizing the Quran feels exciting. Then the struggle becomes real. You repeat the same verses again and again. You forget pages you thought you knew. But the journey to becoming a Hafiz is not only about memory.

It is about patience.

It is about discipline.

It is about returning to the Quran every day, even after forgetting.

It is about protecting your heart, controlling your tongue, avoiding distractions, and allowing the words of Allah to change the person you are becoming.

If you are trying to memorize the Quran, struggling with Hifz, looking for Quran motivation, or searching for an Islamic reminder to reconnect with the Book of Allah, this video was made for you.

description:
Almost every modern gym plays music throughout the day. For Muslims who want to stay healthy and strengthen their bodies, this raises an important question: **Is it permissible to work out in a gym where music is constantly playing?**

In this video, we examine this issue in the light of the **Qur'an, the Sunnah, and the opinions of Islamic scholars**. You will hear the explanation of **Shaykh Assim Al-Hakeem**, who discusses the Islamic ruling on music, the difference between intentionally listening to it and merely being exposed to it, and the practical steps a Muslim can take when avoiding it is difficult.

In this video, you'll learn:

• Why many Islamic scholars consider musical instruments to be prohibited.
• How music can influence the heart and one's spiritual well-being.
• The difference between deliberately listening to music and simply hearing it in public places.
• Whether going to the gym is truly necessary or if there are better alternatives.
• Practical solutions for Muslims who have no choice but to work out in a gym where music is played.
• How to protect your faith while also taking care of your physical health.

This discussion goes far beyond the topic of gyms or music. It reminds us that Islam provides guidance for every aspect of our daily lives. Every decision we make—even the seemingly small ones—is an opportunity to seek what pleases Allah and avoid what distances us from Him.

The purpose of this video is not to judge anyone, but to present the Islamic evidence and the advice of scholars so that every Muslim can make an informed decision based on authentic knowledge.

title: Are You Making This Serious Mistake During Wudu?
description:
In this video we talk about one of the biggest mistakes many Muslims make while performing wudu (ablution) for prayer. 

One day, Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w) was travelling with his  companions. As they were returning to Madinah, the time for Asr prayer was running out. The companions became concerned. They needed to pray quickly. Eventually, they came across water and hurried to perform wudu.

The Prophet arrived and noticed something alarming. 

Some of the companions had rushed so much that parts of their  heels remained dry. The water had not reached every part of the foot. When the Prophet saw this, he did not remain silent. He raised his voice so everyone could hear and said: 

"Woe to the heels from the Fire." And he repeated it three times. 

This hadith teaches us something profound: 

A believer does not only ask, "Am I  worshipping Allah?" 

He also asks, "Am I worshipping Allah the way He commanded me 
to?" 

The companions were the best generation of Muslims, yet the Prophet corrected  them immediately when they made a mistake. This shows us the importance of constantly checking and improving our worship. So, the next time you make wudu, slow down. 

Take a few extra seconds. Make sure every part is washed thoroughly. Make sure no area is left dry. Because those few seconds could make the difference between a complete wudu and an incomplete one. 

======================

title: The Heart Commands the Brain: The Qur’an Revealed This 1400 Years Ago
description:
For generations, humanity has been taught that the brain is the undisputed center of intelligence, thought, memory, decision-making, and consciousness. The heart, according to conventional science, was viewed merely as a muscular organ responsible for pumping blood throughout the body. Yet more than fourteen centuries ago, the Qur’an presented a radically different perspective—one that modern science is only beginning to understand.

Could it be that the heart plays a far greater role in human awareness than previously imagined?

In this eye-opening documentary, we explore one of the most remarkable intersections between modern scientific discovery and divine revelation: the extraordinary relationship between the heart and the brain. We examine how recent breakthroughs in neuroscience, neurocardiology, and human physiology have revealed astonishing facts about the human heart—facts that echo statements found in the Qur’an centuries before microscopes, laboratories, or modern medicine existed.

Scientists have discovered that the heart possesses its own intrinsic nervous system, containing more than 40,000 specialized neurons capable of processing information, learning, remembering, and communicating directly with the brain. Far from being a passive organ, the heart continuously sends signals that influence perception, emotions, behavior, and decision-making. The heart does not merely sustain life—it actively participates in shaping human experience.

Even more fascinating, researchers have found that the heart generates the most powerful electromagnetic field in the human body, significantly stronger than that produced by the brain. Studies suggest that emotions such as gratitude, compassion, love, tranquility, and spiritual devotion create a state known as “heart coherence,” where the heart and brain function in harmony. This state has been linked to greater emotional stability, clearer thinking, reduced stress, enhanced focus, and improved overall well-being.

As these discoveries emerge, many are struck by the profound language of the Qur’an.

Why does the Qur’an repeatedly describe understanding, reflection, guidance, and spiritual awareness as functions of the heart?

Why does it speak of hearts that reason, hearts that reflect, hearts that become hardened, and hearts that become blind?

Allah says:

“Indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but the hearts within the chests that grow blind.” (Qur’an 22:46)

And He says:

“Do they not then reflect upon the Qur’an, or are there locks upon their hearts?” (Qur’an 47:24)

These verses invite us to reconsider what true intelligence really is. They suggest that the heart is not merely a physical organ, but the center of faith, sincerity, moral judgment, spiritual perception, and our relationship with our Creator.

Long before scientists discovered neural networks within the heart, long before terms such as emotional intelligence, neurocardiology, or heart-brain communication existed, the Qur’an consistently emphasized the central role of the heart in understanding truth and receiving guidance.

She did so and he replied, "𝐃𝐨 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐨𝐲 𝐦𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐠𝐚𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 `𝐀'𝐢𝐬𝐡𝐚, 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐢𝐧𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐡𝐚𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐦𝐞 𝐰𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐈 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐢𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐲 𝐰𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐧'𝐬 𝐠𝐚𝐫𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐛𝐮𝐭 `𝐀'𝐢𝐬𝐡𝐚'𝐬." She said, "I repent to God of annoying you, messenger of God." They then called Fatima, sent her to God's messenger, and she spoke to him, but he replied, "Do you not like what I like, girlie?" She said, "Certainly," so he said; "Then love this woman[*]." *i.e., Aisha. (Bukhari and Muslim.) The tradition of Anas, "`A'isha's superiority over women..." has been mentioned in the chapter on the beginning of creation on Aba Musa's authority.

title: IS JESUS GOD? // Pastor Came With Strong Arguments, But Ahmed Deedat Had a Powerful Challenge
description:
In this thought-provoking debate, the late Ahmed Deedat engages Pastor Stanley in a discussion on one of the most important theological questions in history: Is Jesus God?

For centuries, Christians and Muslims have held different beliefs about the nature of Jesus Christ. Christians generally believe that Jesus is divine and part of the Trinity, while Muslims honor Jesus as one of the greatest prophets of God but reject the idea that he is God or the son of God. In this debate, these two perspectives come face to face.

Pastor Stanley presents several biblical passages that he believes demonstrate the divinity of Jesus. He argues that Jesus possesses divine authority and points to verses that are commonly cited in Christian apologetics. Ahmed Deedat, known worldwide for his deep knowledge of both the Bible and the Qur'an, responds by focusing on a simple challenge: can anyone produce a clear statement where Jesus himself explicitly says, “I am God,” or “Worship me”?

Throughout the discussion, Deedat emphasizes the importance of distinguishing between the direct words of Jesus and the interpretations or writings of others. He highlights numerous passages in which Jesus speaks of the Father as greater than himself, acknowledges his dependence on God, and describes himself as one who was sent by God. According to Deedat, these statements are difficult to reconcile with the claim that Jesus is God Almighty.

The debate also examines one of the most frequently discussed passages in the New Testament: John 1:1. Both speakers offer different interpretations of this famous verse, illustrating how the same text can be understood in very different ways depending on one's theological framework.

In the latter part of the video, attention is given to the Qur'anic perspective on Jesus. The Qur'an describes Jesus, the son of Mary, as one of God's greatest messengers who was born miraculously, performed extraordinary miracles by God's permission, and called people to worship the One True God alone (Qur'an 3:51). The Qur'an also emphasizes Jesus' humanity and rejects the idea that he shares in God's divinity (Qur'an 5:75). Furthermore, the Qur'an explicitly rejects the deification of Jesus, stating: "It is not for Allah to take a son. Glory be to Him! When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is" (Qur'an 19:35). 

Whether you are a Christian, a Muslim, a student of comparative religion, or simply someone interested in exploring important theological questions, this debate offers a fascinating opportunity to hear two opposing viewpoints presented directly and passionately.

title: A Professor Tried to Corner Ahmed Deedat, But His Brilliant Response Left Everyone Speechless
description:
For centuries, critics of Islam have raised two common objections about Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him): that he could neither read nor write, and that Islam spread by the sword. But what if these very accusations reveal something entirely different when examined more closely?

In this fascinating debate, Ahmed Deedat responds to a Christian teacher who challenges the foundations of the Islamic faith with these two arguments. Rather than avoiding the questions, Deedat confronts them head-on, drawing upon history, logic, and even passages from the Bible itself.

Can an unlettered man produce a message that transforms civilizations and influences billions of people across centuries? Does the success of a religion necessarily prove that it was imposed by force? Or is there another explanation that deserves consideration?

This video explores how Ahmed Deedat approached these questions and why his answers continue to spark discussion decades later. Whether you are Muslim, Christian, or simply interested in comparative religion, this exchange offers an opportunity to reflect on some of the most frequently debated issues surrounding the life and mission of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).

The discussion also touches upon the observations of renowned Scottish historian and philosopher Thomas Carlyle, whose assessment of Muhammad challenges many popular assumptions about the spread of Islam. His remarks invite us to consider a broader historical perspective and to ask whether ideas can truly conquer hearts through coercion alone.

Whatever your conclusions may be, one thing is certain: this debate raises questions that deserve thoughtful consideration rather than simplistic answers.

title: 3 Big Mistakes Muslims Make During Eid Sacrifice // #eidaladha2026
description:
Every year, millions of Muslims around the world prepare for the blessed days of Eid al-Adha by offering a sacrifice for the sake of Allah. But while many people focus on choosing an animal and preparing for the celebration, countless Muslims unknowingly fall into mistakes that can reduce the reward of this great act of worship — and in some cases even make the sacrifice invalid.

In this video, we discuss some of the most common mistakes people make during Qurbani/Udhiyah and the important Islamic rulings every Muslim should know before slaughtering their animal. These reminders are based on authentic teachings from the Quran and Sunnah and are meant to help believers protect their worship and perform this sacred act correctly.

We will talk about:
- The serious mistake of slaughtering before the Eid prayer
- Why choosing a weak or defective animal goes against the Sunnah
-  The forgotten ruling about cutting hair and nails during the first ten days   of Dhul Hijjah
-  The spiritual meaning behind sacrifice in Islam
-  The connection between Eid al-Adha and the legacy of Prophet Ibrahim

Allah says:

“And proclaim to the people the Hajj; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel…” (Surah Al-Hajj 22:27)

Eid al-Adha is not just a cultural tradition or yearly celebration. It is a powerful act of obedience, gratitude, and submission to Allah — a reminder of the faith and sacrifice of Prophet Ibrahim and his family.

Many Muslims grow up following traditions passed down from family and society without learning the actual rulings of Islam. That is why seeking knowledge before worship is so important. A small mistake done unknowingly can affect a major act of worship, while a small piece of beneficial knowledge can guide an entire family toward the Sunnah.

And hardly did He spit out something, or clear his throat of phlegm, but that they would catch it in the palms of their hands, and rub it over their faces and their bodies. And hardly did a hair fall from him, but that they would rush to get it. Whenever He ordered them to do something, they rushed to his order; and whenever He talked, they lowered their voices in his presence; and they did not fix their gaze on him out of reverence towards him.

Anas related: The Messenger of Allah (SAW) used to pray, and would prolong getting up from praying; and the Prophet (SAW) once urinated into a well that was in his house. He [Anas] said: There was no well in Medina with fresher water than this one. He said: And whenever people came around, He would draw up fresh water from it for them. From Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: A boy from some of the Quraish gave the Prophet (SAW) a cupping treatment, and when he finished the cupping, he took the blood, brought it behind the wall, looked right and left, and when he did not see anyone, he sipped down His blood until he finished it, and then went back. The Prophet (SAW) saw his face and said: “Woe to you, what did you do with the blood!” “I got rid of it behind the wall.” He said: “Where did you get rid of it?” “Oh Messenger of Allah, I was reluctant to give up your blood by spilling it on the ground – it’s in my belly.” He said: “Go now, you’ve saved yourself from hellfire.”

The most heartbreaking moment in Surah Maryam ✨🌷 #deen #deensayings
description:
In Surah Maryam, one of the most emotional and heartbreaking moments appears when Maryam (Mary) is left completely alone during the pain of childbirth. Carrying a miracle that people would never understand, she was overwhelmed by fear, pain, and the thought of how society would judge her. In that moment of unbearable sorrow, she cried out:

“I wish I had died before this and was completely forgotten.”
— Qur’an 19:23

These words reveal the depth of her pain and loneliness. Yet even in that darkest moment, Allah did not abandon her. He comforted her, provided for her, and reminded her that His mercy is always near, even when the heart feels shattered. This moment teaches that even the strongest believers can feel overwhelmed, but Allah’s help always arrives at the perfect time.

The Urine Incident

The following narrations (several of which are classed as sahih, i.e. authentic) discuss the drinking of Prophet Muhammad's urine
Imam Jalal al-Din Suyuti reports from Tabarani and Bayhaqi who narrate from Hukaymah bint Umaymah (May Allah be pleased with her) with an authentic chain of transmission, she said, 'the Prophet (May Allah shower peace and blessings on Him) had a wooden bowl in which He used to urinate and was placed under His bed. One night, He searched for it but did not find it and asked for it saying, ‘where is the bowl?’ The members of the house replied ‘Umm Salamah’s slave girl Barrah drank from it’ who came from Habashah with her. The Prophet replied, ‘surely she has protected herself from the fire with a great wall’’'.
Source: Al-Khasa’is al-Kubra 2:252, Matba’ah Da’irat al-Ma’arif, Hayder Abad

Imam Jalal al-Din Suyuti reports from Abu Ya’la, Hakim, Dar Qutni, Tabarani and Abu Nu’aym from Umm Ayman May Allah be pleased with her, who said, ‘the Prophet got up one night and urinated in a bowl. During that night, I rose in the state of thirst so I drank whatever was in the bowl. In the morning I told Him what I had done to which He smiled and said, ‘surely you will never have pain in your stomach’’. Abu Ya’ala’s wordings are as follows, ‘you will never feel stomach pain as of today’.[3]
Tabarani said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal informed us, who was informed by Yahya ibn Ma’een, who was informed by Hajjaj Bin Muhammad who narrates from Ibn Jurayj who narrates from Hukaymah bint Umaymah, who reports from her mother Umaymah who said, ‘the Prophet SAW used to have a wooden bowl in which he used to urinate and place under His bed. One night, He searched for it but did not find it and asked for it saying, where is the bowl? The members of the house replied ‘Umm Salamah’s slave girl Barrah drank it’ who came from Habashah with her. The Prophet replied, ‘surely she has protected herself from the fire with a great wall’.
Source: Al-Mu’jam al-Kabeer

Tasawwuf & Sufism in Islam | The True Meaning of Sufism Explained
description:
What is Tasawwuf in Islam?
What is the true meaning of Sufism?
Is Sufism something separate from Islam — or is it the spiritual heart of Islam?

In this video, we explore the real concept of Tasawwuf (Sufism) in the light of Qur’an and Sunnah. Many people misunderstand Sufism. Some think it is innovation, others think it is something mysterious. But in reality, Tasawwuf is about purification of the heart, sincerity, Taqwa, and building a deep connection with Allah.

We will discuss:

• What does Tasawwuf actually mean?
• The goal of Sufism in Islam
• The importance of purifying the heart
• The connection between Shariah and Tariqah
• Common misconceptions about Sufism

Tasawwuf is not about strange practices. It is about transforming your character, controlling your nafs, and living Islam with sincerity and excellence (Ihsan).

If you truly want to understand the spiritual dimension of Islam, this video will give you clarity.

Watch till the end — and begin your journey of inner purification.

description:
Inspired by how Yusuf Alwattar honors his mother, Dr. Carmen Botero, by learning her story, I wanted to honor my own. 

In this clip, I reflect on how the courage, sacrifice, and love of our parents shape us in ways we often only recognize in adulthood and on the barakah (blessings) that unfolds when we honor the people who raised us, even imperfectly, and how those blessings ripple through our lives.

Yusuf shares a powerful account of his mother’s life, a story anchored in faith, service, and an unbroken chain of strong women and principled men. Yusuf traces his lineage back to his great-grandparents to reveal the qualities that formed Mama Carmen: generosity, resilience, spiritual devotion, and a lifelong commitment to serving others.

Knowing our parents’ stories deepens our compassion for them and opens us to a kind of abundance only God can give.

Stitch or tag @Suhbahstories and share how you honor your parents. 🤍

Love, Hadiyah

A Muhammad-Evans family production, Suhbah Stories is what happens when good friends, good vibes, and good stories come together. Suhbah (Arabic: صُحبة) means companionship or fellowship, being together on the path of life and faith.

Suhbah is the kind of circle that feeds your soul and reminds you of what really matters. Around our table, stories are gifts: funny, raw, heartfelt, and always real. title: Why Are We Not Talking About Sudan?
description:
Why do some crises move us deeply — while others barely register?

This talk addresses an uncomfortable but necessary topic: selective compassion. Most people don’t ignore suffering out of malice. Often, it’s because we feel less connected, less familiar, or less represented in the stories we see.

From a psychological perspective, empathy tends to follow familiarity — the people who remind us of ourselves, our families, our culture, or our communities. From an Islamic perspective, however, this becomes a spiritual challenge. Our compassion cannot be based on resemblance alone, but on faith.

Using Sudan as a case study, this lecture explores:

— Why empathy is often selective by nature
— How Islam calls us to expand both our in-group and our compassion
— The meaning of the Ummah being “one body”
— Why some suffering tests our īmān more than others
— How to actively cultivate empathy when it doesn’t come naturally

This is not a message of blame or shaming — but a call to awareness, growth, and action. Islam teaches us that empathy is not only a feeling; it is something we practice, even when it is difficult, unfamiliar, or uncomfortable.

May Allāh expand our hearts to carry the pain of the entire Ummah — not just the parts that feel closest to us.

title: Sheikh Nuh Ha Mim Keller - What Muslims Must Know: Ozempic
description:
In this lecture, Sheikh Nuh Keller examines the growing use of Ozempic (semaglutide), a drug developed for type 2 diabetes but now widely promoted as a weight-loss solution. He explains how the hormone GLP-1 works in the body, how semaglutide imitates its effects, and why the pursuit of rapid weight loss overlooks deeper health realities.

He highlights the difference between calorie intake and nutrient deficiency in obesity, and warns of serious risks such as gastroparesis, microbiome disruption, depression, muscle loss, and official safety concerns including thyroid tumors, pancreatitis, and gallbladder disease. These dangers show the reductionist error of treating the body as separate parts rather than as an integrated whole.

Sheikh Nuh concludes by pointing to lasting solutions based on balance and discipline, including exercise, strength training, and fasting. As prevention, he stresses the benefit of a daily twelve-hour fasting window and fasting one day each week, practices that preserve health and strengthen resilience.

title: Omar Suleiman _ If You Notice These 3 Signs, You’re Among ALLAH's Most Valued Believers
description:
Omar Suleiman _ If You Notice These 3 Signs, You’re Among ALLAH's Most Valued Believers
Imam Omar Suleiman is among the most influential Muslim scholars and public intellectuals in the modern era. As an imam, educator, author, activist, and founder of Yaqeen Institute for Islamic Research, he has carved out a unique role that bridges classical Islamic tradition and contemporary intellectual discourse. Known for his warm delivery, spiritual depth, and commitment to justice, Suleiman has become a household name among Muslims in North America and beyond. His books, lectures, and online content reach millions worldwide, and his social activism has earned him respect from both Muslim and non-Muslim communities.

This biography aims to provide a comprehensive 4000-word exploration of his life, works, ideas, and legacy. It will cover his early life, religious training, academic achievements, community leadership, intellectual contributions, publications, activism, and his impact on shaping Muslim identity in the West.
Omar Suleiman was born on June 3, 1986, in New Orleans, Louisiana, United States. He grew up in a family of Palestinian descent, one of many immigrant families who carried with them a strong cultural and religious heritage. His parents emphasized both education and faith, instilling in him a sense of devotion to Islam alongside the responsibility of engaging with the wider world.

Growing up in New Orleans, a city marked by cultural diversity, music, and a vibrant mix of communities, Suleiman was exposed early on to pluralism. However, being a Muslim child in post–Gulf War and later post-9/11 America also meant facing identity struggles and questions about belonging. These experiences later informed his commitment to interfaith dialogue and social justice advocacy.

From a young age, he was drawn toward the Qur’an, spirituality, and stories of the Prophets. His religious curiosity was nurtured by his local Muslim community and early mentors. At the same time, his American upbringing exposed him to issues of racism, inequality, and justice — themes that would later feature prominently in his work.
Omar Suleiman pursued a dual path of education — excelling in both secular academia and Islamic studies. He earned bachelor’s degrees in Accounting and Islamic Law, followed by master’s degrees in Islamic Finance and Political History. His intellectual interests ranged from Shariah sciences to modern economics, reflecting his desire to integrate faith with contemporary realities.

Advanced Islamic Studies

He studied under renowned scholars in the United States and abroad, focusing on Hadith, Fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence), Tafsir (Qur’anic exegesis), and theology. His mentors included scholars from diverse traditions of Sunni Islam, giving him a balanced and inclusive perspective.

In 2020, he completed a Ph.D. in Islamic Thought and Civilization at the International Islamic University of Malaysia (IIUM), one of the leading centers of Islamic scholarship in the modern world. His doctoral research deepened his understanding of Islamic intellectual heritage and its application to contemporary challenges.
After completing much of his training, Omar Suleiman returned to serve as an imam in his hometown of New Orleans. He was appointed imam of the Jefferson Muslim Association, where he served for six years.

During this period, he became deeply involved in community service and interfaith work. The devastating impact of Hurricane Katrina (2005) marked a turning point in his life. Alongside other Muslim leaders, he launched initiatives under Muslims for Humanity, providing relief to victims regardless of faith. His leadership during this crisis drew admiration and demonstrated his philosophy of Islam as a force for compassion and public service.

He also co-founded the East Jefferson Interfaith Clergy Association, fostering dialogue among Christian, Jewish, and Muslim communities. His efforts earned him the Outstanding Citizen Award in 2010, a recognition of his ability to bridge faith and civic responsibility.
Later, Omar Suleiman moved to Dallas, Texas, a city with a large and diverse Muslim population. There, he became the Resident Scholar at Valley Ranch Islamic Center. His role included delivering sermons, teaching classes, mentoring youth, and engaging in community activism.

Dallas provided a larger platform for his work. He became co-chair of Faith Forward Dallas at Thanks-Giving Square, a multifaith coalition addressing issues like poverty, racism, and injustice. His reputation as both a spiritual guide and an activist grew significantly during this time.

title: 042.Consultation (Al-Shura)
description:
042.Consultation (Al-Shura)

A Meccan sura that takes its name from verse 38, where the practice of
consultation (shura) is listed as one characteristic of the Muslim
community. The sura discusses man’s habit of creating division and
disharmony in matters of religion, and God’s all-prevailing power, wisdom,
and ɹnal decision. The unity of religion is stressed (verse 13) as is the
continuity of the prophets (verse 3). The Prophet is reminded that he
cannot compel people to believe, that they will be judged according to their
deeds, and that he is only there to deliver the message. The nature of
revelation is described in verses 51–3.

title: Positive Interpretations of Life by ML AS Khatani
description:
Positive Interpretations: Lessons from the Sahabah's Retreat

This video discusses a significant incident involving Abdullah ibn Umar (radiyallahu ta'ala anhuma) and Rasulullah (sallallahu alayhi wa sallam) that illustrates the principles of compassion and understanding in Islamic teachings. It highlights the following key points:

1. Greeting and Respect: When meeting someone regularly, a simple greeting (salaam) suffices. However, upon returning from a journey or meeting a pious or senior person, more affectionate gestures like embracing or kissing are encouraged.

2. Positive Interpretation of Actions: The document emphasizes the importance of interpreting actions positively, especially when someone makes a mistake. Instead of condemning or rebuking, one should look for a positive angle, as demonstrated by Rasulullah (sallallahu alayhi wa sallam) when he reframed the retreat of some Sahabah during a battle as a strategic regrouping rather than cowardice.

3. Encouragement Over Despair: Rasulullah (sallallahu alayhi wa sallam) provided encouragement to his followers, helping them learn from their setbacks rather than succumbing to despair. This approach fosters resilience and courage among believers.

4. Kissing the Hand of the Pious: The act of kissing the hand or forehead of a pious person is permissible and encouraged in Islam, as long as it is not done excessively. The document references a hadith where Abdullah ibn Umar and others expressed their reverence for the Prophet by kissing his hand.

Overall, the teachings promote a compassionate and understanding approach to interpersonal relations within the framework of Islamic principles.

Ali was 56 year old, and much had happened in the 23 years after the Prophet's (S) death. Ali was preoccupied and disturbed by much that was said about Uthman and his bad administration, all of which was in the negative.  Imam Ali worried about the future of the Islamic nation; there was much at stake.  People complained vehemently to Ali about the deteriorating conditions and about the Governors of Banu Umayyah who acted like dictators using the public treasury (like tax money) as they pleased as if the money belonged to them. Imam Ali was also pained because Uthman being indecisive or incapable left matters in the hands of his Secretary of State, the highly questionable Marwan!  Marwan, the real power, craftily played his hand in a clever way, engineering everything to his own advantage and to the advantage of his family Banu Umayyah. Because of these and other matters, thousands of extremely concerned people came from Iraq and Egypt to express their grievances to the Khalifa.  They wanted a radical change for the betterment of the State, a change in the administration of Uthman.  They went to Ali to see if he could help.

Welcome to "Call of peace" channel.

In the name of Allah, the most Gracious, the most merciful.

Here you have in your hand a wonderful, Nasheed“Tal’a al-Badru Alayna' which  is a timeless and soulful Arabic nasheed that echoes the heartfelt welcome of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to the blessed city of Madinah. This beautiful nasheed, rich in love, spirituality, and reverence, brings to life the joy and honor of that historic moment, resonating deeply with the hearts of Muslims around the world.

Performed by the talented vocalist "M.Huzaifa Jawed." this rendition of Tal’a al-Badr ’Alayna captures the essence of devotion and admiration for the Prophet (PBUH), invoking feelings of peace and spiritual tranquility. The soft, melodic tones and the heartfelt lyrics speak directly to the soul, taking the listener on a journey of remembrance and love.

Through this nasheed, we send a message of peace and love, commemorating a great occasion in the life of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), hoping that this work will be a source of inspiration and comfort for the heart and soul. We pray that Allah accepts this effort in our good deeds and brings us closer to Him and His Messenger.  

Brought to you by Call of Peace, If you enjoy this nasheed, don’t forget to subscribe to the channel, hit the like button, and share this work with your loved ones.

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

 فها بين أيديكم نشيد روحاني خالد “طلع البدر علينا”، وهو من أجمل الأناشيد الع��بية التي تعبر عن الفرحة الكبرى بقدوم النبي محمد ﷺ إلى المدينة المنورة. هذا النشيد يحمل في كلماته معاني الحب والتقدير والروحانية، ويعيد إلى الأذهان ذلك الحدث التاريخي العظيم، ليلامس قلوب المسلمين في كل زمان ومكان.

title: 25 PROPHETS IN ISLAM ☪️ 👆 #shorts #allah
description:
25 PROPHETS IN ISLAM ☪️ 👆 #shorts #allah 


Did you know Islam recognizes 25 prophets mentioned in the Quran?

It all starts with Adam (AS), the first human and prophet. Then came Idris (AS), Nuh (AS) who built the ark, and Hud (AS) who warned his people.

Next, Salih (AS), Ibrahim (AS)—the father of prophets, Lut (AS), Ismail (AS), Ishaq (AS), Yaqub (AS), and Yusuf (AS), known for his dream interpretations.

Then, Shu'ayb (AS), Ayyub (AS)—known for his patience, Dhul-Kifl (AS), Musa (AS) who led the Israelites, Harun (AS), Dawud (AS) who defeated Goliath, and Sulaiman (AS) who ruled with wisdom.

Ilyas (AS), Alyasa (AS), Yunus (AS)—who was swallowed by a whale, Zakariya (AS), Yahya (AS), Isa (AS) (Jesus), and the final prophet, Muhammad (PBUH), the seal of all prophets.

These prophets brought guidance and wisdom. Which one inspires you the most? Let me know in the comments!

Ali (R.A.) was so reliable and trustworthy that the Prophet (S.A.W.) designated him as one of the scribes who would write down the text of the Holy Quran, which had been revealed to the Prophet (S.A.W.) during his lifetime. As Islam began to spread throughout Arabia, Ali (R.A.) helped to establish the new Islamic order by carrying the massages and declaring the Islamic guidelines. Further, Ali (R.A.) was instructed to write down the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, the peace treaty between the Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) and Quraysh. Ali (R.A.) was sent to Yemen to spread the teachings of Islam. He was also charged with settling several disputes and putting down the uprisings of various tribes. He was well versed in the knowledge of lineages, proverbs and the history of important-events. He travelled to Syria and Ethiopia and mixed with non-Arab people, learning things about their lives and customs that no one else knew. He took care of the business that he had inherited from his father and his wealth grew. He was regarded as one of the men of Banu Umayyah clan who were held in high esteem by all of Quraysh. Thus, Uthman (R.A.) was regarded as being of high status among his people and he was loved dearly.

Top Mufti at Islamweb.net Makes Jake Brancatella Look Like a Fool
description:
Mufti Saif Al-Asri is a prominent Islamic scholar renowned for his dedication to Islamic education, refined character, and profound knowledge of the Shari'ah sciences. He was born in the city of Hajja, Yemen, before relocating to Saudi Arabia with his family at a young age due to his father's work. In Saudi Arabia, he began his early education, entering the kingdom at the age of four or five. Shaykh Saif completed his elementary studies there and started reading religious books under scholars by 12, showcasing an early commitment to seeking knowledge.

Upon returning to Yemen, his family settled in the capital, Sana’a, where Shaykh Saif began his journey in structured Islamic learning. He pursued his intermediate (known as الإعدادية) and secondary education there, simultaneously embarking on formal Islamic studies under the mentorship of several Yemeni scholars. One of the most influential figures in his education was Shaykh Hasan Muhammad Maqbul Al-Ahdal, under whom Shaykh Saif studied the Arabic language, Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh), fundamentals of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh), and hadith sciences. During this period, he completed the memorization of the Qur’an, which he had begun in Saudi Arabia.

Shaykh Saif furthered his education by enrolling at Al-Iman University in Sana’a, a prestigious institution focusing on Islamic studies. He was among the university's first students when it opened its doors in the early 1990s (1415 AH). During his time there, he studied under leading Islamic scholars, including the distinguished jurist and legal theorist Shaykh Abdul Karim Zaidan, who authored notable works such as *Al-Mufassal Fi Ahkam Al-Mar’a* and *Al-Wajiz Fi Usul Al-Fiqh*. Shaykh Saif studied several of Shaykh Zaidan’s books in Islamic jurisprudence, legal principles, and da'wah (Islamic propagation).

In addition to Shaykh Zaidan, Shaykh Saif studied with other prominent scholars, such as the Yemeni mufti and judge Muhammad bin Isma’il Al-‘Amrani, the founder of Al-Iman University Shaykh Abdul Majid Al-Zindani, and Shaykh Dr. Abdul Wahhab Al-Daylami, a notable specialist in Qur’anic exegesis. This early foundational education enabled Shaykh Saif to comprehensively understand Shari'ah sciences.

After obtaining his bachelor’s and master’s degrees in 2001, Shaykh Saif began his professional career in Islamic jurisprudence by joining the Islamic advisory team at the Qatar Fatwa Center under IslamWeb, a well-known Islamic network. He served as a mufti from 2001 to 2007, dealing directly with the public's written and oral inquiries, gaining valuable experience in providing Islamic guidance and advisory services. His work involved answering questions via calls, SMS messages, and emails, which enhanced his proficiency in contemporary Islamic issues.

While in Qatar, Shaykh Saif continued his studies under scholars like the renowned scholar of Islamic theology and logic, Shaykh Mustafa Al-Binjawani, and the Iraqi scholar Shaykh As-Sadiq Al-Iraqi. Under their mentorship, he deepened his understanding of logic, rhetoric, and Islamic dialectics.

In 2007, Shaykh Saif moved to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to work in the official Fatwa Center. Over the course of nearly a decade (2007-2016), he expanded his expertise in issuing fatwas, supervising junior muftis, and reviewing religious rulings. His long tenure in Qatar and the UAE fortified his experience in Islamic jurisprudence and broadened his knowledge of contemporary Muslims' diverse issues.

Desiring to further his academic credentials, Shaykh Saif pursued a Ph.D. at Mohammed V University in Rabat, Morocco, under Dr. Farouq Hamada, a prominent Hadith scholar and academic figure. Dr. Hamada, originally from Homs, Syria, is well-regarded for his contributions to Islamic academia and his role in shaping the next generation of scholars.

Shaykh Saif’s scholarly endeavors extended beyond academia and fatwas. He has authored several writings on Islamic jurisprudence, creed, and other areas of Shari’ah, making a valuable contribution to Islamic literature. His commitment to Islamic education and scholarly advancement has led him to travel and teach in various regions, including recent visits to Chechnya. Shaykh Saif's connection with Chechnya began with his participation in educational and religious conferences and has since grown into a long-term commitment to supporting Islamic education there.

In Chechnya, Shaykh Saif has been actively involved in teaching students at Islamic universities and delivering classes on key Islamic texts, including Sharh al-Waraqat in the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh) and Sharh al-Aqeedah al-Tahawiyyah by Al-Imam Abdul-Ghani Al-Maydani. His classes attract students from the Islamic University in Grozny, and he holds study sessions after the noon prayer and on designated days each week. His approach emphasizes a balance between academic rigor and an emphasis on the ethical dimensions of Islamic teachings.

Palestine, Kashmir, and the Promise of Liberation | Ep.12 | Koshur Musalman | With Muneeza Rizvi
description:
In this podcast, we speak to Dr. Muneeza Rizvi about Palestine, Kashmir, and the promise that their struggles for liberation offers to the world. We talk about Rizvi's essay called Palestine and the Question of Islam, in which she interrogates the policing of Islam's visibility in the politics of Palestine. We also dive into the widespread but uncritical belief shared by many in the "impregnability" and "invincibility" of Israeli state. 

In addition to this, we speak about the popular constructions of the good Palestinian unarmed victim, who is seen as worthy of sympathy and protection and is contrasted with the killable and bad Palestinian rebel. Finally, we also discuss the limitations of human rights discourses and international law in what they offer to colonized populations in Palestine or Kashmir. This and more.

Recommended readings: 
1. The Human Right to Dominate, by Nicola Perugini and Neve Gordon (Book)
2. A History of False Hope: Investigative Commissions in Palestine, by Lori Allen (Book)
3. Decolonizing the Civilian in Third World National Liberation Wars, by 
Nicola Perugini (Essay)
4. The Forgotten Muslims: How Kashmiris Breathe Islam Under Occupation, by Ahmed Bin Qasim (Essay)

He participated in almost all the battles against the unbelievers during the time of the Prophet Muhammad (S), except for the Battle of Tabuk in the year 9th Hijri, as the Prophet (S) had placed Ali (R) in charge of the city. As well as being the standard-bearer in those battles, Ali (R) led parties of warriors on raids into enemy lands. At the Battle of Badr, he defeated the Umayyad champion Walid Ibn Utba as well as twenty other polytheist soldiers. Ali (R.A.) was prominent at the Battle of Uhud, In the Battle of the Trench, Ali (R) bravely defeated a prominent leader of the unbelievers called Amr Ibn Wudd. In the Battle of Khaybar, Ali (R) defeated the great commander Marhab. When the Muslim army failed to conquer the fortress twice, the Prophet (S), offered the command and the standard to Ali (R). The fortress fell to the onslaught of the Muslims and victory attained. Additionally, Ali (R) was one the Companions who stood unwavering beside the Prophet Muhammad (S) in the Battle of Hunain.

Ali (RA) was born inside the Holy Ka'bah in Mecca on the 13th of Rajab, 23 years before the migration to Medina. He belonged to the Quraysh tribe and the family of Bani Hashim. His father, Abu Talib, was the uncle of the Holy Prophet (S) and had played a significant role in raising and nurturing Muhammad (S). Ali's mother, Fatima bint Al-Asad, also belonged to the noble tribe of Bani Hashim and was highly respected by the Prophet (S) as if she were his own mother. It was Muhammad (S) who suggested the name Ali for him, adding further significance to his name. Being the first cousin of the Prophet (S), Ali (R) held a prestigious position and was fortunate to have been brought up under the kind and inspiring guidance of the Prophet (S) for most of his life.

Surrey Islamic Society is committed to the promotion of peace, love and respect in the community and on campus. We also aim to increase the understanding of pure Islam - free from any misconceptions and distortion. title: 25 230421 Eid Celebration
description:
On April 21, 2023 Afghans and Afghan Canadians celebrated Eid el Fitr, The Feast after the Fast in several locations. In one location the Afghan Association of Ontario – AAO Canada and Subhan Islamic Association (SIA) had reserved a big hall where over 3,000 people had gathered to observe the festivities and perform the Eid Prayers. 
Community Leaders talked about various issues of importance for the community, among them building a new community centre in eastern part of GTA and also about the Racism and Islamophobia. 

After Eid prayers inside the hall people shook hands and hugged each other congratulating each other that lasted for almost an hour inside the hall and then outside the hall.
The youth gathered outside the hall and celebrated the occasion with music and Atann – the Afghan National dance. Here are some scenes from the event.

title: Allah Will Not Look at Them
description:
As I walk through the snowy woods I discuss those categories of people that  Allah will neither talk to nor look at, nor purify, and they will have a painful punishment. May Allah protect us. Ameen.

Indeed, they who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book and exchange it for a small price – those consume not into their bellies except the Fire. And Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them. And they will have a painful punishment. [Qur’an 2:174]

Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) said, “There are three persons whom Allah will neither talk to nor look at, nor purify from (the sins), and they will have a painful punishment. (They are): (1) A man possessed superfluous water on a way [some versions say ‘in a desert’] and he withheld it from the travelers. (2) a man who gives a pledge of allegiance to a Muslim ruler and gives it only for worldly gains. If the ruler gives him what he wants, he remains obedient to his pledge, otherwise he does not abide by it, and (3) a man bargains with another man after the `Asr prayer and the latter takes a false oath in the Name of Allah claiming that he has been offered so much for the thing and the former (believes him and) buys it.” (Bukhari)

In one version of the hadith, it adds the words:

فَيَقُولُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، الْيَوْمَ أَمْنَعُكَ فَضْلِي، كَمَا مَنَعْتَ فَضْلَ مَا لَمْ تَعْمَلْ يَدَاكَ

Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘Today I withhold My Blessings from you as you withheld the superfluous part of that (water) which your hands did not create.’ (Bukhari)

Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) observed: “Three (are the persons) with whom Allah would neither speak, nor would He absolve them on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Mu’awiya added: He would not look at them and there is grievous torment for them: the aged adulterer, the liar king and the proud destitute.” (Muslim)

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “There are three at whom Allah will not look on the Day of Resurrection: The one who disobeys his parents, the woman who imitates men in her outward appearance, and the cuckold [husband of an adulterous wife]. And there are three who will not enter Paradise: The one who disobeys his parents, the drunkard, and the one who reminds people of what he has given them.” (Nasa’i)

Instagramadan 7x09: When Allah Deprives Us - Ustadh AbdelRahman Murphy
description:
What’s the wisdom in being deprived?

We see being held back from what we want as a bad thing. Why? Because we think we know what's best for us. So we become so disappointed when things don't go our way.

But then something amazing happens; we have a moment where we get clarity and see that the thing we wanted was actually harmful for us.

Subhan Allah! What a humbling moment - and this is exactly what Ibn Ata Illah is talking about in this wisdom, when you are given understanding being deprived is the same as being given.

title: Courageous Lion - Life of Alp Arsalan
description:
Alp Arslan is the son of Cagri, Khorasan governor, one of the founders of the Great Seljuk Empire. Alp Arslan means Heroic Lion in Turkish. Alp Arslan learned to use swords, riding horses, and shooting arrows from an early age.  Alp Arslan participated in the Dandanaqan war with his own soldiers and proved himself with his skills. Alp Arslan realized how difficult the Seljuk Empire was in his youth and worked day and night to keep the state going.

Alp Arslan first made Nizam Al-Mulk the grand vizier. Sultan Alp Arslan first went to Georgia, taking his son Malikshah and Nizam al-Mulk with him. Everyone appreciated that Alp Arslan was successful in the Eastern Anatolian conquests. Abbasi Caliph gave Alp Arslan the title of Father of Conquests.

title: East Bay Interfaith Community Gathering: Into the Light
channel: Muslim Speakers Service of the Bay Area
description:
Thanks to the Eden Area Interfaith Council, Interfaith Interconnect, and the Tri-City Interfaith Council for organizing the "Into the Light: East Bay Interfaith Community Gathering" in the MCC East Bay in Pleasanton. 

This was a heartfelt remembrance of all those we've lost to COVID-19, and a celebration of our community's rebirth and renewal in the pandemic's wake. The speakers are:

- Hina Khan-Mukhtar: Emcee welcome, MCC East Bay, Pleasanton
- Hafiz Ameen Mukhtar: Opening Muslim prayer, MCC East Bay, Pleasanton
- Wendy Jacobsen: Opening meditative prayer and lighting of a candle
Holy Cross Episcopal Church, Castro Valley
- Bishop Robert Lopez & Munir Safi: Personal impact of virus on their family and healing from the pain, Eden Area Interfaith Council & Mar Thoma Orthodox Church, Northridge & MCC East Bay, Pleasanton
- Jamie Ireland & Elsa Grabowski: Poem of memory for those lost to this virus & and poem “A Year Like No Other”, Tri-Valley Cultural Jews, Pleasanton
- Trish Munro: impact and response of City of Livermore, Livermore City Council
- Ruth Gasten: a joyful post-pandemic experience, Tri-Valley Interfaith Interconnect
- Congressman Eric Swalwell: reflections and gratitude to East Bay interfaith community efforts, California 15th Congressional District
- Arelis Sandoval, R.N, P.H.N.: Virus' impact on front-line healthcare personnel and ongoing response
Alameda County Public Health
- Joy Barnitz, how we practice interfaith during a pandemic, Tri-City Interfaith Council
- Leslie Mero: Memorial prayer and thanksgiving for days ahead, Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Hayward
- Cantor Linda Hirschhorn: A song of healing and coming out of brokenness, Temple Beth Sholom, San Leandro
- Mark Vaz: The Prayer of St. Francis, Our Lady of Grace Catholic Church, Castro Valley
- Rev. Dr. Arlene K. Nehring: Caring for our most vulnerable in community, Eden United Church of Christ, Hayward
- Roujheen Sabetan: A prayer for the departed, Baha'i Community, Pleasanton
- Soni Kaur, Gagan Singh & Manjeev Singh from Sikh Choir: Hymn and song musically expressed in Sikh faith, Gurdwara Sahib, Hayward

This recording was delivered via the Muslim Community Center - East Bay (MCC East Bay) in Pleasanton, California on June 27, 2021.

We gather to mourn the victims of the horrific yearlong pandemic on our community.

The Coronavirus caused millions of deaths and disrupted billions of lives globally.

Group worship was also disrupted, but the outbreak has bolstered the religious faith of many faithful and opened opportunities to pray and to serve our community with food, medical supplies, and more.

Disasters and crises have a way of making some question the existence of a greater force for good in the world and others to become more religious in the wake of tragedy.

As we look forward to better days, we reflect on the intersection of faith, a pandemic, a historic social movement.

description:
Join us today as we go behind the scenes where you meet the team of The Good Tree, hear our thoughts and insights on how we went about creating this podcast, and you will also hear our reflections on Season 1.

We also pay tribute to all our scholars who without their time and support this would not have been possible. 


Find out more: https://www.thegoodtree.faith​​
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/thegoodtree...​

About the podcast
The Good Tree podcast is a weekly discussion with renowned scholars deep diving into a range of ethical topics. We begin the first series on relationships.

Allah (swt) directs us to look at Prophet Muhammad (saw) as our moral guide in order to gain closeness to Him (swt).

Our name ‘The Good Tree’ comes from the Holy Qur’an, Chapter 14 Surah Ibrahim, verses 24 and 25:

Have you not considered how Allah presents an example, [making] a good word like a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed and its branches [high] in the sky? [14:24​​]

It produces its fruit all the time, by permission of its Lord. And Allah presents examples for the people that perhaps they will be reminder. [14:25​​]

We hope you will enjoy listening to these podcasts and find them beneficial on your journey towards Allah (swt).

title: Guided Meditation | Mindful Eating
description:
Eating is one of the most important parts of our day. In addition to providing us with energy, it can also be a great source of pleasure. This guided meditation is designed to bring attention to our eating so that we can get much more pleasure and joy from our food without being distracted by other things. So let's just eat. 

Some tips: 

1. Try to find a quiet place where you can sit undistracted (We know this can be hard to find if you have children. We get you)

2. Try to listen to the video while looking at your food. 

3. We don't need to finish our plate after we are full. (This is not Israf)
4. Feel free to come back to this video whenever you want to enjoy your food. 

5. Share this with your friends so they can enjoy their food too.

title: Answer Key 2
To Be a Woman in an Islamic Society | OIC Youth Connect EPISODE 5 | Dr Celene Ibrahim & Dr Afiya Zia
description:
Since time immemorial, women have left their mark on their societies, changing the course of history at times, and influencing significant spheres of life at others. In Muslim Civilization, extraordinary women worked alongside men to advance their communities. Their inspiring stories, charismatic personalities and determination has contributed to the world as we know it today. 

In this episode, we hope to highlight empowered women of the past and present, their forgotten legacies, the 21st century obstacles that they face, as well as the stereotypes associated with their identities as Muslim women, the feminist discourse in Muslim societies, and most importantly the way forward - how things can be improved for the empowered women to come tomorrow and the work cut out for them. 

The fifth episode of OIC Youth Connect is brought to you by National MOIC Pakistan in collaboration with ICYF-ERC.

Welcome to Seerah Pearls, which aims to highlight some tantalising learning points from each episode of the Seerah- Life of the Prophet (sallallahu alayhi wasallam).

So what is ‘Seerah’? The word linguistically means ‘a path’, ‘to walk in a particular direction’. More figuratively, it refers to someone’s life biography. Specifically, Seerah refers to the Prophetic biography. It includes everything from the occurrences in the life the Prophet Muhammad (sallallahu alayhi wasallam), from his daily practices, attributes, physical characteristics, mannerisms, expeditions, to family life.

Why study Seerah? It goes hand-in-hand with the study of the Quran. The Quran itself states that there is not a better example than the Prophet Muhammad (sallallahu alayhi wasallam) himself:

There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern for anyone whose hope is in Allah and the Last Day and [who] remembers Allah often. (Quran 33:21)

This series hopes to be different from dry, factual studies, or ‘superhero-tales’, which we may feel we cannot ever aspire to: it aims to humanise the Prophet Muhammad (sallallahu alayhi wasallam)  and provide eternal practical lessons for every-day life, as well as engender love for the best of humankind. How can you possibly love someone you do not know?

Question: 
Can you recommend a supplication for overcoming difficulty?

Answer: 
Ask Allah as He loves to be asked and always gives, realize your neediness before Him, and trust in Allah, realizing: “There is no movement or power except through Allah (La hawla wa la quwwata illa bi Allah).”

The following supplication may also be recited:

“O Allah! There is nothing easy except that which You make easy; and You make the difficult, if You wish, easy (Allahumma la sahla illa ma ja`altahu sahla wa anta taj`al ul-hazna idha shi’ta sahla).”

title: Jurong Legacy - 13 May 2018
description:
The early morning drizzle did not dampened the spirit of our friends attending today's event with a responsive turn out beyond expectations. We started off our hike from Chinese Garden MRT Station to Kiat Hong HongKah and several other remote sites till our end point at Bricklands. More photos and video to follow. Thank you for making our event a success.

Jurong appeared on the map as early as 1828 and probably derived from the Malay word 'Jerong', which means shark. It was also called PengKang in Chinese, and in the northern part Lokyang, ChongKeng & Bulim (Seng Boo Lim Rubber Estate). Today, we braved the rain to see the latter prior to experiencing similar fate as the Lentor Stream and many other green lung that will ultimately be consumed by a monster called 'urbanisation'.

channel: 5 Pillars of Marriage With Sr. Haleh Banani
description:
Marriage and Divorce in The United Arab Emirates - Al Jazeera Everywoman with Shahnaz Pakravan

Is giving up on marriage getting easier?

Divorce rates globally are on the increase, here in the middle east the figures have been rising steadily and seem set to continue that way. 

In the last year alone over 40% of couples in the United Arab Emirates chose not to stay together and in Saudi Arabia, an average of 33 divorce cases are recorded per day. In 2001 the first-ever divorce via SMS text messaging was registered.

What will it help with it help step the rise in the number so couples divorcing in the middle east?

We sent our reporter Julie Mcdonald to Dubai to find out what they are doing to address the problem.

Haleh Banani and her Husband Abdulmajeed Muriby are a picture of happiness and they are proud of their multicultural marriage and three children.

description:

Saya sebagai Trader forex sudah menemukan jawaban yang lengkap atas kegundahan saya akhir-akhir ini. Semoga video ini menjawab keraguan dan ketidaktahuan Umat Islam tentang haramnya forex. 

Sheikh Hacene Chebbani was born in Algeria and has been living in Canada since 1997. Sheikh Hacene has completed a Master's in Islamic finance (2012) from UK. While there he took the opportunity to study Aqīdah, Fiqh and Hadīth with some of the notable scholars of that blessed city.
 
In Canada Sheikh Hacene has worked in Islamic schools teaching the Arabic language and Islamic studies and has served as Sharīah consultant and head teacher for over 6 years.

description:
Muhammad Abdul Jabbar







On the authority of Abu Sa`id (radhiallahu `anhu) that the Prophet sallallahu `alayhi wa sallam said, "Whoever sees something evil should change it with his hand. If he cannot, then with his tongue; and if he cannot do even that, then in his heart. That is the weakest degree of faith." 

Please note - Humza Arshad was approached by the exCrew and other scholars, but he rejected them. The exCrew notified Humza that they were going to release a video. Every effort was made.

Here is the evidence from Islam (our source..remember?) for why we should speak out against such Munkar and condemn the action:

"There can be no backbiting of one who casts off the mantle of modesty." [Suyuti, Al-Jami` As-Saghir, 2/519, from Bayhaqi.]

Ibn Majjah narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed that the messenger (saw) said: "Let not one of you scorn himself". They said : O messenger of Allah, how one of us will scorn himself?. He (saw) said: "He sees a person whom Allah blamed, then he does not say about him what Allah has said about him. Allah (swt) will say to him: What prevented you from saying about this person so and so? He says: the fear from people. Allah says : Come, come to me, I am the one deserved to be feared"

Bukhari and Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr (ra) that the messenger (saw) said : "Any people in which there are sins done among them, they can change the evil and they do not change, Allah will cover them with a punishment from him".

Bukhari and Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu saeed (ra) that the messenger (saw) said: "Let not the fear of people prevent one of you to utter the truth when he sees it (i.e. sees the munkar) or hears it".

In this video, Muhammad Abdul Jabbar and the ex crew of Diary of badman highlight some of the issues regarding the Diary of badman videos. The project began with good intentions, but led to many misconceptions and bad examples. Every effort was made to advise Humza Arshad, but it failed as he chose to ignore.

As a result, the brothers had to speak out, and why we should refrain from watching Diary of a Badman

title: Unmarked Fruit - Shaykh Husain Abdul Sattar
description:
sacredlearning.org


Shaykh Husain Abdul Sattar

Shaykh Husain (may Allah preserve him) was born in Chicago (USA) in 1972. After completing his primary education at schools in his hometown near Chicago, he joined the University of Chicago where he studied Biology, Arabic and Islamic Civilization. It was during this period that he began his study of sacred knowledge, studying Arabic grammar (nahw), Hanafi Fiqh and Usul al-Fiqh under ulama (scholars) in Chicago. In 1994 Shaykh Husain also began training in Islamic spirituality under Shaykh Zulfiqar Ahmad, a leading shaykh in this field.

After obtaining his undergraduate degree, Shaykh Husain enrolled in the Pritzker School of Medicine at the University of Chicago. Along with his medical studies, he continued his studies of sacred knowledge. In his final year he took leave from medical school to focus on his religious studies, traveling to Syria and then Pakistan, where he studied a traditional curriculum for a number of years under some of their greatest scholars.

Throughout his years of study, Shaykh Husain continued his training under Shaykh Zulfiqar Ahmad (db). He was blessed with the close company of his Shaykh, learning the science of the purification of the heart. The deep taqwa and firm adherence to the sunnah and Shariah that characterized his teacher were eventually transferred to the student and Shaykh Husain was formally authorized in this science by Shaykh Zulfiqar (db) in July 2001.

Shaykh Husain has completed medical school and is currently an Assistant Professor of Pathology at University of Chicago's Prizker School of Medicine and also practices Surgical Pathology at the University of Chicago Medical Center. During his free time, he teaches and lectures across the United States on various subjects of Islamic knowledge, including purification of the soul.

Shaykh Husain is presently engaged in editing and publishing the translations of his teacher's books into English. In addition, he is completing his own written works including the popular series, "Fundamentals of Classical Arabic" and a manual on Hanafi fiqh entitled, "The Stairs to Bliss." [forthcoming]

AlKauthar Bradford Presents:

Prayer Makes Perfect
23rd - 24th February 2013
Weekend Experience
With Shaykh Bilal Ismail
Register Today: http://www.alkauthar.org/course.php?course=373

What do you think of an act of worship -- the most ordered in the Qurʾan, the first on which we'll be judged, the true sign of one's belief, the one that brings you the closest to Allah and the one that brings you to the true station of servitude (prostration)? A simple 5 minute act of worship that is more beloved to Allah than this world and all that is in it!

Little wonder is it not, that the Prophet's last advice before he passed away was: 'The Prayer, the Prayer!'

Yet with such importance, how few are those who learn about it and practice it correctly? On top of that, how much differences exists in the ummah in the manner of prayer? And finally, how pitiful that people don't take the full reward of the prayer -- just as the Prophet (ṣalla'llāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam) said in the authentic ḥadīth: A person prays and yet for him only a tenth or a quarter or a half of its reward is written.

Are you sure your prayers are correct?

Are you sure they are done in the manner that deems them acceptable?

title: Mohamed by Non-Muslim Scholars
description:
Non-Muslim scholars, over the last several hundred years speak out about Muhammad, peace be upon him. After reviewing authentic reports, these same scholars offer excellent and unbiased presentations confirming the greatness of Muhammad, peace be upon him, his attractive manners, humble attitude and as well as excellent integrity and moral character. 

France has some very open anti-Muhammad activity going on these days. About this anyone can pick up a newspaper, look at TV or radio news and see quickly the very clear and biased prejudices being carried out against the way of Islam, the people who follow it and the founder himself, Muhammad, peace be upon him,

But now consider, if you will, without prejudice, without bias, without hatred and with a clear heart - what the following 15 famous scholars over the last few centuries have said in praise and endorsement of this very man - Muhammad, peace be upon him:

Doctor William Draper, Philip K. Hitti, Thomas Carlyle, Mahatma Gandhi, Edward Gibbon and Simon Oakly, Reverend Bosworth Smith, Gibbon (Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire), De Lacy O'Leary, Sir George Bernard Shaw (1936),  Michael Hart (1978),  W. Montgomery Watt (1953),  Washington Irving, James Michener (1955), Lawrence E. Browne (1944), Alphonse de LaMartaine (1854)

Read this quote, "Philosopher, Orator, Apostle, Legislator, Conqueror of Ideas, Restorer of Rational beliefs, founder of 20 terrestrial empires and one spiritual empire . . that was Muhammad (peace be upon him)
We may well ask, "Was there ever any man greater than he?" - Alphonse de LaMaratine (1854)

Compare now, today what we see and hear on the Internet, TV, radio, newspapers and even from the pulpits of some churches around the world about this very same man. None of these bring the story in its fullness, nor with integrity, nor with good intention to build and contribute to the success of our futures.

Now, after consideration of what has been presented here and on our site ProphetOfIslam.com, we must ask ourselves ~ What do we say about Muhammad?

title: Famous Women in Islam, Dr. Umar Faruq Abd-Allah, Part 1.2 of 14
description: "Islamic history has one of the most remarkable legacies of famous women in human history. This set is primarily biographical and focuses on a select number of prominent women in Islamic history from the Age of the Prophet until modern times in a wide variety of areas from scholarship, mysticism, and poetry to social patronage, war, and politics. It shows that the status of women in Islamic societies has never been uniform or monolithic but has shifted from place to place, from age to age, and from class to social class. The greatest disparity, however, has been between the norms of the Prophetic period and those of subsequent ages. Prophetic society lacked the rigid divisions of social space that became characteristic of many traditional Islam societies, and, as a rule, Prophetic society was more open and less patriarchal, giving women greater freedom and allowing the a conspicuous role within the matrix of social and civic life. A second major shift in women's status occurred during the colonial, post-colonial, and modern periods, when the position of Muslim women often deteriorated markedly. Although the class focuses on the legacies or particular women, it will look at their lives as an index of a number of concrete theological and legal issues pertaining to gender and sexuality in Islam Law and Muslim culture. This set is not intended for women alone or just for Muslims."

title: The Poem that made Imam Ahmad Cry
description:
The Poem that made the Imām of Ahlus-Sunnah, Ahmad bin Hanbal (rahimahullaah) Cry, so much so that one of his students said that he almost perished due to him crying so much.

إذا ما قال لي ربي .. أما استحييت تعصيني
وتخفي الذنب عن خلقي .. وبالعصيان تأتيني
If my Lord asks me
"Have you no shame in disobeying me?
You hide your faults from my creation
yet full of sin you come to Me"

فكيف أجيب يا ويحي .. ومن ذا سوف يحميني
So what will I answer? O' Woe to me,
and who shall protect me do you see?

أسلي النفس بالآمال .. من حين إلى حين
I keep forestalling my soul
with thoughts of hope from time to time

وأنسى ما وراء الموت .. ماذا بعد تكفيني
And forgetting what is to come after death,
and after I am warped in the sheets of the dead

كاني قد ضمنت العيش .. ليس الموت يأتيني
As if I have guaranteed living forever,
and that death will not overcome me

وجاءت سكرة الموت الشديدة من سيحميني
Then the harsh drunkenness of death overtakes me,
who now will be able to protect me?

نظرت إلى الوجوه أليس منهم من سيفديني
I looked at the faces, is there not from amongst them
who will ransom me?

سأسأل ما الذي قدمت في دنياي ينجيني
I will be asked
what have I put forth in my life to save myself

فكيف إجابتي من بعد ما فرطت في ديني
So what will I answer,
after I've been neglectful regarding my Deen

ويا ويحي ألم أسمع كلام الله يدعوني
O' woe to me, did I not hear the
Speech of Allah calling out to me??

ألم أسمع لما قد جاء في ق و يس
Did I not hear what has come in Qaaf'n, wa Yaseen'i

ألم أسمع بيوم الحشر يوم الجمع والدين
Did i not hear of the day the crowds will be summoned,
the day we will be collected, and the day of al-Deen'i

ألم أسمع منادي الموت يدعوني يناديني
Did I not hear the caller of death
calling me; seeking me

فيا رباه عبد تائب من ذا سيؤويه
O my lord a slave to you I come repenting,
who than shall grant me shelter?

سوى رب غفور واسع للحق يهديني
Other than an oft-forgiving Lord,
to the truth he will guide me

أتيت إليك فارحمني وثقل في موازيني
I have come to you, so have mercy on me,
and make heavy my weights

وخفف في جزائي أنت أرجى من يجازيني
And lighten my reckoning you are the best
of who will bring me to reckoning

title: Book trailer for Far from Home, a novel about Zimbabwe - Tariro
description:
Katie and Tariro are two girls linked by a terrible secret, grappling with the complexities of adolescence, family and a painful colonial legacy as their lives play out against the tragic history of the land in Zimbabwe.

14-year-old Tariro is a daughter of the soil: she loves the land, the baobab tree she was born beneath, her loving family - and brave, handsome Nhamo. She couldn't be happier. But then the white settlers arrive, and everything changes - suddenly, violently, and tragically, robbing Tariro of all that she loves.

Forty years later, 14-year-old Katie adores her doting father, her exclusive boarding school, and her farm with its baobab tree in rural Zimbabwe. Life is great. Until the land acquisition programme forces the family off the land and to cold, rainy London.
Atmospheric, gripping and epic in scope, Far from Home brings the turbulent history of Zimbabwe to vivid, tangible life, challenging the reader to see it with new eyes.

title: 'THE TRIBE WORD MUST STOP' SH ABU TAUBAH.flv
description:
Abu Taubah was born and raised in New York, he comes from an educated family where his mother was an English teacher turned Principal and his father a politician. Public lecture delivered by Shaykh Yasir Qadhi titled 'Dua - The Weapon of the Believers' at the International Islamic Peace Conference 2009 held at Somaiya Ground Mumbai, India 2009, as shown on Peace TV.

International Islamic Peace Conference 2009 - Understanding Islam & Global Unity is a 10 Day International Islamic Conference & Exhibition that was held on 30th October to 8th November. The location a vast ground, Somaiya Ground (Spread over 30 acres) Sion (E), Mumbai, India. Admission is free: People of all religion were welcome.

Dua supplication) is the most powerful weapon of the believer and a means of communicating with his Lord - Shaykh Yasir Qadhi elaborates on the status, importance and etiquette of dua' in Islam. For more information and details please refer to the book published by the speaker of the same title which is the most comprehensive work yet to be written in English on the topic, the author discusses, amongst other matters: the excellence and benefits of du'a; the types of du'a; the pre-conditions that are needed in order for a du'a to be accepted; the recommended etiquette of performing du'a; the timings and situations in which a du'a is more likely to be answered; the various factors that aid or prevent a du'a from being accepted; the relationship of du'a with the Divine Decree (qadr); the wisdom behind a delayed response, and many other relevant topics.

Yasir Qadhi was born in Houston, Texas and completed his primary and secondary education in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. He graduated with a B.Sc. in Chemical Engineering from the University of Houston, after which he was accepted as a student at the Islamic University of Madinah. After completing a diploma in Arabic, he graduated with a B.A. from the College of Hadith and Islamic Sciences. Thereafter, he completed a M.A. in Islamic Theology from the College of Dawah.

His published works include Riya'a: The Hidden Shirk, Du'aa: The Weapon of the Believer, and An Introduction to the Sciences of the Qur'an.

title: LA ILAHA ILA ALLAH    CHAHADA
A Special Message from Imam Siraj Wahhaj
description:
Siraj Wahhaj is an African-American Muslim convert to Islam and public figure for Muslims in North America. He is currently the Imam of Al-Taqwa mosque in Brooklyn, New York and the Amir (Leader) of The Muslim Alliance in North America (MANA).

Born and raised in New York, he became a Sunday school teacher as at a young age, then later went to Wilfrid Laurier University (WLU) where he studied biology education.

In 1969 he joined the Nation of Islam and was taught under Louis Farrakhan at the height of the NOI's anti-Malcolm X rhetoric. He became a Sunni Muslim after the death of Elijah Muhammad in 1975 and Muhammad's son Warith Deen Mohammed took over and reorganized the organization, urging members to come to orthodox Islam. Kearse then changed his name to Siraj Wahhaj. He was chosen to study Islam at the Umm al-Qura university of Mecca in 1978. He also briefly taught a course in Islamic studies at Howard University. In 1981 he started his own mosque, Masijd ul-Taqwa, in a friend's apartment in Brooklyn. Although it originally started out with only 25 people, today it is well-known.

In 1988 he led his community in an anti-drug patrol in which they staked out drug houses in Bedford-Stuyvesant in the cold of winter for 40 days and nights, forcing the closure of 15 drug houses. This effort received high praise from the New York City Police Department and the media.

Since that time, Siraj has been active in many Islamic organizations. He has been vice president of the Islamic Society of North America since 1997 and has served on the Majlis al Shura, a consultative council of Islamic scholars, since 1987. He is a member of the Board of Advisors for the American Muslim Council and has also served on the national board of the Council on American-Islamic Relations.

Siraj is a prolific speaker in America. He makes many appearances at major North American Muslim conventions, and numerous forums and lectures in New England. His audio and video lectures are also popular in America's Muslim community. He is known to encourage Muslims to be God-fearing, enjoin good and forbid evil, practice regular charity, stay away from drugs, abstain from pre-marital relations, and other issues as well. He has also appeared on several national television talk shows and has had interviews with several media outlets.

In 1991 Siraj offered an invocation (opening prayer) to the United States House of Representatives. He was the first Muslim to do so.

title: When does a person become Hizbee.
description:
When does a person become Hizbi.

Shaykh Zayd al-Madkhalee: - 

He is considered the second man in the district of Jaazaan with regard to knowledge, fatwaa, and calling to Allaah (Da'wah) after Shaikh Ahmad bin Yahyaa An-Najmee. May Allaah lengthen both of them in lifespan. 

Shaikh Ahmad An-Najmee was asked: "O Shaikh! What do you say about one who says: 'I don't recognize Shaikh Zayd Al-Madkhalee or Shaikh Rabee' Al-Madkhalee. I don't recognize them to be from the scholars and I won't take any knowledge from them. I don't acknowledge anyone except Shaikh 'Abdul-'Azeez bin Baaz.' So how would you respond to this?" 

The Shaikh answered: "We ask Allaah to guide this person and to grant him direction, for indeed, Shaikh Rabee' Al-Madkhalee and Shaikh Zayd Al-Madkhalee -- both of them are from the sincere Salafee scholars. He must acknowledge and be aware of this. And he must not disparage them, because disparaging them means disparaging the Sunnah of Allaah's Messenger, which they are carrying. We are not saying that they are free from error. However, their methodology is Salafee. So the students of knowledge must read their books and get to know the truth that is in them..."
